When finished it watered more than forty thousand qing of salty land from the Jing, yielding a zhong per mu; Guanzhong became fertile with no more famine years, Qin grew richer and stronger and in the end swallowed the lords. The canal was named after Zheng Guo.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷二十九 河渠書
passages.textZh: 渠就，用注填閼之水，溉澤鹵之地四萬餘頃，收皆畝一鐘。於是關中為沃野，無凶年，秦以富彊，卒并諸侯，因命曰鄭國渠。

summary.zh: 秦王政十七年，內史騰攻韓，俘韓王安，盡取其地，設潁川郡。韓是六國中第一個被秦滅亡的。
summary.en: In the seventeenth year of King Zheng, the Clerk of the Capital Teng attacked Han, captured King An, took all his land and made it Yingchuan commandery. Han was the first of the six states to fall.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 內史騰攻韓，得韓王安，盡納其地，以其地為郡，命曰潁川。

summary.zh: 秦將王賁攻魏，引黃河與鴻溝之水灌大梁，三個月後城牆崩壞，魏王假出降，魏亡。
summary.en: The Qin general Wang Ben attacked Wei and turned the Yellow River and the Hong canal onto Daliang; after three months the walls collapsed, King Jia surrendered and Wei ended.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 王賁攻魏，引河溝灌大梁，大梁城壞，其王請降，盡取其地。

summary.zh: 李信率二十萬秦軍伐楚失敗後，秦王政親自請回老將王翦，以六十萬大軍伐楚，攻取陳以南至平輿之地，俘楚王負芻；次年項燕立昌平君為楚王，兵敗而死，楚亡。
summary.en: After Li Xin's two hundred thousand men failed against Chu, King Zheng went himself to bring back the old general Wang Jian, who invaded with six hundred thousand, took the land from Chen south to Pingyu and captured King Fuchu. The next year Xiang Yan set up the Lord of Changping as king; he was defeated and killed, and Chu was gone.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 秦王復召王翦，彊起之，使將擊荊。取陳以南至平輿，虜荊王。秦王游至郢陳。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 二十三年，秦王復召王翦，彊起之，使將擊荊。取陳以南至平輿，虜荊王。
passages.textEn: In the twenty-third year the King of Qin called Wang Jian back, pressed him to serve, and sent him against Jing (Chu). He took the land from Chen south to Pingyu and captured the king of Jing.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 二十四年，王翦、蒙武攻荊，破荊軍，昌平君死，項燕遂自殺。
passages.textEn: In the twenty-fourth year Wang Jian and Meng Wu attacked Jing and broke its army; the Lord of Changping died and Xiang Yan killed himself.

label.zh: 王翦取陳以南至平輿，虜荊王
label.en: Wang Jian from Chen south to Pingyu

summary.zh: 郿人，秦國名將，封武安君。前293年伊闕之戰斬首二十四萬，前278年攻破楚都郢，前260年長平之戰坑殺趙降卒四十萬。後與丞相范雎不和，拒絕再攻邯鄲，被賜死。
summary.en: Of Mei, the great general of Qin, Lord of Wu'an. He beheaded two hundred and forty thousand at Yique in 293 BCE, took the Chu capital Ying in 278 and at Changping in 260 buried alive four hundred thousand surrendered Zhao soldiers. Falling out with the chancellor Fan Ju and refusing to attack Handan again, he was ordered to kill himself.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十三 白起王翦列傳
passages.textZh: 白起者，郿人也。善用兵，事秦昭王。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十三 白起王翦列傳
passages.textZh: 曰：「我何罪于天而至此哉？」良久，曰：「我固當死。長平之戰，趙卒降者數十萬人，我詐而盡阬之，是足以死。」

summary.zh: 中山國靈壽人，入燕為燕昭王所重用，聯合五國伐齊，攻下齊國七十餘城。昭王死後遭疑，出奔趙國。
summary.en: Of Lingshou in Zhongshan; trusted by King Zhao of Yan, he led five states against Qi and took more than seventy of its cities. Distrusted after the king's death, he fled to Zhao.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十 樂毅列傳
passages.textZh: 樂毅者，其先祖曰樂羊。樂羊為魏文侯將，伐取中山，魏文侯封樂羊以靈壽。

summary.zh: 趙國上卿。奉和氏璧入秦而完璧歸趙；澠池之會又折服秦王。名將廉頗不服，屢欲羞辱他，他以國家為重處處退讓，廉頗知道後「肉袒負荊」登門請罪，二人結為刎頸之交。
summary.en: Senior minister of Zhao. He took the He jade disc to Qin and brought it back whole, and at the meeting at Mianchi he faced down the King of Qin. The general Lian Po resented him and wanted to humiliate him; Lin, putting the state first, kept out of his way, until Lian Po, learning why, came to his door "bare-backed and carrying thorns" to apologise, and they became friends to the death.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十一 廉頗藺相如列傳
passages.textZh: 廉頗聞之，肉袒負荊，因賓客至藺相如門謝罪。曰：「鄙賤之人，不知將軍寬之至此也。」

summary.zh: 名無忌，魏昭王少子，戰國四公子之一，仁而下士，門客三千。前257年竊符救趙，大破秦軍；前247年率五國之兵擊退秦將蒙驁。後受魏王猜忌，飲酒而死。
summary.en: Prince Wuji, youngest son of King Zhao of Wei, one of the four great princes of the Warring States, generous to men of talent, with three thousand retainers. In 257 BCE he stole the army tally to save Zhao and beat the Qin army; in 247 he led five states to drive back the Qin general Meng Ao. Distrusted by the king, he drank himself to death.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十七 魏公子列傳
passages.textZh: 魏公子無忌者，魏昭王子少子而魏安釐王異母弟也。

summary.zh: 名軻，騶人，受業於子思的門人。遊說齊宣王、梁惠王，主張仁政，不被採用，退而與弟子萬章等著書七篇。
summary.en: Meng Ke, of Zou, a student of Zisi's disciples. He urged humane government on King Xuan of Qi and King Hui of Liang without success, and withdrew to write seven books with his disciples Wan Zhang and others.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十四 孟子荀卿列傳
passages.textZh: 受業子思之門人。道既通，游事齊宣王，宣王不能用。

summary.zh: 陽翟大商人。在邯鄲遇到作質子的秦公子子楚，認為「此奇貨可居」，助其歸國繼位（秦莊襄王），自任丞相；秦王政即位後尊為相國、仲父，主持編撰《呂氏春秋》。後因嫪毐事被免，飲鴆而死。
summary.en: A great merchant of Yangdi. Meeting the Qin prince Zichu, a hostage at Handan, he judged him "a rare commodity worth holding", helped him home to the throne (King Zhuangxiang) and became chancellor; under King Zheng he was Chancellor of State and "Second Father", and sponsored the Lüshi chunqiu. Disgraced over the Lao Ai affair, he took poison.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十五 呂不韋列傳
passages.textZh: 呂不韋者，陽翟大賈人也。往來販賤賣貴，家累千金。

summary.zh: 楚國上蔡人，師從荀子，入秦為客卿。秦王下令驅逐客卿時上〈諫逐客書〉：「太山不讓土壤，故能成其大；河海不擇細流，故能就其深」，秦王收回逐客令。後任丞相，主張郡縣制、焚書、統一文字。始皇死後與趙高偽造詔書立胡亥，後為趙高所害，腰斬於咸陽。
summary.en: Of Shangcai in Chu, a student of Xunzi, who went to Qin as a guest adviser. When the king ordered all foreign advisers expelled, he wrote his famous memorial — "Mount Tai refuses no soil, and so is great; the rivers and seas reject no stream, and so are deep" — and the order was withdrawn. As chancellor he argued for commanderies, the burning of the books and a single script. After the First Emperor's death he joined Zhao Gao in forging the will that put Huhai on the throne, and was later destroyed by Zhao Gao and cut in two at Xianyang.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 李斯列傳
passages.textZh: 李斯者，楚上蔡人也。年少時，為郡小吏；見吏舍廁中鼠食不絜，近人犬，數驚恐之。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 李斯列傳
passages.textZh: 是以太山不讓土壤，故能成其大；河海不擇細流，故能就其深；王者不卻眾庶，故能明其德。

summary.zh: 韓國公子，與李斯同師荀子，喜刑名法術之學，著〈孤憤〉〈五蠹〉等。秦王讀其書而嘆息，後韓非使秦，被李斯、姚賈陷害，死於獄中。
summary.en: A prince of Han who studied with Li Si under Xunzi and devoted himself to law and statecraft, writing "Solitary Indignation", "The Five Vermin" and more. The King of Qin sighed with admiration on reading them; when Han Fei came to Qin as envoy, Li Si and Yao Jia had him jailed, and he died in prison.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六十三 老子韓非列傳
passages.textZh: 韓非者，韓之諸公子也。喜刑名法術之學，而其歸本於黃老。

summary.zh: 秦始皇徵發逃亡者、贅婿、商人等攻取陸梁地（嶺南），設桂林、象郡、南海三郡，並遷徙罪人戍守。靈渠的開鑿溝通了湘江與漓江，保障了南征的運輸。
summary.en: The First Emperor sent fugitives, bonded sons-in-law and merchants to conquer the Luliang lands (the far south), creating the commanderies of Guilin, Xiang and Nanhai and settling convicts there as garrisons. The Ling canal, joining the Xiang and the Li rivers, carried the supplies.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 發諸嘗逋亡人、贅婿、賈人略取陸梁地，為桂林、象郡、南海，以適遣戍。西北斥逐匈奴。

confidenceNote.zh: 考古發掘顯示阿房宮前殿只完成了夯土台基，杜牧〈阿房宮賦〉所寫的宮殿與「楚人一炬」多屬文學想像。
confidenceNote.en: Excavation shows only the rammed-earth platform of the front hall was finished; the palace of Du Mu's famous rhapsody, and its burning by Xiang Yu, are largely literary imagination.

summary.zh: 秦始皇在渭南上林苑營建朝宮，先建前殿阿房，東西五百步、南北五十丈，上可坐萬人；又修驪山陵墓，徵發刑徒七十餘萬人。
summary.en: The First Emperor began a new court palace in the Shanglin park south of the Wei, starting with the front hall at Epang — five hundred paces east to west, fifty zhang north to south, seating ten thousand; with the tomb at Mount Li, the works took over seven hundred thousand convicts.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 先作前殿阿房，東西五百步，南北五十丈，上可以坐萬人，下可以建五丈旗。周馳為閣道，自殿下直抵南山。

summary.zh: 丞相趙高想篡權，擔心群臣不服，便牽一頭鹿獻給秦二世，說是馬。二世笑說丞相錯了，問左右，有人沉默，有人附和說是馬，說是鹿的人後來都被趙高陷害。不久趙高逼殺二世，立子嬰。
summary.en: The chancellor Zhao Gao, plotting to seize power and unsure the ministers would follow, presented a deer to the Second Emperor and called it a horse. The emperor laughed that he was mistaken and asked those around him; some kept silent, some agreed it was a horse, and those who said "deer" Zhao Gao later destroyed. Soon after he forced the Second Emperor to kill himself and set up Ziying.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 趙高欲為亂，恐群臣不聽，乃先設驗，持鹿獻於二世，曰：「馬也。」二世笑曰：「丞相誤邪？謂鹿為馬。」問左右，左右或默，或言馬以阿順趙高。或言鹿（者），高因陰中諸言鹿者以法。後群臣皆畏高。

summary.zh: 劉邦先入關中，項羽大怒，欲攻劉邦。劉邦次日帶百餘騎到鴻門向項羽謝罪。宴會上范增多次以玉玦示意項羽殺劉邦，項羽默然不應；項莊舞劍意在沛公，樊噲闖帳護主，劉邦藉口如廁脫身。
summary.en: Liu Bang had entered Guanzhong first, and Xiang Yu in fury meant to attack him. The next day Liu Bang came to Hongmen with a hundred horsemen to apologise. At the feast Fan Zeng raised his jade ring to Xiang Yu again and again as a signal to kill Liu Bang; Xiang Yu sat silent. Xiang Zhuang danced with a sword, meaning to strike; Fan Kuai burst in to protect his lord, and Liu Bang slipped away on the pretext of going to the latrine.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 沛公旦日從百餘騎來見項王，至鴻門，謝曰：「臣與將軍戮力而攻秦，將軍戰河北，臣戰河南，然不自意能先入關破秦，得復見將軍於此。今者有小人之言，令將軍與臣有郤。」

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 范增數目項王，舉所佩玉珪以示之者三，項王默然不應。

summary.zh: 鴻門宴後數日，項羽引兵入咸陽，屠城，殺已投降的秦王子嬰，焚燒秦宮室，大火三月不滅，掠奪財寶婦女而東歸。隨後分封十八路諸侯，自立為西楚霸王。
summary.en: A few days after Hongmen, Xiang Yu led his army into Xianyang, massacred its people, killed Ziying, the surrendered King of Qin, and burned the Qin palaces — the fire burned for three months — and went east with the treasure and the women. He then divided the realm among eighteen kings and made himself Hegemon-King of Western Chu.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項羽引兵西屠咸陽，殺秦降王子嬰，燒秦宮室，火三月不滅；收其貨寶婦女而東。

summary.zh: 項羽北擊齊國時，漢王劉邦率五路諸侯五十六萬大軍東進，攻入楚都彭城。項羽親率三萬精兵回師，清晨從蕭縣出擊，中午大破漢軍，漢軍死傷十餘萬，劉邦僅率數十騎逃脫，父母妻子被俘。
summary.en: While Xiang Yu was fighting in Qi, Liu Bang led five allied armies, five hundred and sixty thousand men, east and took the Chu capital Pengcheng. Xiang Yu came back with thirty thousand picked men, struck from Xiao at dawn and by noon had routed the Han army, killing over a hundred thousand; Liu Bang escaped with a few dozen horsemen, his father and wife captured.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項王乃西從蕭，晨擊漢軍而東，至彭城，日中，大破漢軍。漢軍皆走，相隨入穀、泗水，殺漢卒十餘萬人。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 於是田榮弟田橫收齊亡卒得數萬人，反城陽。項王因留，連戰未能下。
passages.textEn: Then Tian Rong's younger brother Tian Heng gathered tens of thousands of Qi's scattered soldiers and rose at Chengyang; King Xiang stayed to fight, but could not take it.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 春，漢王部五諸侯兵，凡五十六萬人，東伐楚。項王聞之，即令諸將擊齊，而自以精兵三萬人南從魯出胡陵。四月，漢皆已入彭城，收其貨寶美人，日置酒高會。項王乃西從蕭，晨擊漢軍而東，至彭城，日中，大破漢軍。
passages.textEn: In spring the King of Han led the troops of five lords, five hundred and sixty thousand men, east against Chu. Hearing of it, King Xiang left his generals to fight Qi and himself came south with thirty thousand picked men by Lu and Huling. In the fourth month the Han army had entered Pengcheng, seized its treasure and women, and feasted daily. King Xiang came round west by Xiao, struck the Han army at dawn moving east, reached Pengcheng and by noon had routed it.

label.zh: 自以精兵三萬人南從魯
label.en: Xiang Yu south from Qi by Lu

names.name: The battle with backs to the river (Jingxing)

summary.zh: 韓信率數萬漢軍東出井陘擊趙。他先派萬人背靠綿蔓水列陣，趙軍見了大笑；又派二千輕騎繞到趙營後方。趙軍傾巢出擊不能取勝，回營時見營壘已插滿漢軍赤旗，大亂潰敗，趙王歇被俘。
summary.en: Han Xin led a few tens of thousands of Han troops east through the Jingxing pass against Zhao. He first set ten thousand men in battle order with their backs to the river — the Zhao army laughed to see it — and sent two thousand light horsemen round behind the Zhao camp. When the whole Zhao army came out and could not win, it turned back to find its camp covered in Han red banners, broke and fled; King Xie of Zhao was captured.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十二 淮陰侯列傳
passages.textZh: 信乃使萬人先行，出，背水陳。趙軍望見而大笑。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十二 淮陰侯列傳
passages.textZh: 信與張耳以兵數萬，欲東下井陘擊趙。趙王、成安君陳餘聞漢且襲之也，聚兵井陘口，號稱二十萬。
passages.textEn: Han Xin and Zhang Er, with several tens of thousands of men, meant to go east down Jingxing to attack Zhao. The king of Zhao and Chen Yu, Lord of Cheng'an, hearing Han was coming, gathered their troops at the mouth of Jingxing, two hundred thousand by report.

label.zh: 信與張耳欲東下井陘擊趙
label.en: Han Xin down the Jingxing pass

summary.zh: 楚漢在滎陽一帶相持多年，項羽兵疲糧盡，與劉邦約定「中分天下」，以鴻溝為界，西屬漢、東屬楚，並放還劉邦的父母妻子。項羽東歸後，劉邦採納張良、陳平的建議背約追擊，終有垓下之戰。
summary.en: After years of stalemate around Xingyang, Xiang Yu, his men weary and short of food, agreed with Liu Bang to "divide the realm down the middle" along the Hong canal — west to Han, east to Chu — and released Liu Bang's father and wife. As Xiang Yu went east, Liu Bang, on Zhang Liang and Chen Ping's advice, broke the truce and pursued him, leading to Gaixia.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項王乃與漢約，中分天下，割鴻溝以西者為漢，鴻溝而東者為楚。

summary.zh: 淮陰人。少時貧困，曾受胯下之辱。投奔劉邦後經蕭何力薦拜為大將，暗渡陳倉平定三秦，背水一戰破趙，又平定燕、齊，垓下率軍圍困項羽。劉邦稱帝後改封楚王，後降為淮陰侯，前196年被呂后與蕭何設計殺害於長樂宮。
summary.en: Of Huaiyin. Poor as a young man, he once crawled between a bully's legs rather than fight. He joined Liu Bang and, on Xiao He's urging, was made commander-in-chief; he took the three Qin kingdoms, beat Zhao with his back to the river, conquered Yan and Qi, and surrounded Xiang Yu at Gaixia. Made King of Chu, then reduced to Marquis of Huaiyin, he was lured into the Changle palace by Empress Lü and Xiao He and killed in 196 BCE.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十二 淮陰侯列傳
passages.textZh: 淮陰侯韓信者，淮陰人也。始爲布衣時，貧無行，不得推擇爲吏，又不能治生商賈，常從人寄食飲，人多厭之者，常數從其下鄉南昌亭長寄食，數月，亭長妻患之，乃晨炊蓐食。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八 高祖本紀
passages.textZh: 夫運籌策帷帳之中，決勝於千里之外，吾不如子房。鎮國家，撫百姓，給餽馕，不絕糧道，吾不如蕭何。連百萬之軍，戰必勝，攻必取，吾不如韓信。此三者，皆人傑也，吾能用之，此吾所以取天下也。項羽有一范增而不能用，此其所以為我擒也。

summary.zh: 字子房，先世為韓國相。秦滅韓後曾在博浪沙狙擊秦始皇未中。輔佐劉邦，劉邦稱讚：「夫運籌策帷帳之中，決勝於千里之外，吾不如子房。」封留侯，晚年學道引辟穀。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zifang, from a family of chancellors of Han. After Qin destroyed Han he tried to assassinate the First Emperor at Bolangsha and missed. He served Liu Bang, who said: "Planning in the tent and deciding victory a thousand li away — in that I cannot match Zifang." Made Marquis of Liu, he spent his last years on Taoist exercises.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷五十五 留侯世家
passages.textZh: 留侯張良者，其先韓人也。大父開地，相韓昭侯、宣惠王、襄哀王。

summary.zh: 沛縣人，劉邦的同鄉與丞相。劉邦入咸陽時，他獨先收取秦丞相府的律令圖書，因而掌握天下形勢；楚漢相爭時坐鎮關中，保障糧餉兵源。漢朝建立後制定律令，功列第一。
summary.en: Of Pei, Liu Bang's fellow townsman and chancellor. When Liu Bang entered Xianyang he alone first secured the laws, maps and registers of the Qin chancellery, and so knew the state of the realm; through the war with Chu he held Guanzhong, keeping the grain and recruits flowing. He drew up the Han laws and was ranked first in merit.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷五十三 蕭相國世家
passages.textZh: 蕭相國何者，沛豐人也。以文無害為沛主吏掾。

summary.zh: 居鄛人，年七十投奔項梁，勸立楚懷王之後以收民心，後為項羽謀士，被尊為「亞父」。鴻門宴上屢勸項羽殺劉邦不成；後項羽中陳平反間計疏遠他，范增憤而辭歸，途中背疽發作而死。
summary.en: Of Juchao, who joined Xiang Liang at seventy and urged him to set up a descendant of King Huai of Chu to win the people; as Xiang Yu's adviser he was honoured as "Second Father". At Hongmen he urged Xiang Yu again and again to kill Liu Bang, in vain; later, when Chen Ping's agents set Xiang Yu against him, he left in anger and died of an abscess on the way home.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 居鄛人范增，年七十，素居家，好奇計，往說項梁曰：「陳勝敗固當。夫秦滅六國，楚最無罪。自懷王入秦不反，楚人憐之至今，故楚南公曰『楚雖三戶，亡秦必楚』也。今陳勝首事，不立楚後而自立，其勢不長。今君起江東，楚蠭起之將皆爭附君者，以君世世楚將，為能復立楚之後也。」

names.name: The fall of the Lü clan

summary.zh: 呂后臨朝稱制十五年，大封呂氏子弟為王。呂后死後，太尉周勃、丞相陳平等奪取北軍兵權，盡捕諸呂男女斬之，迎立代王劉恆即位，是為漢文帝。
summary.en: Empress Lü ruled as regent for fifteen years and made her kinsmen kings. When she died, the Grand Commandant Zhou Bo and the chancellor Chen Ping seized the Northern Army, rounded up the Lü men and women and executed them all, and brought in Liu Heng, King of Dai, as emperor — Emperor Wen.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九 呂太后本紀
passages.textZh: 悉捕諸呂男女，無少長皆斬之。

names.name: Tiying saves her father; mutilating punishments abolished

summary.zh: 齊太倉令淳于意有罪當受肉刑，他的小女兒緹縈隨父入長安，上書願沒入為官婢以贖父刑。漢文帝憐其意，下詔廢除黥、劓、斬趾等肉刑。
summary.en: Chunyu Yi, granary director of Qi, was sentenced to mutilation. His youngest daughter Tiying went with him to Chang'an and petitioned to be made a government slave to redeem his punishment. Moved, Emperor Wen abolished the mutilating punishments — tattooing, cutting off the nose, cutting off the feet.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十 孝文本紀
passages.textZh: 其少女緹縈自傷泣，乃隨其父至長安，上書曰：「妾父為吏，齊中皆稱其廉平，今坐法當刑。妾傷夫死者不可復生，刑者不可復屬，雖復欲改過自新，其道無由也。妾願沒入為官婢，贖父刑罪，使得自新。」

names.name: The Rebellion of the Seven States

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 漢景帝用晁錯之策削減諸侯王封地，吳王劉濞聯合楚、趙、膠西、濟南、菑川、膠東共七國以「誅晁錯、清君側」為名起兵。景帝殺晁錯仍不能止，命周亞夫率軍平叛，三個月而定。此後諸侯王權力大為削弱。
summary.en: Emperor Jing, on Chao Cuo's advice, cut down the lands of the kings. Liu Pi, King of Wu, with Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, Jinan, Zichuan and Jiaodong — seven kingdoms — rose "to punish Chao Cuo and clear the emperor's side". Executing Chao Cuo did not stop them; Zhou Yafu put the rising down in three months, and the kings never again had such power.

label.en: Liu Pi, King of Wu, killed (defeated)

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十一 孝景本紀
passages.textZh: 吳王濞、楚王戊、趙王遂、膠西王卬、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、膠東王雄渠反，發兵西鄉。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百六 吳王濞列傳
passages.textZh: 初，吳王之度淮，與楚王遂西敗棘壁，乘勝前，銳甚。
passages.textEn: When the king of Wu first crossed the Huai, he and the king of Chu went west and won at Jibi, and pressed on flushed with victory.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百六 吳王濞列傳
passages.textZh: 初，吳王之度淮，與楚王遂西敗棘壁，乘勝前，銳甚。梁孝王恐，遣六將軍擊吳，又敗梁兩將，士卒皆還走梁。
passages.textEn: At first, when the King of Wu crossed the Huai, he and the King of Chu went west and won at Jibi; pressing on with their victory, they were very strong. King Xiao of Liang, alarmed, sent six generals against Wu, but Wu beat two of them and their men all fled back to Liang.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷五十七 絳侯周勃世家
passages.textZh: 太尉既會兵滎陽，吳方攻梁，梁急，請救。太尉引兵東北走昌邑，深壁而守。
passages.textEn: The Grand Commandant had gathered his troops at Xingyang when Wu was attacking Liang; Liang, hard pressed, asked for help, but he led his army north-east to Changyi and dug in behind high walls.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷五十七 絳侯周勃世家
passages.textZh: 太尉不奉詔，堅壁不出，而使輕騎兵弓高侯等絕吳楚兵後食道。
passages.textEn: The Grand Commandant would not obey the order but kept behind his walls, and sent light cavalry under the Marquis of Gonggao to cut the Wu and Chu armies' supply line behind them.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百六 吳王濞列傳
passages.textZh: 吳兵欲西，梁城守堅，不敢西，即走條侯軍，會下邑。欲戰，條侯壁，不肯戰。吳糧絕，卒饑，數挑戰，遂夜奔條侯壁，驚東南。條侯使備西北，果從西北入。吳大敗，士卒多饑死，乃畔散。於是吳王乃與其麾下壯士數千人夜亡去，度江走丹徒，保東越。
passages.textEn: Wu wanted to go west, but Liang held its walls so firmly that Wu dared not, and turned on the Marquis of Tiao's army instead, meeting it at Xiayi. Wu wanted battle, but the Marquis stayed behind his walls. Wu's food ran out and its men starved; after many challenges it rushed the Marquis's walls by night, feinting at the south-east corner. The Marquis had the north-west guarded, and that is where they came in. Wu was crushed; many of its men died of hunger and the rest scattered. The King of Wu fled by night with a few thousand of his guard, crossed the Yangzi to Dantu and took refuge with Dong Yue.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百六 吳王濞列傳
passages.textZh: 漢使人以利啗東越，東越即紿吳王，吳王出勞軍，即使人鏦殺吳王，盛其頭，馳傳以聞。
passages.textEn: Han bribed Dong Yue, which tricked the King of Wu: when he came out to review its troops, they speared him to death and sent his head by post to the emperor.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百六 吳王濞列傳
passages.textZh: 三王之圍齊臨菑也，三月不能下。漢兵至，膠西、膠東、菑川王各引兵歸。
passages.textEn: The three kings had besieged Linzi in Qi for three months without taking it. When the Han army arrived, the Kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong and Zichuan each led their troops home.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷五十七 絳侯周勃世家
passages.textZh: 凡相攻守三月，而吳楚破平。
passages.textEn: In all the fighting lasted three months before Wu and Chu were broken and pacified.

label.zh: 吳王之度淮，與楚王遂西敗棘壁
label.en: Wu and Chu cross the Huai and win at Jibi

label.zh: 太尉引兵東北走昌邑，深壁而守

label.en: Wu turns on Zhou Yafu at Xiayi

label.zh: 吳王…夜亡去，度江走丹徒
label.en: The King of Wu flees to Dantu

label.zh: 三王之圍齊臨菑也，三月不能下

confidenceNote.zh: 「罷黜百家，獨尊儒術」是後人的概括；武帝朝仍兼用法家與黃老之術，今人對這一政策的實際程度有不同看法。
confidenceNote.en: "Dismiss the hundred schools and honour Confucianism alone" is a later summary; Wu's court still used legalist and Huang–Lao methods, and how far the policy went is debated.

summary.zh: 漢武帝即位後策問賢良，董仲舒對策建議「推明孔氏，抑黜百家」。武帝設五經博士、太學，以儒學取士，儒家逐漸成為官方正統。
summary.en: Emperor Wu questioned scholars on policy, and Dong Zhongshu proposed to "promote the school of Confucius and suppress the hundred schools". Wu set up erudites of the Five Classics and an imperial academy and recruited officials through Confucian learning, and Confucianism became, step by step, the official orthodoxy.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷五十六 董仲舒傳
passages.textZh: 推明孔氏，抑黜百家。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀 贊
passages.textZh: 罷黜百家，表章六經。

summary.zh: 衛青率軍出雲中，西至高闕，攻取河南地直到隴西，俘獲數千人、牲畜數十萬，趕走匈奴白羊王、樓煩王，漢以河南地設朔方郡。
summary.en: Wei Qing struck west from Yunzhong to Gaoque and took the land south of the river bend as far as Longxi, capturing thousands of people and hundreds of thousands of animals and driving off the Baiyang and Loufan kings of the Xiongnu; Han made the land into Shuofang commandery.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 令車騎將軍青出雲中以西至高闕。遂略河南地，至于隴西，捕首虜數千，畜數十萬，走白羊、樓煩王。遂以河南地為朔方郡。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 令車騎將軍青出雲中以西至高闕。遂略河南地，至于隴西，捕首虜數千，畜數十萬，走白羊、樓煩王。
passages.textEn: The General of Chariots and Cavalry Wei Qing was sent out from Yunzhong west to Gaoque. He overran the land south of the river as far as Longxi, took several thousand heads and prisoners and hundreds of thousands of beasts, and drove off the kings of Baiyang and Loufan.

label.en: Through the land south of the river to Longxi

summary.zh: 主父偃建議讓諸侯王推恩，把封地分給所有子弟為侯國。漢武帝採納此議，諸侯國越分越小，不再能與朝廷抗衡。
summary.en: Zhufu Yan proposed that kings be allowed to "extend grace" by dividing their lands among all their sons as marquisates. Emperor Wu adopted it; the kingdoms grew ever smaller and could no longer stand against the court.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十二 平津侯主父列傳
passages.textZh: 願陛下令諸侯得推恩分子弟，以地侯之。

summary.zh: 連年對匈奴用兵，國庫空虛。漢武帝任用鹽商東郭咸陽、冶鐵商孔僅為大農丞，主管鹽鐵事務，將煮鹽、冶鐵收歸官營，又行均輸、平準與算緡告緡。
summary.en: Years of war with the Xiongnu had emptied the treasury. Emperor Wu put the salt merchant Dongguo Xianyang and the iron master Kong Jin in charge of salt and iron as assistants to the Grand Minister of Agriculture, made salt-boiling and iron-smelting state monopolies, and added price stabilisation, state transport and new taxes on merchants' wealth.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十 平準書
passages.textZh: 以東郭咸陽、孔僅為大農丞，領鹽鐵事；桑弘羊以計算用事，侍中。

summary.zh: 太初元年五月，漢武帝改定曆法，以正月為歲首（此前沿用秦曆，以十月為歲首），崇尚黃色，定官名，協音律。太初曆是中國第一部有完整記載的曆法。
summary.en: In the fifth month of 104 BCE Emperor Wu reformed the calendar, making the first month the start of the year (Han had kept the Qin practice of starting it in the tenth month), adopting yellow as the dynastic colour, fixing official titles and tuning the musical pitches. The Taichu calendar is the first Chinese calendar recorded in full.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 正曆，以正月為歲首。色上黃，數用五，定官名，協音律。

summary.zh: 漢武帝為得大宛汗血馬，命貳師將軍李廣利遠征大宛。第一次遠征兵疲糧盡而返；再次出兵圍宛城四十餘日，大宛貴族殺國王毋寡求和，漢軍取良馬數十匹、中等以下馬三千餘匹而還。
summary.en: To get the "blood-sweating" horses of Dayuan (Ferghana), Emperor Wu sent Li Guangli, the Ershi General, against it. The first expedition came back exhausted and starving; the second besieged the city for over forty days until the Dayuan nobles killed their king Wugua and sued for peace, and the Han army returned with dozens of fine horses and three thousand lesser ones.

label.en: The Ershi general marches on Dayuan

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 貳師將軍廣利斬大宛王首，獲汗血馬來。

summary.zh: 騎都尉李陵率步兵五千人出居延北，與單于主力遭遇，轉戰千里，斬首虜萬餘人，終因矢盡無援兵敗投降匈奴。司馬遷為其辯護，觸怒武帝，被處以宮刑。
summary.en: Li Ling, Commandant of Cavalry, led five thousand infantry north from Juyan and met the Chanyu's main army; fighting for a thousand li, he killed or captured over ten thousand, but with arrows gone and no relief he was beaten and surrendered. Sima Qian spoke in his defence, angered the emperor, and was castrated.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 騎都尉李陵將步兵五千人出居延北，與單于戰，斬首虜萬餘級。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 李陵傳
passages.textZh: 陵於是將其歩卒五千人出居延，北行三十日，至浚稽山止營，舉圖所過山川地形，使麾下騎陳歩樂還以聞。
passages.textEn: So Li Ling led his five thousand foot out from Juyan, marched north for thirty days and made camp at Mount Junji, mapping the mountains and rivers he passed, and sent his rider Chen Bule back to report.

label.zh: 將其歩卒五千人出居延，北行三十日，至浚稽山
label.en: Five thousand foot north from Juyan to Mount Junji

summary.zh: 晚年的漢武帝疑心有人以巫蠱詛咒自己，命江充等查辦。江充在太子劉據宮中掘出蠱物，太子恐懼，與皇后衛子夫謀殺江充，發兵與丞相劉屈氂大戰於長安，死者數萬。太子兵敗自殺，衛皇后亦自盡。
summary.en: In his old age Emperor Wu suspected sorcery against him and set Jiang Chong to investigate. Jiang Chong "dug up" curse objects in the palace of the Crown Prince Liu Ju; the frightened prince, with Empress Wei Zifu, had Jiang Chong killed and fought the chancellor Liu Qumao in the streets of Chang'an, tens of thousands dying. The prince was beaten and killed himself; the empress did the same.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 桉道侯韓說、使者江充等掘蠱太子宮。壬午，太子與皇后謀斬充，以節發兵與丞相劉屈氂大戰長安，死者數萬人。

names.name: The debate on salt and iron

summary.zh: 漢昭帝始元六年，詔令郡國推舉的賢良、文學之士詢問民間疾苦，賢良文學與御史大夫桑弘羊就鹽鐵官營、酒榷、均輸等政策展開辯論，部分措施被罷除。桓寬後來將辯論整理為《鹽鐵論》。
summary.en: In 81 BCE Emperor Zhao had the worthies and literati recommended by the commanderies asked about the people's hardships; they debated the salt and iron monopolies, the liquor monopoly and state transport with the Imperial Counsellor Sang Hongyang, and some measures were dropped. Huan Kuan later wrote the debate up as the Discourses on Salt and Iron.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷七 昭帝紀
passages.textZh: 詔有司問郡國所舉賢良文學民所疾苦。

names.name: The Huhanye Chanyu comes to court

summary.zh: 匈奴內亂，五單于爭立，呼韓邪單于向漢稱臣。甘露三年正月，呼韓邪單于親至甘泉宮朝見漢宣帝，漢待以殊禮，並派兵護送其歸國。漢與匈奴此後維持了數十年和平。
summary.en: The Xiongnu fell into civil war among five rival chanyus, and the Huhanye Chanyu submitted to Han. In the first month of 51 BCE he came in person to the Ganquan palace to meet Emperor Xuan, was received with special honours and escorted home by Han troops. Peace with the Xiongnu followed for decades.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷八 宣帝紀
passages.textZh: 匈奴呼韓邪單于稽侯蛳來朝，贊謁稱藩臣而不名。

names.name: Chen Tang kills the Zhizhi Chanyu

summary.zh: 西域都護副校尉陳湯與甘延壽矯詔發西域諸國兵，遠征康居境內的郅支單于城，攻破其城，斬郅支單于。陳湯上疏說：「明犯彊漢者，雖遠必誅。」
summary.en: Chen Tang, deputy to the Protector of the Western Regions, with Gan Yanshou raised the armies of the Western Regions on forged orders and marched on the Zhizhi Chanyu's fortress in Kangju, stormed it and killed the chanyu. Chen Tang wrote: "Those who offend mighty Han shall be punished, however far away."

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷七十 陳湯傳
passages.textZh: 明犯彊漢者，雖遠必誅。

summary.zh: 名雉，劉邦微時的妻子。劉邦稱帝後立為皇后，協助誅殺韓信、彭越等功臣。惠帝死後臨朝稱制八年，大封呂氏為王，是中國歷史上第一位臨朝稱制的皇后。
summary.en: Lü Zhi, Liu Bang's wife from his humble days, made empress when he took the throne; she helped destroy the great generals Han Xin and Peng Yue. After Emperor Hui died she ruled as regent for eight years and made her kinsmen kings — the first empress in Chinese history to rule in her own name as regent.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九 呂太后本紀
passages.textZh: 呂太后者，高祖微時妃也，生孝惠帝、女魯元太后。

summary.zh: 名劉恆，劉邦之子，原為代王。誅諸呂後被迎立為帝，在位期間輕徭薄賦、與民休息、廢除肉刑，生活儉樸；與景帝並稱「文景之治」。
summary.en: Liu Heng, a son of Liu Bang and King of Dai, brought to the throne after the fall of the Lü. He lightened taxes and labour, let the country recover, abolished mutilating punishments and lived frugally; with his son Emperor Jing his reign is remembered as the "rule of Wen and Jing".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十 孝文本紀
passages.textZh: 孝文皇帝，高祖中子也。高祖十一年春，已破陳豨軍，定代地，立為代王，都中都。

summary.zh: 名劉徹，在位五十四年。北擊匈奴、通西域、南平南越、東滅朝鮮，設刺史部，獨尊儒術，行鹽鐵官營，首創年號。晚年巫蠱之禍中太子被逼自殺，後下〈輪台詔〉悔過。
summary.en: Liu Che, who reigned fifty-four years. He struck at the Xiongnu, opened the Western Regions, conquered Nanyue and Joseon, created the inspection provinces, made Confucianism the state learning, monopolised salt and iron and began the custom of era names. In the witchcraft affair of his old age his heir was driven to suicide; he later issued the Luntai edict regretting his wars.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十二 孝武本紀
passages.textZh: 孝武皇帝者，孝景中子也。母曰王太后。

summary.zh: 平陽人，出身奴僕，因姊衛子夫得寵而進用。七次出擊匈奴，前127年收復河南地，前119年漠北之戰擊敗單于主力，官至大將軍、大司馬。
summary.en: Of Pingyang, born a servant, he rose when his sister Wei Zifu became the emperor's favourite. He led seven campaigns against the Xiongnu, took back the land south of the river bend in 127 BCE and beat the Chanyu's main army beyond the desert in 119, rising to General-in-Chief and Grand Marshal.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 大將軍衛青者，平陽人也。其父鄭季，為吏，給事平陽侯家，與侯妾衛媼通，生青。

summary.zh: 隴西成紀人，善騎射，匈奴稱他為「漢之飛將軍」，數年不敢入右北平。一生與匈奴大小七十餘戰卻始終未能封侯。前119年漠北之戰中迷路失期，自剄而死。司馬遷贊他：「桃李不言，下自成蹊。」
summary.en: Of Chengji in Longxi, a superb horseman and archer whom the Xiongnu called "the Flying General of Han" and for years dared not raid Youbeiping. He fought the Xiongnu more than seventy times but was never made a marquis. In the great campaign of 119 BCE he lost his way, arrived late and cut his own throat. Sima Qian wrote of him: "The peach and the plum do not speak, yet a path forms beneath them."

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百零九 李將軍列傳
passages.textZh: 李將軍廣者，隴西成紀人也。其先曰李信，秦時爲將，逐得燕太子丹者也。

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百零九 李將軍列傳
passages.textZh: 諺曰「桃李不言，下自成蹊」

confidenceNote.zh: 生卒年為約數。
confidenceNote.en: Dates approximate.

summary.zh: 廣川人，治《春秋》公羊學。漢武帝策問時上〈天人三策〉，主張「推明孔氏，抑黜百家」，以天人感應之說論政，影響漢代以後兩千年的政治思想。
summary.en: Of Guangchuan, a scholar of the Gongyang tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals. In answer to Emperor Wu's questions he presented three memorials on Heaven and man, urging the promotion of Confucius and the suppression of the other schools and reading politics through the mutual response of Heaven and man — shaping political thought for two thousand years.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷五十六 董仲舒傳
passages.textZh: 董仲舒，廣川人也。少治《春秋》，孝景時爲博士。

summary.zh: 字子卿。前100年以中郎將持節出使匈奴，被扣留，不肯投降，被放逐到北海（今貝加爾湖）牧羊，「杖漢節牧羊，臥起操持，節旄盡落」。十九年後才得歸漢。
summary.en: Courtesy name Ziqing. Sent to the Xiongnu as envoy with the imperial tally in 100 BCE, he was detained and would not surrender, and was banished to herd sheep by the "Northern Sea" (Lake Baikal) — "he herded the sheep with the Han tally in his hand, holding it waking and sleeping, until its tassels had all fallen away". He came home after nineteen years.

label.en: Leaves as envoy to the Xiongnu

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 蘇武傳
passages.textZh: 武既至海上，廩食不至，掘野鼠去草實而食之。杖漢節牧羊，臥起操持，節旄盡落。

summary.zh: 霍去病之弟，受漢武帝遺詔輔佐昭帝，以大司馬大將軍主政二十年。昭帝死後立昌邑王劉賀，二十七日後以「行淫亂」廢之，改立宣帝。死後霍氏因謀反被族滅。
summary.en: Huo Qubing's half-brother, named by Emperor Wu's will to guide the boy Emperor Zhao, he ran the government as Grand Marshal for twenty years. After Zhao died he set up Liu He, King of Changyi, deposed him after twenty-seven days for "licentiousness" and enthroned Emperor Xuan. After his death his family was exterminated for treason.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六十八 霍光傳
passages.textZh: 霍光字子孟，票騎將軍去病弟也。

summary.zh: 字子公，山陽瑕丘人。任西域都護副校尉時，與甘延壽矯詔發兵遠征康居，斬郅支單于，上疏說「明犯彊漢者，雖遠必誅」。後因矯詔等事屢遭貶黜。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zigong, of Xiaqiu in Shanyang. As deputy to the Protector of the Western Regions he joined Gan Yanshou in raising troops on forged orders, marched into Kangju and killed the Zhizhi Chanyu, writing that "those who offend mighty Han shall be punished, however far away". He was later demoted repeatedly, for the forged orders among other things.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷七十 陳湯傳
passages.textZh: 陳湯字子公，山陽瑕丘人也。少好書，博達善屬文。

summary.zh: 王莽末年荊州饑荒，百姓入山澤挖野荸薺充飢，互相爭奪。新市人王匡、王鳳為眾人調解糾紛，被推為首領，聚眾於綠林山，數年間發展至數萬人，後分為新市兵、下江兵等，擁立劉玄為更始帝。
summary.en: Late in Wang Mang's reign famine struck Jingzhou; people went into the marshes to dig wild water chestnuts and fought over them. Wang Kuang and Wang Feng of Xinshi settled their quarrels and were made leaders, gathering in the Lülin hills; in a few years they were tens of thousands, later dividing into the Xinshi and Xiajiang armies and setting up Liu Xuan as the Gengshi Emperor.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷十一 劉玄傳
passages.textZh: 王莽末，南方飢饉，人庶羣入野澤，掘鳧茈而食之，更相侵奪。

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷十一 劉玄傳
passages.textZh: 新市人王匡、王鳳爲平理諍訟，遂推爲渠帥，衆數百人。

summary.zh: 琅邪人樊崇在莒起事，轉戰青、徐一帶。為了在與官軍交戰時辨識敵我，起義者把眉毛塗成紅色，號稱「赤眉」。後西入關中，攻佔長安，立劉盆子為帝。
summary.en: Fan Chong of Langya rose at Ju and fought across Qing and Xu. To tell friend from foe in battle with the government troops, his men painted their eyebrows red and were called the "Red Eyebrows". They later marched west, took Chang'an and set up Liu Penzi as emperor.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷十一 劉盆子傳
passages.textZh: 乃皆朱其眉以相識別，由是號曰赤眉。

summary.zh: 昆陽之戰後各地紛紛響應。地皇四年十月，起義軍攻入長安，宮中大火，王莽退守漸臺，被商人杜吳殺死，校尉公賓就斬其首。新朝滅亡。
summary.en: After Kunyang the provinces rose on every side. In the tenth month of 23 the rebels broke into Chang'an; the palace burned, Wang Mang fell back to the Jian terrace, and there the merchant Du Wu killed him and the officer Gongbin Jiu cut off his head. Xin was over.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十九下 王莽傳下
passages.textZh: 商人杜吳殺莽，取其綬。

summary.zh: 建武元年六月，劉秀在鄗縣南千秋亭五成陌即皇帝位，改元建武，延續漢朝國號；十月定都洛陽，史稱東漢。
summary.en: In the sixth month of 25 Liu Xiu took the throne at Hao, proclaiming the Jianwu era and keeping the name Han; in the tenth month he made Luoyang his capital — the Eastern Han.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一上 光武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 六月己未，即皇帝位。

summary.zh: 公孫述據蜀稱帝十二年。建武十二年，吳漢、臧宮率漢軍攻成都，大破之，公孫述受傷當夜死去，蜀地平定，光武帝完成統一。
summary.en: Gongsun Shu had held Shu as emperor for twelve years. In 36 Wu Han and Zang Gong stormed Chengdu; Gongsun Shu was wounded and died that night, Shu was pacified, and Emperor Guangwu's reunification was complete.

label.en: Gongsun Shu, wounded, died that night (defeated)

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一下 光武帝紀下
passages.textZh: 吳漢、臧宮與公孫述戰於成都，大破之。

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一下 光武帝紀下
passages.textZh: 秋七月，威虜將軍馮駿拔江州，獲田戎。九月，吳漢大破公孫述將謝豐于廣都，斬之。輔威將軍臧宮拔涪城，斬公孫恢。
passages.textEn: In the seventh month, in autumn, Feng Jun took Jiangzhou and captured Tian Rong. In the ninth month Wu Han routed Gongsun Shu's general Xie Feng at Guangdu and beheaded him. Zang Gong took Fucheng and beheaded Gongsun Hui.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一下 光武帝紀下
passages.textZh: 冬十一月戊寅，吳漢、臧宮與公孫述戰於成都，大破之。述被創，夜死。辛巳，吳漢屠成都，夷述宗族及延岑等。
passages.textEn: On wuyin of the eleventh month, in winter, Wu Han and Zang Gong fought Gongsun Shu at Chengdu and routed him; Shu was wounded and died that night. On xinsi Wu Han sacked Chengdu and wiped out Shu's clan and Yan Cen and the others.

label.zh: 拔江州；吳漢大破謝豐于廣都
吳漢與公孫述戰於成都

names.name: The Trưng sisters and Ma Yuan

summary.zh: 建武十六年，交阯女子徵側與妹妹徵貳起兵反漢，攻佔交阯等郡，自立為王。光武帝派伏波將軍馬援南征，建武十九年斬徵側、徵貳，平定交阯。越南史上尊二人為「徵氏姊妹」。
summary.en: In 40 the sisters Zheng Ce and Zheng Er (Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị) of Jiaozhi rose against Han, took Jiaozhi and neighbouring commanderies and declared themselves queens. Emperor Guangwu sent Ma Yuan, the Wave-Calming General, south; in 43 he killed both sisters and pacified Jiaozhi. Vietnamese history honours them as the Trưng Sisters.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷二十四 馬援列傳
passages.textZh: 交阯女子徵側及女弟徵貳反，攻沒其郡，九真、日南、合浦蠻夷皆應之，寇略嶺外六十餘城，側自立爲王。

summary.zh: 建武二十四年，匈奴南邊八部大人共立比為呼韓邪單于，歸附漢朝，入居塞內，是為南匈奴；留在漠北者為北匈奴。
summary.en: In 48 the chiefs of the eight southern Xiongnu tribes set up Bi as Huhanye Chanyu and submitted to Han, moving inside the frontier — the Southern Xiongnu; those who stayed beyond the desert were the Northern Xiongnu.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八十九 南匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 八部大人共議立比為呼韓邪單于，以其大父嘗依漢得安，故欲襲其號。

names.name: Envoys from the land of Wa (Na)

summary.zh: 建武中元二年，倭奴國派使者到洛陽奉貢朝賀，使者自稱大夫，光武帝賜以印綬。1784年日本福岡志賀島出土刻有「漢委奴國王」的金印，一般認為就是這方印。
summary.en: In 57 envoys from the Na kingdom of Wa came to Luoyang with tribute, calling themselves ministers, and Emperor Guangwu gave them a seal and ribbon. A gold seal inscribed "King of Na of Wa of Han" found on Shikanoshima near Fukuoka in 1784 is generally taken to be this seal.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八十五 東夷列傳
passages.textZh: 建武中元二年，倭奴國奉貢朝賀，使人自稱大夫，倭國之極南界也。

names.name: Gan Ying sets out for Rome

summary.zh: 和帝永元九年，西域都護班超派甘英出使大秦（羅馬），到達條支，臨大海欲渡，安息船人告訴他海上往返難測，甘英遂止。這是漢代使者西行最遠的記錄。
summary.en: In 97 Ban Chao, Protector of the Western Regions, sent Gan Ying as envoy to Da Qin (Rome). He reached Tiaozhi on the edge of a great sea; Parthian sailors told him the voyage was long and perilous, and he turned back — the farthest west any Han envoy is recorded to have gone.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八十八 西域傳
passages.textZh: 都護班超遣甘英使大秦，抵條支。臨大海欲度，而安息西界船人謂英曰：「海水廣大，往來者逢善風三月乃得度，若遇遲風，亦有二歲者，故入海人皆齎三歲糧。海中善使人思土戀慕，數有死亡者。」

confidenceNote.zh: 考古發現西漢已有麻紙（如灞橋紙、放馬灘紙），蔡倫應是改良與推廣者，而非紙的發明者。引文照錄維基文庫此卷文字，該卷為簡體字本。
confidenceNote.en: Archaeology has found hemp paper from the Western Han (Baqiao, Fangmatan): Cai Lun improved and spread paper rather than inventing it. The quotation follows the Wikisource text of this chapter, which is in simplified characters.

summary.zh: 宦官蔡倫用樹皮、麻頭、破布和舊魚網造紙，元興元年奏上，和帝稱善，此後紙張廣泛使用，世稱「蔡侯紙」。
summary.en: The eunuch Cai Lun made paper from tree bark, hemp scraps, rags and old fishing nets and presented it in 105; the emperor praised it, paper came into general use, and people called it "Marquis Cai's paper".

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷七十八 宦者列傳 蔡倫
passages.textZh: 伦乃造意，用树肤、麻头及敝布、鱼网以为紙。元兴元年奏上之，帝善其能，自是莫不从用焉，故天下咸称“蔡侯紙”。元初元年，邓太后以伦久宿卫，封为龍亭侯，邑三百户。

summary.zh: 外戚梁冀專權二十年，毒死質帝，立桓帝，權傾朝野。延熹二年，桓帝與宦官單超等五人密謀，派司隸校尉張彪率兵包圍梁冀府第，收其大將軍印綬，梁冀與妻自殺。五名宦官同日封侯，宦官從此專權。
summary.en: The consort kinsman Liang Ji had ruled for twenty years, poisoning Emperor Zhi and setting up Emperor Huan. In 159 Huan plotted with five eunuchs led by Shan Chao; the Colonel of the Capital Zhang Biao surrounded Liang Ji's mansion and took his seal, and Liang Ji and his wife killed themselves. The five eunuchs were all made marquises the same day, and the eunuchs ruled from then on.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷七 孝桓帝紀
passages.textZh: 帝御前殿，詔司隷校尉張彪將兵圍兾第，收大將軍印綬，兾與妻皆自殺。

summary.zh: 延熹九年，宦官誣告司隸校尉李膺等「結黨」誹謗朝政，李膺等二百餘人被捕下獄，名字被登記於王府，終身禁錮不得做官。169年第二次黨錮，李膺等百餘人被殺。直到184年黃巾起事才解除黨禁。
summary.en: In 166 the eunuchs accused the Colonel of the Capital Li Ying and others of forming a faction to slander the government; over two hundred were jailed and their names recorded so they could never hold office. In the second proscription of 169 Li Ying and more than a hundred others were killed. The ban was lifted only when the Yellow Turbans rose in 184.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷七 孝桓帝紀
passages.textZh: 司隷校尉李膺等二百餘人受誣爲黨人，並坐下獄，書名王府。

names.name: Envoys from "Andun, King of Da Qin"

summary.zh: 延熹九年，自稱大秦王安敦的使者從日南郡邊外來到漢朝，獻象牙、犀角、玳瑁，大秦與漢從此第一次直接往來。「安敦」一般認為指羅馬皇帝馬可·奧理略·安東尼努斯；使者可能是自稱羅馬使節的商人。
summary.en: In 166 envoys claiming to come from "Andun, King of Da Qin" arrived from beyond Rinan, presenting ivory, rhinoceros horn and tortoiseshell — the first direct contact between Rome and Han. "Andun" is usually identified with the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus; the "envoys" may have been merchants presenting themselves as such.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八十八 西域傳
passages.textZh: 大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外獻象牙、犀角、瑇瑁，始乃一通焉。

summary.zh: 熹平四年，漢靈帝詔令蔡邕等儒者校正五經文字，刻於石碑，立在洛陽太學門外，作為經書的標準文本。這是中國最早的官定刻石經書，殘石至今尚存。
summary.en: In 175 Emperor Ling ordered Cai Yong and other scholars to correct the texts of the Five Classics and carve them on stone tablets set up outside the imperial academy at Luoyang as the standard text — the earliest official stone classics in China; fragments survive.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀
passages.textZh: 詔諸儒正五經文字，刻石立于太學門外。

summary.zh: 字文淵，扶風茂陵人，東漢開國名將，任伏波將軍。南征交阯平定徵側、徵貳，晚年請纓出征五溪蠻，死於軍中。他曾說：「男兒要當死於邊野，以馬革裹屍還葬耳。」
summary.en: Courtesy name Wenyuan, of Maoling in Fufeng, a founding general of the Eastern Han, the Wave-Calming General. He put down the Trưng sisters in Jiaozhi, and in old age volunteered against the Wuxi tribes and died on campaign. He once said: "A man should die on the frontier and come home wrapped in a horse's hide."

label.en: Dies on campaign against the Wuxi tribes

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷二十四 馬援列傳
passages.textZh: 援曰：「方今匈奴、烏桓尚擾北邊，欲自請擊之。男兒要當死於邊野，以馬革裹屍還葬耳，何能臥床上在兒女子手中邪！」

summary.zh: 字孟堅，扶風安陵人，班超之兄。繼承父親班彪的事業，歷二十餘年撰成《漢書》，是第一部紀傳體斷代史；又作〈兩都賦〉，隨竇憲北征時撰〈燕然山銘〉。後因竇憲案牽連，死於獄中。《漢書》的八表與〈天文志〉由其妹班昭等續成。
summary.en: Courtesy name Mengjian, of Anling in Fufeng, elder brother of Ban Chao. Continuing his father Ban Biao's work, he spent over twenty years writing the Book of Han, the first history of a single dynasty in annals-and-biographies form; he also wrote the "Rhapsody on the Two Capitals" and, on Dou Xian's northern campaign, the Yanran inscription. Caught up in Dou Xian's fall, he died in prison; his sister Ban Zhao and others completed the Book of Han's tables and astronomy treatise.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷四十上 班彪列傳上 附班固
passages.textZh: 固字孟堅。年九歲，能屬文誦詩賦，及長，遂博貫載籍，九流百家之言，無不窮究。

summary.zh: 字敬仲，桂陽人，東漢宦官，任尚方令時改良造紙術，世稱「蔡侯紙」，封龍亭侯。後因牽涉安帝祖母宋貴人冤案，畏罪自殺。
summary.en: Courtesy name Jingzhong, of Guiyang, a eunuch of Eastern Han who, as head of the imperial workshops, improved papermaking — "Marquis Cai's paper" — and was made Marquis of Longting. Implicated in the wrongful case against Emperor An's grandmother Lady Song, he killed himself.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷七十八 宦者列傳 蔡倫
passages.textZh: 蔡伦字敬仲，桂陽人也。

summary.zh: 字元禮，潁川襄城人，任司隸校尉，執法嚴厲，不畏宦官，士人以能與他交往為榮，稱為「登龍門」。166年第一次黨錮被捕，169年第二次黨錮死於獄中。
summary.en: Courtesy name Yuanli, of Xiangcheng in Yingchuan, Colonel of the Capital, who enforced the law without fear of the eunuchs; scholars counted it an honour to be received by him — "to pass the Dragon Gate". Arrested in the first proscription of 166, he died in prison in the second, in 169.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷六十七 黨錮列傳 李膺
passages.textZh: 士有被其容接者，名爲登龍門。

summary.zh: 中平六年，大將軍何進謀誅宦官反被殺，并州牧董卓率兵入洛陽，廢少帝劉辯為弘農王，立年僅九歲的陳留王劉協為帝（漢獻帝），隨即殺何太后，專斷朝政。
summary.en: In 189 the General-in-Chief He Jin was killed plotting against the eunuchs, and Dong Zhuo, governor of Bing, marched into Luoyang. He deposed the young emperor Liu Bian, made the nine-year-old Prince of Chenliu, Liu Xie, emperor (Emperor Xian), then killed Empress Dowager He and took the government into his own hands.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝獻帝紀
passages.textZh: 九月甲戌，即皇帝位，年九歲。

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝獻帝紀
passages.textZh: 丙子，董卓殺皇太后何氏。

names.name: Dong Zhuo moves the capital to Chang'an

summary.zh: 關東諸州郡起兵討董卓，董卓挾獻帝西遷長安，驅趕洛陽百姓全部西入關中，並焚燒洛陽宮廟與民居。
summary.en: When the eastern provinces rose against him, Dong Zhuo took Emperor Xian west to Chang'an, drove the people of Luoyang into the passes and burned the palaces, temples and houses of the old capital.

label.en: The people of Luoyang driven west

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝獻帝紀
passages.textZh: 丁亥，遷都長安。董卓驅徙京師百姓悉西入關，自留屯畢圭苑。

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝獻帝紀
passages.textZh: 己酉，董卓焚洛陽宮廟及人家。

summary.zh: 初平三年四月，司徒王允與董卓部將呂布合謀，在長安刺殺董卓，夷其三族。不久董卓部將李傕、郭汜攻破長安，王允被殺，呂布出逃。
summary.en: In the fourth month of 192 the Minister over the Masses Wang Yun and Dong Zhuo's own officer Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo in Chang'an and exterminated his family. Soon after, Dong Zhuo's generals Li Jue and Guo Si stormed Chang'an; Wang Yun was killed and Lü Bu fled.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝獻帝紀
passages.textZh: 夏四月辛巳，誅董卓，夷三族。司徒王允錄尚書事，揔朝政，遣使者張种撫慰山東。

names.name: Cao Cao brings the emperor to Xu

summary.zh: 獻帝從長安東歸，流離至殘破的洛陽。建安元年，曹操迎獻帝遷都許縣，自任司空、行車騎將軍事，從此「奉天子以令不臣」。
summary.en: Emperor Xian escaped east from Chang'an to the ruins of Luoyang. In 196 Cao Cao brought him to Xu, made himself Minister of Works acting as General of Chariots and Cavalry, and from then on gave orders in the emperor's name.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝獻帝紀
passages.textZh: 庚申，遷都許。己巳，幸曹操營。九月，太尉楊彪、司空張喜罷。冬十一月丙戌，曹操自爲司空，行車騎將軍事，百官緫己以聽。

summary.zh: 曹操死後，其子曹丕繼為魏王。延康元年十月，漢獻帝被迫禪位，曹丕即皇帝位，國號魏，改元黃初，東漢亡。
summary.en: After Cao Cao died his son Cao Pi became King of Wei. In the tenth month of 220 Emperor Xian was made to abdicate; Cao Pi took the throne as emperor of Wei with the era Huangchu, and the Eastern Han was over.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷二 魏書 文帝紀
passages.textZh: 使兼御史大夫張音持節奉璽綬禪位

summary.zh: 聽聞曹丕篡漢、又傳獻帝遇害，劉備於章武元年四月在成都武擔山之南即皇帝位，國號仍為漢，史稱蜀漢。
summary.en: Hearing that Cao Pi had usurped the Han — and rumours that Emperor Xian was dead — Liu Bei took the throne in the fourth month of 221 south of Wudan hill in Chengdu, keeping the name Han; historians call his state Shu Han.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 即皇帝位於成都武擔之南。

summary.zh: 黃龍元年四月，夏口、武昌報稱黃龍、鳳凰出現，孫權在武昌南郊即皇帝位，改元黃龍，同年秋遷都建業。三國鼎立正式形成。
summary.en: In the fourth month of 229, after reports of a yellow dragon and phoenixes at Xiakou and Wuchang, Sun Quan took the throne at the southern suburb of Wuchang with the era Huanglong, moving his capital to Jianye that autumn. Three emperors now reigned at once.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 吳書 吳主傳
passages.textZh: 夏四月，夏口、武昌並言黃龍、鳳凰見。丙申，南郊即皇帝位。

summary.zh: 嘉平元年正月，少帝曹芳往高平陵祭掃魏明帝，輔政的大將軍曹爽兄弟隨行。稱病多年的太傅司馬懿乘機關閉洛陽城門，奏請永寧太后罷免曹爽兄弟，隨後誅殺曹爽及其黨羽，夷三族。魏國大權從此歸於司馬氏。
summary.en: In the first month of 249 the boy emperor Cao Fang went to sacrifice at the Gaoping tomb of Emperor Ming, and the regent Cao Shuang and his brothers went with him. Sima Yi, who had feigned illness for years, shut the gates of Luoyang and had the Empress Dowager dismiss the Cao brothers; soon he executed Cao Shuang and his party with their families. Power in Wei passed to the Sima.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一 宣帝紀
passages.textZh: 天子謁高平陵，爽兄弟皆從。是日，太白襲月。帝于是奏永寧太后廢爽兄弟。時景帝為中護軍，將兵屯司馬門。

confidenceNote.zh: 受禪在咸熙二年十二月丙寅，換算為公元266年2月。引文出自〈武帝紀〉所載告天策文。
confidenceNote.en: The abdication fell on bingyin of the twelfth month of Xianxi 2, i.e. February 266. The quotation is from the address to Heaven recorded in the annals.

summary.zh: 咸熙二年十二月（公元266年初），魏元帝曹奐禪位，晉王司馬炎即皇帝位，國號晉，改元泰始，定都洛陽，史稱西晉。
summary.en: At the end of 265 (early 266 by the Western calendar) the last Wei emperor Cao Huan abdicated, and Sima Yan, King of Jin, took the throne as emperor of Jin with the era Taishi, ruling from Luoyang — the Western Jin.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷三 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 敬簡元辰，升壇受禪，告類上帝，永答眾望。

summary.zh: 晉滅吳統一後頒布戶調之式：男子一人可佔田七十畝、女子三十畝；丁男課田五十畝、丁女二十畝，次丁男減半。官員依品級佔田。
summary.en: After the conquest of Wu, Jin issued its household tax rules: each man might hold seventy mu of land and each woman thirty; adult men were taxed on fifty mu and adult women on twenty, younger adults half that. Officials held land by rank.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷二十六 食貨志
passages.textZh: 男子一人占田七十畝，女子三十畝。其外丁男課田五十畝，丁女二十畝，次丁男半之，女則不課。

names.name: The War of the Eight Princes

summary.zh: 晉惠帝愚弱，皇后賈南風聯合楚王司馬瑋誅殺輔政的太傅楊駿，廢黜楊太后。此後汝南王亮、楚王瑋、趙王倫、齊王冏、長沙王乂、成都王穎、河間王顒、東海王越相繼起兵爭權，混戰十六年，西晉元氣耗盡，北方各族乘機起兵。
summary.en: Emperor Hui was simple-minded. Empress Jia Nanfeng, with the Prince of Chu Sima Wei, killed the regent Yang Jun and deposed the Empress Dowager Yang. Then the princes of Runan, Chu, Zhao, Qi, Changsha, Chengdu, Hejian and Donghai fought one another for power for sixteen years, draining the Western Jin and opening the north to the peoples who rose against it.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷四 惠帝紀
passages.textZh: 三月辛卯，誅太傅楊駿，駿弟衛將軍珧，太子太保濟，中護軍張劭，散騎常侍段廣、楊邈，左將軍劉預，河南尹李斌，中書令蔣俊，東夷校尉文淑，尚書武茂，皆夷三族。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷四 惠帝紀
passages.textZh: 賈后矯詔廢皇太后爲庶人，徙于金墉城

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷四 惠帝紀
passages.textZh: 己亥，趙王倫矯詔害賈庶人于金墉城。

summary.zh: 匈奴左賢王劉淵（字元海）在左國城起兵，永興元年在南郊即漢王位，追尊蜀漢後主劉禪，以漢的繼承者自居。308年稱帝，遷都平陽；其族子劉曜後改國號為趙（前趙）。
summary.en: Liu Yuan (courtesy name Yuanhai), Worthy King of the Left of the Xiongnu, rose at Zuoguo and in 304 took the title King of Han at the southern suburb, honouring the last Shu Han emperor Liu Shan and presenting himself as heir to the Han. He became emperor in 308 at Pingyang; his kinsman Liu Yao later renamed the state Zhao (the Former Zhao).

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零一 劉元海載記
passages.textZh: 元海乃為壇於南郊，僭即漢王位

summary.zh: 流民首領李特之子李雄攻佔成都，永興元年稱成都王，廢除晉法，約法七章；306年稱帝，國號大成（後改漢，史稱成漢）。
summary.en: Li Xiong, son of the refugee leader Li Te, took Chengdu and in 304 styled himself King of Chengdu, abolishing the Jin laws for a code of seven articles; in 306 he became emperor of Great Cheng (later renamed Han — the Cheng Han).

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十一 李雄載記
passages.textZh: 以永興元年僭稱成都王，赦其境內，建元為建興，除晉法，約法七章。

names.name: Emperor Min surrenders; the Western Jin ends

summary.zh: 建興四年十一月，漢趙大將劉曜圍長安，城中糧盡，晉愍帝乘羊車、袒露上身、口銜玉璧、載著棺材出城投降，被送往平陽，次年遇害。西晉滅亡。
summary.en: In the eleventh month of 316 the Han Zhao general Liu Yao besieged Chang'an until its food ran out; Emperor Min rode out in a goat cart, bare to the waist, a jade disc in his mouth and his coffin carried behind him, and surrendered. He was taken to Pingyang and killed the next year. The Western Jin was over.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷五 愍帝紀
passages.textZh: 使侍中宋敞送箋于曜，帝乘羊車，肉袒銜壁，輿櫬出降。

names.name: Sima Rui becomes King of Jin in Jiankang

summary.zh: 長安陷落的消息傳到江東，琅邪王司馬睿於建武元年三月在建康即晉王位，次年即皇帝位，是為晉元帝，東晉開始。
summary.en: When news of Chang'an's fall reached the south, Sima Rui, Prince of Langya, took the title King of Jin at Jiankang in the third month of 317 and became emperor the next year — Emperor Yuan, first of the Eastern Jin.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷六 元帝紀
passages.textZh: 辛卯，卽王位，大赦，改元。其殺祖父母、父母，及劉聰、石勒，不從此令。

summary.zh: 羯人石勒原為劉淵部將，319年在襄國自稱趙王（史稱後趙），減百姓田租一半，設立經學、律學、史學祭酒。329年滅前趙，330年稱帝。
summary.en: Shi Le, a Jie who had served Liu Yuan, proclaimed himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo in 319 (the Later Zhao), halved the land tax and appointed directors for the classics, law and history. He destroyed the Former Zhao in 329 and became emperor in 330.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零五 石勒載記下
passages.textZh: 勒偽稱趙王，赦殊死已下，均百姓田租之半，賜孝悌力田死義之孤帛各有差，孤老鰥寡谷人三石，大酺七日。

summary.zh: 永昌元年正月，大將軍王敦以誅劉隗為名在武昌起兵，攻入建康，殺戴淵、周顗等，元帝憂憤而死。324年王敦再次舉兵，病死軍中，叛亂平定。
summary.en: In the first month of 322 the General-in-Chief Wang Dun rose at Wuchang, ostensibly to punish Liu Wei, took Jiankang and killed Dai Yuan and Zhou Yi; Emperor Yuan died of grief. Wang Dun rose again in 324 and died of illness in camp, and the rising collapsed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷六 元帝紀
passages.textZh: 戊辰，大將軍王敦舉兵於武昌，以誅劉隗爲名，龍驤將軍沈充帥衆應之。

summary.zh: 咸和二年，庾亮執政，欲徵歷陽太守蘇峻入朝以奪其兵權。蘇峻聯合豫州刺史祖約起兵，次年攻陷建康，縱兵大掠。329年陶侃、溫嶠等聯軍平定叛亂。
summary.en: In 327 the regent Yu Liang tried to summon Su Jun, governor of Liyang, to court and strip him of his army. Su Jun rose with Zu Yue, governor of Yu, took Jiankang the next year and let his men sack it. Tao Kan and Wen Jiao put the rising down in 329.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷七 成帝紀
passages.textZh: 十一月，豫州刺史祖約、歷陽太守蘇峻等反。

summary.zh: 永和三年三月，荊州刺史桓溫率軍溯江入蜀，攻克成都，成漢主李勢投降，益州平定。桓溫由此威名大振。
summary.en: In the third month of 347 Huan Wen, governor of Jing, went up the Yangtze into Shu and took Chengdu; Li Shi of Cheng Han surrendered and Yi province was pacified. The victory made Huan Wen's name.

label.en: Huan Wen goes up the Yangtze

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八 穆帝紀
passages.textZh: 三年春三月乙卯，桓溫攻成都，克之。丁亥，李勢降，益州平。

confidenceNote.zh: 「死者二十餘萬」是《晉書》的記載，數字可能有誇大。
confidenceNote.en: "More than two hundred thousand dead" is the Book of Jin's figure and may be exaggerated.

summary.zh: 後趙末年大亂，漢人將領冉閔（石虎養孫）掌握鄴城，下令城內趙人斬一胡首送鳳陽門者，文官進位三等，武職悉拜牙門，一日之中斬首數萬，屠殺胡羯不分男女老少二十餘萬人。不久冉閔稱帝，國號魏。
summary.en: In the chaos at the end of the Later Zhao, the Han general Ran Min, adopted grandson of Shi Hu, held Ye. He announced that any "man of Zhao" who brought a barbarian's head to the Fengyang gate would be promoted three grades if an official, or made an officer if a soldier; tens of thousands were beheaded in a day, and more than two hundred thousand Hu and Jie — men, women and children — were killed. Ran Min soon declared himself emperor of Wei.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零七 石季龍載記下 附冉閔
passages.textZh: 閔知胡之不為己用也，班令內外趙人，斬一胡首送鳳陽門者，文官進位三等，武職悉拜牙門。一日之中，斬首數萬。閔躬率趙人誅諸胡羯，無貴賤男女少長皆斬之，死者二十餘萬

names.name: Fu Jian (the elder) takes the throne

summary.zh: 氐人苻洪死後，其子苻健率部西入關中，佔據長安，351年稱天王、大單于，352年在太極前殿即皇帝位，國號秦，史稱前秦。
summary.en: After the Di chief Fu Hong died, his son Fu Jian led his people west into the Guanzhong and took Chang'an, styling himself Heavenly King in 351 and taking the imperial throne in the Taiji hall in 352 — the Qin, known as the Former Qin.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十二 苻健載記
passages.textZh: 八年，健僭即皇帝位於太極前殿

confidenceNote.zh: 〈蘭亭集序〉真跡已不存，今傳摹本與刻本；1965年起曾有其真偽之爭。
confidenceNote.en: The original manuscript is lost; tracings and rubbings survive, and its authenticity was debated from 1965.

summary.zh: 永和九年三月初三，王羲之與謝安、孫綽等四十一人在會稽山陰蘭亭修禊，曲水流觴，飲酒賦詩，王羲之為詩集作序，即〈蘭亭集序〉，被後世尊為「天下第一行書」。
summary.en: On the third day of the third month of 353 Wang Xizhi, Xie An, Sun Chuo and others — forty-one in all — gathered at the Orchid Pavilion in Shanyin, Kuaiji, for the spring purification, floating wine cups down a winding stream and composing poems. Wang Xizhi wrote the preface to their collection, later revered as the finest running script ever written.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十 王羲之傳
passages.textZh: 永和九年，歲在癸丑，暮春之初，會於會稽山陰之蘭亭，修禊事也。群賢畢至，少長咸集。

summary.zh: 永和十年，桓溫率軍北伐前秦，進至長安東面的灞上，關中百姓牽牛擔酒迎於道旁，老人感泣說：「不圖今日復見官軍！」後因糧盡退兵。
summary.en: In 354 Huan Wen marched against the Former Qin and reached Bashang just east of Chang'an. People of the Guanzhong came out with oxen and wine to greet him, and old men wept: "We never thought to see the government's army again!" He withdrew when his supplies ran out.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 溫進至霸上，健以五千人深溝自固，居人皆安堵復業，持牛酒迎溫于路者十八九，耆老感泣曰：「不圖今日復見官軍！」

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 溫遂統步騎四萬發江陵，水軍自襄陽入均口。至南鄉，步自淅川以征關中，命梁州刺史司馬勳出子午道。
passages.textEn: Wen then set out from Jiangling with forty thousand foot and horse, his fleet entering Junkou from Xiangyang. At Nanxiang he left the boats and marched by Xichuan against Guanzhong, ordering Sima Xun, Inspector of Liang Province, out by the Ziwu road.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 溫進至霸上，健以五千人深溝自固，居人皆安堵復業，持牛酒迎溫于路者十八九
passages.textEn: Wen advanced to Bashang; Fu Jian dug in with five thousand men, and the local people went back to their work, eight or nine in ten coming out on the road with oxen and wine to welcome Wen

label.zh: 發江陵，水軍自襄陽入均口
label.en: From Jiangling by way of Xiangyang

label.zh: 步自淅川以征關中，進至霸上
label.en: On foot by Xichuan to Bashang
Sima Xun by the Ziwu road

summary.zh: 太和四年，桓溫第三次北伐前燕，進至枋頭。因袁真未能打通石門水道，軍糧耗盡，桓溫焚船步退，被慕容垂率八千騎追擊，在襄邑大敗，死者三萬人。
summary.en: In 369 Huan Wen marched a third time north, against the Former Yan, and reached Fangtou. Yuan Zhen failed to open the Shimen waterway, supplies ran out, and Huan Wen burned his boats and retreated on foot; Murong Chui pursued with eight thousand horsemen and routed him at Xiangyi, killing thirty thousand.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 溫焚舟步退，自東燕出倉垣，經陳留，鑿井而飲，行七百餘里。垂以八千騎追之，戰於襄邑，溫軍敗績，死者三萬人。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 溫擊破之，遂至枋頭。
passages.textEn: Wen routed them and reached Fangtou.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 乃鑿钜野三百餘里以通舟運，自清水入河。
passages.textEn: He cut a channel of over three hundred li at Juye to carry the boats, and entered the Yellow River from the Qing.

label.zh: 鑿钜野以通舟運，自清水入河，遂至枋頭
label.en: By canal from Juye to Fangtou

names.name: The Former Qin unites the north

summary.zh: 前秦天王苻堅任用王猛，370年滅前燕，373年取梁、益二州，376年派苟萇攻陷涼州俘張天錫、滅前涼，同年滅代，統一北方。
summary.en: Fu Jian, Heavenly King of the Former Qin, with Wang Meng as his minister, destroyed the Former Yan in 370, took Liang and Yi in 373, and in 376 sent Gou Chang to take Liangzhou, capturing Zhang Tianxi and ending the Former Liang; the same year he destroyed Dai. The north was united.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝武帝紀
passages.textZh: 秋七月，苻堅將苟萇陷涼州，虜刺史張天錫，盡有其地。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九 孝武帝紀
passages.textZh: 十一月，苻堅將楊安陷梓潼及梁、益二州，刺史周仲孫帥騎五千南遁。

summary.zh: 淝水之戰後前秦崩潰，鮮卑拓跋珪於登國元年正月在牛川即代王位，四月改稱魏王，398年遷都平城稱帝，史稱北魏。
summary.en: After Fei River the Former Qin fell apart. In the first month of 386 the Xianbei Tuoba Gui took the title King of Dai at Niuchuan, changing it to King of Wei in the fourth month; in 398 he moved to Pingcheng and became emperor — the Northern Wei.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀
passages.textZh: 登國元年春正月戊申，帝即代王位，郊天，建元，大會於牛川。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀
passages.textZh: 夏四月，改稱魏王。

summary.zh: 五斗米道首領孫恩從海島起事，隆安三年十一月攻陷會稽，殺內史王凝之，東南八郡響應，前後轉戰數年。402年兵敗投海自盡，餘眾由盧循率領。劉裕在鎮壓孫恩的戰爭中嶄露頭角。
summary.en: Sun En, a leader of the Five Pecks of Rice sect, came ashore from the islands and in the eleventh month of 399 took Kuaiji and killed its governor Wang Ningzhi; eight southeastern commanderies rose with him and the fighting went on for years. Beaten in 402, he drowned himself, and Lu Xun led the remnants. Liu Yu made his name fighting him.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷十 安帝紀
passages.textZh: 十一月甲寅，妖賊孫恩陷會稽，內史王凝之死之，吳國內史桓謙、臨海太守新蔡王崇、義興太守魏隱並委官而遁，吳興太守謝邈、永嘉太守司馬逸皆遇害。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷十 安帝紀
passages.textZh: 輔國司馬劉裕破恩於南山。

summary.zh: 桓溫之子桓玄據有荊、江，402年攻入建康，殺司馬元顯，自任丞相、太尉。元興二年十二月，桓玄逼晉安帝禪位，在建康城南登壇稱帝，國號楚。404年劉裕在京口起兵討伐，桓玄兵敗被殺。
summary.en: Huan Wen's son Huan Xuan held Jing and Jiang, took Jiankang in 402 and killed the regent Sima Yuanxian. In the twelfth month of 403 he forced Emperor An to abdicate and mounted an altar south of the city as emperor of Chu. In 404 Liu Yu rose against him at Jingkou; Huan Xuan was beaten and killed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十九 桓玄傳
passages.textZh: 玄乃于城南七里立郊，登壇篡位，以玄牡告天，百僚陪列，而儀注不備，忘稱萬歲

names.name: Liu Yu destroys the Southern Yan

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 南燕主慕容超屢次侵掠淮北。義熙五年劉裕北伐，南燕不守大峴山之險，劉裕越過大峴時舉手指天說：「吾事濟矣！」隨後在臨朐大敗燕軍，圍廣固，410年二月破城，擒慕容超送建康斬首，南燕亡。
summary.en: Murong Chao of the Southern Yan kept raiding north of the Huai. In 409 Liu Yu marched north; the Yan failed to hold the Daxian pass, and as he crossed it Liu Yu pointed to the sky and said, "Our cause will prevail!" He crushed the Yan army at Linqu, besieged Guanggu, took it in the second month of 410 and sent Murong Chao to Jiankang to be beheaded. The Southern Yan was over.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 初偽燕王鮮卑慕容德僭號於青州，德死，兄子超襲位，前後屢為邊患。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 公既入峴，舉手指天曰：「吾事濟矣！」

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 三月，公抗表北討，以丹陽尹孟昶監中軍留府事。四月，舟師發京都，泝淮入泗。五月，至下邳，留船艦輜重，步軍進琅邪。所過皆築城留守。鮮卑梁父、莒城二戍並奔走。
passages.textEn: In the third month the Duke sent up a memorial for the northern campaign, leaving Meng Chang in charge at home. In the fourth month the fleet left the capital and went up the Huai into the Si. In the fifth month at Xiapi he left the ships and baggage and marched on foot into Langye, building forts and leaving garrisons wherever he went; the Xianbei garrisons of Liangfu and Ju fled.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 眾軍步進，有車四千兩，分車為兩翼，方軌徐行，車悉張幔，御者執矟。又以輕騎為遊軍。
passages.textEn: The army advanced on foot with four thousand carts split into two wings, moving slowly side by side, every cart hung with curtains and its driver holding a lance, with light horse as a flying column.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 日向昃，公遣諮議參軍檀韶直趨臨朐。詔率建威將軍向彌、參軍胡藩馳往，即日陷城，斬其牙旗，悉虜超輜重。超聞臨朐已拔，引眾走，公親鼓之，賊乃大奔。超遁還廣固。
passages.textEn: As the sun went down the Duke sent Tan Shao straight at Linqu; with Xiang Mi and Hu Fan he rode in, took the town that day, cut down Murong Chao's standard and captured all his baggage. Hearing that Linqu had fallen, Chao pulled back; the Duke beat the drum himself and the enemy fled in rout, Chao back to Guanggu.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 明日，大軍進廣固，即屠大城，超退保小城。於是設長圍守之，圍高三丈，外穿三重塹。
passages.textEn: The next day the army came to Guanggu and stormed the outer city; Chao fell back into the inner city, which the Duke ringed with a wall three zhang high and three ditches beyond it.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷一 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 六年二月丁亥，屠廣固。超踰城走，征虜賊曹喬胥獲之，殺其王公以下，納口萬餘，馬二千疋，送超京師，斬于建康市。
passages.textEn: On dinghai of the second month of the sixth year Guanggu was stormed. Murong Chao went over the wall and fled, and was caught by Qiao Xu; his princes and officials were killed, over ten thousand people and two thousand horses were taken, and Chao was sent to the capital and beheaded in the market of Jiankang.

label.zh: 舟師發京都，泝淮入泗，至下邳
label.en: By boat from the capital to Xiapi

label.zh: 留船艦輜重，步軍進琅邪
檀韶直趨臨朐，即日陷城
大軍進廣固…六年二月屠廣固
label.en: The siege and fall of Guanggu

summary.zh: 永初元年六月，晉恭帝禪位，劉裕在建康南郊即皇帝位，國號宋，東晉滅亡，南朝開始。次年劉裕派人殺死恭帝。
summary.en: In the sixth month of 420 Emperor Gong of Jin abdicated and Liu Yu took the throne at the southern suburb of Jiankang as emperor of Song. The Eastern Jin was over and the Southern Dynasties began. The next year Liu Yu had the former emperor killed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷三 武帝紀下
passages.textZh: 永初元年夏六月丁卯，設壇於南郊，即皇帝位，柴燎告天。

summary.zh: 太平真君五年正月，北魏太武帝下詔：王公以下至庶人家中私養沙門、師巫者，限期送交官府，過期不出，沙門處死，主人滿門抄斬。446年太武帝在崔浩鼓動下進一步下令誅殺沙門、焚毀佛像經卷，是「三武一宗滅佛」的第一次。
summary.en: In the first month of 444 Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei decreed that anyone, prince or commoner, who kept monks or shamans in his household must hand them over by a deadline; after it, the monks would die and the householder's family with them. In 446, urged on by Cui Hao, he ordered monks killed and images and scriptures burned — the first of the four great persecutions of Buddhism.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四下 世祖紀下
passages.textZh: 自王公已下至於庶人，有私養沙門、師巫及金銀工巧之人在其家者，皆遣詣官曹，不得容匿。限今年二月十五日，過期不出，師巫、沙門身死，主人門誅。

names.name: Cui Hao and the state history

confidenceNote.zh: 崔浩被殺的真正原因史家說法不一，「國史之獄」之外還有漢族士族與鮮卑貴族的矛盾等解釋。
confidenceNote.en: Historians disagree on why Cui Hao was really killed; besides the history affair, tension between Han gentry and Xianbei nobles is often cited.

summary.zh: 司徒崔浩奉命修北魏國史，將拓跋氏早期史事直書並刻石立於通衢，觸怒鮮卑貴族。太平真君十一年六月，崔浩被誅，清河崔氏不論遠近，及其姻親范陽盧氏、太原郭氏、河東柳氏皆被滅族。
summary.en: The minister Cui Hao, ordered to write the history of the Wei, recorded the Tuoba clan's early history plainly and had it carved on steles beside the highway, enraging the Xianbei nobility. In the sixth month of 450 he was executed, and the Cui of Qinghe, near and distant, with their in-laws the Lu of Fanyang, the Guo of Taiyuan and the Liu of Hedong, were wiped out.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷三十五 崔浩傳
passages.textZh: 真君十一年六月誅浩，清河崔氏無遠近，范陽盧氏、太原郭氏、河東柳氏，皆浩之姻親，盡夷其族。

summary.zh: 劉宋末年皇室自相殘殺，大將蕭道成掌權。建元元年四月，宋順帝禪位，蕭道成即皇帝位於建康南郊，國號齊，史稱南齊。
summary.en: The Liu Song imperial house slaughtered itself, and the general Xiao Daocheng took control. In the fourth month of 479 Emperor Shun of Song abdicated and Xiao Daocheng took the throne at the southern suburb of Jiankang as emperor of Qi — the Southern Qi.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Southern Qi (Xiao Zixian, 537)
passages.locator: 卷二 高帝紀下
passages.textZh: 建元元年夏四月甲午，上即皇帝位於南郊，設壇柴燎告天

summary.zh: 太和九年十月，北魏孝文帝（實由馮太后主政）下詔派使者巡行州郡，與地方官一起「均給天下之田」，按人口授田，人死還田。均田制此後為北齊、北周、隋、唐沿用約三百年。
summary.en: In the tenth month of 485 Emperor Xiaowen of the Northern Wei (in practice the Empress Dowager Feng) sent commissioners through the provinces to "distribute the land of the realm equally" with the local governors, allotting fields by head and taking them back at death. The equal-field system was kept by the Northern Qi, Northern Zhou, Sui and Tang for some three hundred years.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷七上 高祖紀上
passages.textZh: 今遣使者，循行州郡，與牧守均給天下之田，還受以生死為斷

summary.zh: 遷都洛陽後，孝文帝推行漢化：禁胡服、斷北語，太和二十年正月下詔改皇族拓跋氏為元氏，其他鮮卑貴族也改為單字漢姓，並與漢族士族通婚。
summary.en: After the move to Luoyang Emperor Xiaowen pressed on with sinicisation: Xianbei dress and speech were banned at court, and in the first month of 496 the imperial Tuoba clan was renamed Yuan; other Xianbei nobles took one-character Chinese surnames and married into the Han gentry.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷七下 高祖紀下
passages.textZh: 二十年春正月丁卯，詔改姓為元氏。

summary.zh: 南齊東昏侯殘暴，雍州刺史蕭衍自襄陽起兵攻入建康。天監元年四月，齊和帝禪位，蕭衍即皇帝位於南郊，國號梁，是為梁武帝，在位四十八年。
summary.en: The Southern Qi's Marquis of Donghun was a tyrant; Xiao Yan, governor of Yong, marched from Xiangyang and took Jiankang. In the fourth month of 502 Emperor He of Qi abdicated and Xiao Yan took the throne at the southern suburb as emperor of Liang — Emperor Wu, who reigned forty-eight years.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Liang (Yao Silian, 636)
passages.locator: 卷二 武帝紀中
passages.textZh: 天監元年夏四月丙寅，高祖卽皇帝位於南郊。

names.name: Emperor Wu of Liang gives himself to the Tongtai temple

summary.zh: 大通元年三月，篤信佛教的梁武帝到同泰寺「捨身」為寺奴，三日後還宮，大赦改元。此後他又三次捨身，每次都由群臣以巨款向寺院「贖回」。
summary.en: In the third month of 527 Emperor Wu of Liang, a devout Buddhist, "gave himself" to the Tongtai temple as its servant, returning to the palace three days later with an amnesty and a new era name. He did so three more times, and each time his ministers "ransomed" him from the temple with vast sums.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Liang (Yao Silian, 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 武帝紀下
passages.textZh: 三月辛未，輿駕幸同泰寺捨身。甲戌，還宮，赦天下，改元。

names.name: Gao Yang founds the Northern Qi

summary.zh: 高歡之子高洋承襲東魏大權，武定八年五月逼東魏孝靜帝禪位，在鄴城南郊即皇帝位，國號齊，史稱北齊。
summary.en: Gao Huan's son Gao Yang inherited control of the Eastern Wei, forced Emperor Xiaojing to abdicate in the fifth month of 550, and took the throne at the southern suburb of Ye as emperor of Qi — the Northern Qi.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Northern Qi (Li Baiyao, 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 文宣帝紀
passages.textZh: 戊午，乃即皇帝位於南郊，升壇柴燎告天

names.name: Yuwen Jue founds the Northern Zhou

summary.zh: 宇文泰死後，其姪宇文護輔政，逼西魏恭帝禪位於宇文泰之子宇文覺。557年正月宇文覺即天王位，國號周，史稱北周。
summary.en: After Yuwen Tai died his nephew Yuwen Hu forced Emperor Gong of the Western Wei to abdicate to Yuwen Tai's son Yuwen Jue, who took the title Heavenly King in the first month of 557 — the Zhou, known as the Northern Zhou.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 孝閔帝紀
passages.textZh: 元年春正月辛丑，即天王位。柴燎告天，朝百官於路門。

summary.zh: 侯景之亂與江陵陷落後，陳霸先平定建康一帶。永定元年十月，梁敬帝禪位，陳霸先即皇帝位於南郊，國號陳。
summary.en: After Hou Jing's rebellion and the fall of Jiangling, Chen Baxian restored order around Jiankang. In the tenth month of 557 Emperor Jing of Liang abdicated and Chen Baxian took the throne at the southern suburb as emperor of Chen.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Chen (Yao Silian, 636)
passages.locator: 卷二 高祖紀下
passages.textZh: 永定元年冬十月乙亥，高祖即皇帝位于南郊

names.name: Emperor Wu of Zhou bans Buddhism and Daoism

summary.zh: 建德三年五月，北周武帝宇文邕下詔禁斷佛、道二教，毀壞經像，令沙門、道士還俗為民，寺院財產沒收充軍國之用。這是「三武一宗滅佛」的第二次。
summary.en: In the fifth month of 574 Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou, Yuwen Yong, banned Buddhism and Daoism, destroyed their scriptures and images and sent monks and Daoist priests back to lay life; temple property went to the state and army. It was the second of the four great persecutions of Buddhism.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Zhou (Linghu Defen et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷五 武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 丙子，初斷佛、道二教，經像悉毀，罷沙門、道士，並令還民。

summary.zh: 名司馬炎，字安世，司馬昭長子。266年代魏建晉，280年滅吳統一全國，頒行占田制。晚年怠於政事，立愚弱的司馬衷為太子，又大封宗室諸王並授以兵權，為八王之亂埋下禍根。
summary.en: Sima Yan, courtesy name Anshi, eldest son of Sima Zhao. He replaced the Wei with the Jin in 266, conquered Wu in 280 to reunite China and issued the land-allotment law. In his later years he neglected government, kept his simple-minded son as heir and gave the imperial princes great fiefs with armies — sowing the War of the Eight Princes.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷三 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。

summary.zh: 字世龍，上黨武鄉的羯人，少年時曾被販賣為奴。依附劉淵後屢立戰功，319年自立為趙王，329年滅前趙，統一北方大部分地區，330年稱帝。雖不識字，卻喜歡讓人讀史書給他聽。
summary.en: Courtesy name Shilong, a Jie of Wuxiang in Shangdang, sold as a slave in his youth. He won fame fighting for Liu Yuan, proclaimed himself King of Zhao in 319, destroyed the Former Zhao in 329 to rule most of the north, and became emperor in 330. Illiterate, he loved to have the histories read to him.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百零四 石勒載記上
passages.textZh: 石勒字世龍，初名㔨，上黨武鄉羯人也。其先匈奴別部羌渠之胄。

summary.zh: 字元子，東晉權臣、名將。347年滅成漢，354年、356年、369年三次北伐，曾收復洛陽，枋頭大敗後聲望受挫。晚年廢晉帝司馬奕，立簡文帝，謀求禪代未成而死。
summary.en: Courtesy name Yuanzi, general and strongman of the Eastern Jin. He conquered Cheng Han in 347 and marched north in 354, 356 and 369, once retaking Luoyang, until the disaster at Fangtou dented his prestige. Late in life he deposed Emperor Sima Yi and set up Emperor Jianwen, and died before he could take the throne himself.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十八 桓溫傳
passages.textZh: 桓溫，字元子，宣城太守彝之子也。

confidenceNote.en: Dates vary between sources: 303–361 and 321–379 are both proposed.

summary.zh: 字逸少，琅邪臨沂人，王導之姪，官至右軍將軍、會稽內史，世稱「王右軍」。書法兼善隸、草、楷、行各體，被尊為「書聖」，代表作〈蘭亭集序〉。
summary.en: Courtesy name Yishao, of Linyi in Langya, Wang Dao's nephew, General of the Right and governor of Kuaiji. Master of clerical, cursive, standard and running scripts, he is revered as the "Sage of Calligraphy"; his best-known work is the Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Poems.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十 王羲之傳
passages.textZh: 王羲之，字逸少，司徒導之從子也。

summary.zh: 字景略，北海劇縣人，出身寒微，以賣畚箕為生。受苻堅重用為丞相，整頓吏治、抑制豪強，使前秦國富兵強，370年率軍滅前燕。臨終勸苻堅不要攻打東晉，苻堅不聽，終有淝水之敗。
summary.en: Courtesy name Jinglüe, of Ju in Beihai, a man of humble birth who once sold baskets. Fu Jian made him chancellor; he cleaned up the administration, curbed the great families and made the Former Qin rich and strong, and destroyed the Former Yan in 370. On his deathbed he urged Fu Jian not to attack the Eastern Jin — advice ignored before the defeat at Fei River.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十四 苻堅載記下
passages.textZh: 王景略一時奇士，陛下每擬之孔明，其臨終之言不可忘也。

confidenceNote.zh: 《晉書》稱他為天竺人，指其父籍；他本人生於龜茲。生卒年另有350–409之說。
confidenceNote.en: The Book of Jin calls him Indian after his father; he was born in Kucha. Some date him 350–409.

summary.zh: 父親是天竺人，母親是龜茲公主，生於龜茲。前秦大將呂光破龜茲後將他帶到涼州，401年後秦姚興迎入長安，主持譯場，譯出《金剛經》《法華經》《大智度論》等三百餘卷，是中國佛經翻譯史上最重要的譯師之一。
summary.en: Born in Kucha to an Indian father and a Kuchean princess. The Former Qin general Lü Guang carried him off to Liangzhou after taking Kucha; in 401 Yao Xing of the Later Qin brought him to Chang'an, where he led a translation bureau that rendered the Diamond Sutra, the Lotus Sutra, the Great Treatise on the Perfection of Wisdom and some three hundred fascicles in all — one of the greatest translators of Buddhist scripture into Chinese.

label.en: Taken by Lü Guang to Liangzhou

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷九十五 藝術傳 鳩摩羅什
passages.textZh: 鳩摩羅什，天竺人也。

confidenceNote.zh: 卒年有343、363等說法。
confidenceNote.en: His death is dated variously to 343 or 363.

summary.zh: 字稚川，丹陽句容人，自號抱朴子，東晉道教理論家、醫藥學家、煉丹家。著《抱朴子》內外篇，《肘後備急方》中記載以青蒿汁治瘧，啟發了現代青蒿素的發現。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zhichuan, of Jurong in Danyang, self-styled Baopuzi — Daoist theorist, physician and alchemist of the Eastern Jin. He wrote the Baopuzi; his handbook of emergency prescriptions records treating malaria with the juice of sweet wormwood, which inspired the modern discovery of artemisinin.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷七十二 葛洪傳
passages.textZh: 葛洪，字稚川，丹陽句容人也。

confidenceNote.en: His birth year is also given as 352, 372 or 376.

summary.zh: 名潛，字淵明（一說字元亮），尋陽柴桑人，東晉名將陶侃的曾孫。曾任彭澤令八十餘日，「不能為五斗米折腰」，辭官歸隱田園，作〈歸去來兮辭〉〈桃花源記〉及大量田園詩，被稱為「田園詩人之宗」。
summary.en: Tao Qian, courtesy name Yuanming (or Yuanliang), of Chaisang in Xunyang, great-grandson of the Eastern Jin general Tao Kan. After some eighty days as magistrate of Pengze, unwilling to "bow for five pecks of rice", he resigned to farm, writing "The Return", "Peach Blossom Spring" and many poems of country life — the father of Chinese pastoral poetry.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷九十三 隱逸傳 陶潛
passages.textZh: 陶潛字淵明，或云淵明字元亮，尋陽柴桑人也。曾祖侃，晉大司馬。

summary.zh: 字伯淵，清河人，北魏太武帝的重臣，精通天文曆算，參與謀劃滅夏、滅北涼等戰爭，主張排佛。因主修國史觸怒鮮卑貴族，450年被誅，其家族及姻親被滅族。
summary.en: Courtesy name Boyuan, of Qinghe, chief adviser to Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei, versed in astronomy and calendrics; he helped plan the conquests of Xia and the Northern Liang and urged the suppression of Buddhism. His state history offended the Xianbei nobility, and in 450 he was executed and his family and in-laws exterminated.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷三十五 崔浩傳
passages.textZh: 崔浩，字伯淵，清河人也，白馬公玄伯之長子。
