confidenceNote.zh: 圓周率的數值見於《隋書·律曆志》，〈祖沖之傳〉未載。
confidenceNote.en: The value of π is recorded in the Book of Sui's calendar treatise, not in this biography.

summary.zh: 字文遠，范陽薊人，南朝宋、齊的數學家、天文學家。將圓周率精確推算到3.1415926與3.1415927之間，此紀錄保持近千年；又製《大明曆》，首次將歲差引入曆法。
summary.en: Courtesy name Wenyuan, of Ji in Fanyang, mathematician and astronomer of the Song and Qi. He fixed π between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, a record that stood for nearly a thousand years, and his Daming calendar was the first to take the precession of the equinoxes into account.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Southern Qi (Xiao Zixian, 537)
passages.locator: 卷五十二 文學傳 祖沖之
passages.textZh: 祖沖之字文遠，范陽薊人也。

confidenceNote.zh: 生卒年為約數。
confidenceNote.en: Dates approximate.

summary.zh: 字子真，南鄉舞陰人，南朝齊、梁的思想家。在竟陵王蕭子良門下反對因果報應之說，著〈神滅論〉，主張「形存則神存，形謝則神滅」，梁武帝曾發動數十人與他辯論。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zizhen, of Wuyin in Nanxiang, thinker of the Qi and Liang. At the court of Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, he rejected karmic retribution and wrote "On the Mortality of the Soul": "while the body lives the spirit lives; when the body decays the spirit perishes". Emperor Wu of Liang set dozens of scholars to argue against him.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Liang (Yao Silian, 636)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 儒林傳 范縝
passages.textZh: 范縝字子真，南鄉舞陰人也。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Liang (Yao Silian, 636)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 儒林傳 范縝
passages.textZh: 神卽形也，形卽神也；是以形存則神存，形謝則神滅

summary.zh: 字通明，丹陽秣陵人，南朝齊、梁的道士與醫藥學家，隱居茅山，整理上清派經典，撰《本草經集注》。梁武帝遇國家大事常派人入山諮詢，時人稱他為「山中宰相」。
summary.en: Courtesy name Tongming, of Moling in Danyang, Daoist master and pharmacologist of the Qi and Liang. Living as a hermit on Mount Mao, he edited the Shangqing scriptures and wrote the Collected Commentaries on the Materia Medica. Emperor Wu of Liang sent to consult him on affairs of state, so people called him "the chancellor in the mountains".

passages.sourceEn: Book of Liang (Yao Silian, 636)
passages.locator: 卷五十一 處士傳 陶弘景
passages.textZh: 陶弘景字通明，丹陽秣陵人也。

confidenceNote.en: He died in 262 or 263.

summary.zh: 字叔夜，譙國銍人，曹魏宗室的女婿，與阮籍、山濤、向秀、劉伶、阮咸、王戎同遊竹林，世稱「竹林七賢」。崇尚老莊，拒絕與司馬氏合作，被鍾會構陷處死，臨刑前彈奏〈廣陵散〉。
summary.en: Courtesy name Shuye, of Zhi in Qiao, married into the Cao imperial family. With Ruan Ji, Shan Tao, Xiang Xiu, Liu Ling, Ruan Xian and Wang Rong he roamed the bamboo grove — the "Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove". A follower of Laozi and Zhuangzi, he refused to serve the Sima, was framed by Zhong Hui and executed, playing "Guangling san" on the zither before he died.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷四十九 嵇康傳
passages.textZh: 嵇康，字叔夜，譙國銍人也。

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷四十九 嵇康傳
passages.textZh: 所與神交者惟陳留阮籍、河内山濤，豫其流者河内向秀、沛國劉伶、籍兄子咸、琅邪王戎，遂爲竹林之遊，世所謂「竹林七賢」

summary.zh: 北周外戚、大丞相楊堅總攬朝政，平定尉遲迥等人的反抗後，於開皇元年二月受北周靜帝禪讓，在長安臨光殿即皇帝位，國號隋，改元開皇。
summary.en: Yang Jian, father-in-law of the Northern Zhou emperor and its chancellor, crushed the resistance of Yuchi Jiong and others and in the second month of 581 accepted the abdication of Emperor Jing, taking the throne in the Linguang hall at Chang'an as emperor of Sui with the era Kaihuang.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷一 高祖紀上
passages.textZh: 開皇元年二月甲子，上自相府常服入宮，備禮即皇帝位於臨光殿。

summary.zh: 漢長安舊城狹小殘破，開皇二年六月，隋文帝命左僕射高熲、將作大匠劉龍等在舊城東南的龍首原營建新都，由宇文愷規劃，九個月即建成，次年遷入，命名大興城。唐代改稱長安，沿用三百年。
summary.en: Old Han Chang'an was cramped and decayed. In the sixth month of 582 Emperor Wen ordered the chancellor Gao Jiong, the Chief Architect Liu Long and others to build a new capital on the Longshou plain to the southeast, laid out by Yuwen Kai; it was finished in nine months and occupied the next year as Daxing. The Tang renamed it Chang'an and ruled from it for three hundred years.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷一 高祖紀上
passages.textZh: 左僕射高熲、將作大匠劉龍、鉅鹿郡公賀婁子幹、太府少卿高龍叉等創造新都。

summary.zh: 仁壽四年七月，隋文帝死於仁壽宮，太子楊廣即位，是為隋煬帝。漢王楊諒在并州起兵反對，被楊素平定。
summary.en: In the seventh month of 604 Emperor Wen died at the Renshou palace and the crown prince Yang Guang took the throne — Emperor Yang. His brother Yang Liang, Prince of Han, rose against him at Bingzhou and was put down by Yang Su.

question.en: Did Yang Guang kill his father?

claim.zh: 本紀只記文帝崩、太子即位，未言死因。
claim.en: The annals say only that Emperor Wen died and the heir succeeded, with no cause of death.

source.en: Book of Sui 3: Annals of Emperor Yang

accounts.quoteZh: 四年七月，高祖崩，上即皇帝位於仁壽宮。

claim.zh: 〈后妃傳〉及唐人筆記記楊廣調戲宣華夫人、文帝欲廢太子而突然死去，後世由此有弒父之說。
claim.en: The consorts' biographies and Tang anecdotes tell of Yang Guang molesting Lady Xuanhua and of the emperor dying suddenly as he moved to depose him, whence the story of parricide.

source.en: Book of Sui, consorts' biographies; Tang anecdotes

note.zh: 此說無法確證，引文尚未錄入。
note.en: It cannot be proved; that text has not been quoted here yet.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 煬帝紀上
passages.textZh: 四年七月，高祖崩，上即皇帝位於仁壽宮。

names.name: Building the Eastern Capital at Luoyang

summary.zh: 隋煬帝即位後下詔在伊水、洛水之間營建東京（東都洛陽），每月役使民夫二百萬人，次年建成，同時遷入大批富商大賈。
summary.en: Soon after his accession Emperor Yang ordered an Eastern Capital built between the Yi and Luo rivers at Luoyang; two million labourers worked on it each month, it was finished the following year, and wealthy merchants were moved in to fill it.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 煬帝紀上
passages.textZh: 今可於伊、洛營建東京，便即設官分職，以為民極也。

summary.zh: 大業四年正月，隋煬帝徵發河北諸郡男女百餘萬人開鑿永濟渠，引沁水南通黃河，北通涿郡（今北京一帶），為征伐高句麗運送兵員糧草。與通濟渠、邗溝、江南河共同構成隋朝大運河。
summary.en: In the first month of 608 Emperor Yang conscripted more than a million men and women of the northern commanderies to dig the Yongji canal, leading the Qin river south to the Yellow River and north to Zhuo commandery (near modern Beijing), to carry troops and grain for his wars on Goguryeo. With the Tongji canal, the Han channel and the Jiangnan canal it made up the Sui Grand Canal.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 煬帝紀上
passages.textZh: 四年春正月乙巳，詔發河北諸郡男女百餘萬開永濟渠，引沁水南達于河，北通涿郡。

summary.zh: 隋煬帝第二次親征高句麗時，在黎陽督運糧草的禮部尚書楊玄感（楊素之子）起兵反隋，進逼東都洛陽。煬帝急忙撤軍回救，楊玄感兵敗自殺。這是隋朝統治集團內部的第一次大分裂。
summary.en: During Emperor Yang's second campaign against Goguryeo, Yang Xuangan, Minister of Rites and son of Yang Su, who was overseeing supplies at Liyang, rose against the Sui and advanced on Luoyang. The emperor broke off the campaign to save the capital; Yang Xuangan was beaten and killed himself. It was the first great split inside the Sui ruling class.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 煬帝紀下
passages.textZh: 六月乙巳，禮部尚書楊玄感反於黎陽。丙辰，玄感逼東都。

summary.zh: 大業十一年八月，隋煬帝北巡，東突厥始畢可汗率數十萬騎謀襲，煬帝逃入雁門城，被突厥包圍，官軍屢戰不利，煬帝驚恐抱著幼子痛哭。各地援軍趕到後突厥才退去。
summary.en: In the eighth month of 615, on a northern tour, Emperor Yang was nearly ambushed by the Eastern Turkic Shibi Qaghan with hundreds of thousands of horsemen. He fled into Yanmen and was besieged; his troops lost every sally and the terrified emperor wept holding his young son. The Turks withdrew only when relief armies arrived.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 煬帝紀下
passages.textZh: 壬申，車駕馳幸雁門。癸酉，突厥圍城，官軍頻戰不利。

names.name: Li Mi seizes the Xingluo granary

summary.zh: 瓦崗軍首領翟讓推李密為主，大業十三年二月攻陷洛陽附近的興洛倉（洛口倉），開倉放糧，百姓歸附者數十萬，李密自稱魏公，成為隋末最強大的反隋勢力之一。
summary.en: Zhai Rang, leader of the Wagang rebels, made Li Mi his chief. In the second month of 617 they took the Xingluo (Luokou) granary near Luoyang and opened it to the people; hundreds of thousands joined them, and Li Mi, styling himself Duke of Wei, became one of the strongest rebel powers at the end of the Sui.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 煬帝紀下
passages.textZh: 庚寅，賊帥李密、翟讓等陷興洛倉。越王侗遣武賁郎將劉長恭、光祿少卿房崱擊之，反為所敗，死者十五六。

summary.zh: 大業十三年，天下大亂，太原留守李淵在李世民與晉陽令劉文靜的勸說下起兵，五月誅殺副留守王威、高君雅，七月率軍南下，十一月攻入長安，立代王楊侑為帝，次年代隋建唐。
summary.en: In 617, with the empire in chaos, Li Yuan, regent of Taiyuan, was urged by his son Li Shimin and Liu Wenjing, magistrate of Jinyang, to rise. In the fifth month he killed his deputies Wang Wei and Gao Junya, in the seventh marched south, in the eleventh took Chang'an and set up the Prince of Dai Yang You as emperor; the next year he replaced the Sui with the Tang.

label.en: Li Yuan marches south to Chang'an

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一 高祖紀
passages.textZh: 太宗與晉陽令劉文靜首謀，勸舉義兵。

summary.zh: 名楊廣，隋文帝次子。滅陳時任行軍元帥，後奪得太子之位。即位後營建東都、開鑿大運河、三征高句麗，徭役繁重，激起全國反抗。618年在江都被宇文化及等縊殺。「煬」是唐朝所加的惡諡。
summary.en: Yang Guang, Emperor Wen's second son, commander-in-chief of the conquest of Chen, who later supplanted his elder brother as heir. As emperor he built the Eastern Capital, dug the Grand Canal and invaded Goguryeo three times; the crushing labour and levies set the whole empire ablaze. In 618 Yuwen Huaji and others strangled him at Jiangdu. "Yang" is the damning posthumous name the Tang gave him.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 煬帝紀上
passages.textZh: 煬皇帝諱廣，一名英，小字阿𡡉，高祖第二子也。

summary.zh: 字昭玄，隋文帝的首席宰相，執政近二十年，主持營建大興城、制定律令，平陳時任元帥長史。因反對廢太子楊勇而被罷免，煬帝時因議論朝政被殺。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zhaoxuan, Emperor Wen's chief minister for nearly twenty years, who oversaw the building of Daxing and the drafting of the laws, and was chief of staff in the conquest of Chen. Dismissed for opposing the removal of the heir Yang Yong, he was executed under Emperor Yang for criticising the government.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 高熲傳
passages.textZh: 高熲，字昭玄，一名敏，自雲渤海蓚人也。

summary.zh: 字安樂，隋代建築家。出身武將世家而獨好讀書，規劃設計大興城與東都洛陽，又主持開鑿廣通渠，曾為煬帝造可容數百人的觀風行殿。
summary.en: Courtesy name Anle, architect of the Sui. Born into a family of soldiers, he alone loved books; he planned Daxing and the Eastern Capital at Luoyang, oversaw the Guangtong canal, and built Emperor Yang a movable hall that held several hundred people.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷六十八 宇文愷傳
passages.textZh: 宇文愷，字安樂，杞國公忻之弟也。

summary.zh: 字法主，北周八柱國李弼的曾孫。曾參與楊玄感起兵，失敗後投奔瓦崗軍，被推為首領，號魏公，與王世充在洛陽一帶反覆激戰。618年兵敗降唐，次年叛唐被殺。
summary.en: Courtesy name Fazhu, great-grandson of Li Bi, one of the Eight Pillars of the Northern Zhou. He joined Yang Xuangan's rising and after its failure went over to the Wagang rebels, who made him their leader as Duke of Wei; he fought Wang Shichong around Luoyang again and again. Beaten in 618, he surrendered to the Tang, rebelled the next year and was killed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷七十 李密傳
passages.textZh: 李密字法主，真鄉公衍之從孫也。

summary.zh: 後梁太祖朱溫病重，打算傳位給養子朱友文。乾化二年六月，郢王朱友珪率兵入宮殺死朱溫，矯詔殺朱友文，自立為帝。次年其弟均王朱友貞起兵殺朱友珪，即位為梁末帝。
summary.en: As Zhu Wen, founder of the Later Liang, lay dying he meant to leave the throne to his adopted son Zhu Youwen. In the sixth month of 912 his son Zhu Yougui, Prince of Ying, broke into the palace with troops, killed his father, had Youwen killed on a forged order and made himself emperor. The next year his brother Zhu Youzhen, Prince of Jun, rose, killed him and took the throne as the last Liang emperor.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷二 梁本紀 太祖下
passages.textZh: 六月，疾革，郢王友珪反。

summary.zh: 神冊元年二月，契丹迭剌部首領耶律阿保機接受群臣與各屬國所上尊號「大聖大明天皇帝」，建元神冊，正式建立契丹國家（947年改國號遼）。
summary.en: In the second month of 916 Abaoji, chief of the Yila tribe of the Khitan, accepted from his officials and subject peoples the title "Great Sage, Great Bright Heavenly Emperor" and the era Shence, founding the Khitan state (renamed Liao in 947).

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀上
passages.textZh: 丙申，群臣及諸屬國築壇州東，上尊號曰大聖大明天皇帝，后曰應天大明地皇后。大赦，建元神冊。

names.name: Li Cunxu takes the throne and destroys the Liang

summary.zh: 沙陀人晉王李存勗與後梁夾河鏖戰十餘年。同光元年四月在魏州即皇帝位，國號唐（後唐）；十月奇兵渡河直取汴州，梁末帝自殺，後梁滅亡。
summary.en: Li Cunxu, the Shatuo Prince of Jin, had fought the Later Liang along the Yellow River for more than ten years. In the fourth month of 923 he took the throne at Weizhou as emperor of Tang (the Later Tang); in the tenth month he crossed the river in a surprise march on Bianzhou, the last Liang emperor killed himself, and the Later Liang was over.

label.en: The Later Tang strikes at Bianzhou

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷五 唐本紀 莊宗下
passages.textZh: 夏四月己巳，皇帝即位，大赦，改元，國號唐。

names.name: The Later Tang conquers the Former Shu

summary.zh: 同光三年九月，後唐派魏王李繼岌與郭崇韜率軍伐蜀，七十日而至成都，十一月前蜀後主王衍出降，前蜀滅亡。次年王衍在押往洛陽途中被殺。
summary.en: In the ninth month of 925 the Later Tang sent Li Jiji, Prince of Wei, and Guo Chongtao against Shu; they reached Chengdu in seventy days, and in the eleventh month Wang Yan, last ruler of the Former Shu, surrendered. He was killed the next year on the road to Luoyang.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷五 唐本紀 莊宗下
passages.textZh: 己酉，王衍降。

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 唐書 莊宗紀七
passages.textZh: 時王衍將幸秦州，以其軍五萬屯於利州。聞我師至，遣步騎三萬逆戰於三泉，延孝與李嚴以勁騎三千擊之，蜀軍大敗，斬首五千級，餘眾奔潰。王衍聞敗，自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津，浮梁而去。
passages.textEn: Wang Yan was about to visit Qinzhou and had fifty thousand men camped at Lizhou. Hearing our army was coming, he sent thirty thousand foot and horse to meet it at Sanquan; Yanxiao and Li Yan struck them with three thousand picked horse, and the Shu army was routed with five thousand beheaded and the rest scattered. Hearing of the defeat, Wang Yan fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, cutting the floating bridge at Jibai ford behind him.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 唐書 莊宗紀七
passages.textZh: 丙辰，蜀主王衍出降，語在衍傳。
passages.textEn: On bingchen Wang Yan, the ruler of Shu, came out and surrendered; the details are in his biography.

label.en: The Later Tang marches on Shu

summary.zh: 李存勗滅梁後寵信伶人宦官、猜忌功臣，各地兵變四起，大將李嗣源被擁立入汴。同光四年四月初一，從馬直指揮使郭從謙在洛陽作亂，李存勗中流矢而死，屍體被伶人焚燒。李嗣源隨即入洛即位，是為後唐明宗。
summary.en: After destroying the Liang, Li Cunxu indulged his actors and eunuchs and distrusted his generals; mutinies broke out everywhere and the general Li Siyuan was carried by his troops into Bianzhou. On the first day of the fourth month of 926 Guo Congqian, commander of the Congma guard, mutinied in Luoyang; Li Cunxu was killed by a stray arrow and his body burned by actors. Li Siyuan entered Luoyang and took the throne as Emperor Mingzong.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷五 唐本紀 莊宗下
passages.textZh: 從馬直指揮使郭從謙反。夏四月丁亥朔，皇帝崩。年四十三。

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷五 唐本紀 莊宗下
passages.textZh: 帝尸為伶人焚之，明宗入洛，得其骨燼。

summary.zh: 天顯元年，耶律阿保機親征渤海國，圍忽汗城（上京龍泉府），渤海王大諲譔素服牽羊，率僚屬三百餘人出降。阿保機改渤海為東丹國，以皇太子耶律倍為人皇王統治。同年阿保機在回師途中病死。
summary.en: In 926 Abaoji marched in person against Balhae and besieged its capital Huhan (Upper Capital Longquan); King Dae Inseon came out in white with a sheep on a rope, leading three hundred officials, and surrendered. Abaoji made Balhae the kingdom of Dongdan under his eldest son Yelü Bei, "King of Men", and died of illness on the way home that same year.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀下
passages.textZh: 辛未，諲譔素服，稿索牽羊，率僚屬三百餘人出降。上優禮而釋之。

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀下
passages.textZh: 丙午，改渤海國為東丹，忽汗城為天福。

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀下
passages.textZh: 丁巳，次商嶺，夜圍扶餘府。
passages.textEn: On dingsi he halted at Shangling and surrounded Fuyu prefecture by night.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀下
passages.textZh: 庚申，拔扶餘城，誅其守將。
passages.textEn: On gengshen he took the city of Fuyu and put its commander to death.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀下
passages.textZh: 皇太子、大元帥堯骨、南府宰相蘇、北院夷離堇斜涅赤，南院夷離堇迭里是夜圍忽汗城。己巳，諲譔請降。
passages.textEn: That night the heir apparent, the commander Yaogu, the chief minister Su, and the generals Xienieci and Dieli surrounded Huhan. On jisi Yinzhuan asked to surrender.

label.zh: 拔扶餘城；是夜圍忽汗城
label.en: From Fuyu to Huhan, the Bohai capital

names.name: The state prints the Nine Classics

summary.zh: 長興三年二月，後唐宰相馮道、李愚等奏請依照石經文字雕刻《九經》印板，明宗批准。此後歷經後晉、後漢至後周廣順三年（953）全部刻成，是中國第一次由官方大規模雕版印刷儒家經典。
summary.en: In the second month of 932 the Later Tang ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu asked that the Nine Classics be carved on printing blocks following the stone classics, and Emperor Mingzong agreed. The work went on through the Later Jin and Later Han and was finished under the Later Zhou in 953 — the first large-scale official woodblock printing of the Confucian classics.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷四十三 唐書 明宗紀九
passages.textZh: 辛未，中書奏：「請依石經文字刻《九經》印板。」從之。

names.name: Li Bian founds the Southern Tang

summary.zh: 吳國權臣徐知誥（李昪）於天祚三年十月受吳帝楊溥禪讓，在金陵稱帝，國號齊，改元昇元；939年恢復李姓，改國號為唐，史稱南唐，是十國中最富庶的國家之一。
summary.en: Xu Zhigao (Li Bian), strongman of the kingdom of Wu, received the abdication of the Wu ruler Yang Pu in the tenth month of 937 and became emperor at Jinling as ruler of Qi with the era Shengyuan; in 939 he took back the surname Li and renamed the state Tang — the Southern Tang, among the richest of the Ten Kingdoms.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷六十二 南唐世家
passages.textZh: 十月，溥遣攝太尉楊璘傳位於昪，國號齊，改元昇元。

names.name: The Khitan take Kaifeng and proclaim the Liao

summary.zh: 後晉出帝對契丹稱孫不稱臣，雙方交戰。946年底遼太宗耶律德光大舉南下，晉軍主帥杜重威率二十萬大軍投降。947年正月遼軍入汴，晉出帝被押往北方，後晉亡。二月耶律德光在汴京建國號大遼，改元大同，並將晉朝的百官、宮人、圖籍、樂器等盡數送往上京。因中原各地反抗，四月北撤，死於途中。
summary.en: Emperor Chu of the Later Jin agreed to call himself the Khitan emperor's grandson but not his subject, and war followed. At the end of 946 Yelü Deguang (Emperor Taizong of Liao) swept south and the Jin commander Du Chongwei surrendered with two hundred thousand men. In the first month of 947 the Khitan entered Bian; the Jin emperor was carried off north and the Later Jin was over. In the second month Deguang proclaimed the Great Liao at Bian with the era Datong, and shipped the Jin officials, palace women, archives, instruments and regalia to his Upper Capital. Facing risings all over the north, he withdrew in the fourth month and died on the way.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀下
passages.textZh: 二月丁巳朔，建國號大遼，大赦，改元大同。

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀下
passages.textZh: 壬寅，晉諸司僚吏、嬪御、宦寺、方技、百工、圖籍、歷象、石經、銅人、明堂刻漏、太常樂譜、諸宮縣、鹵簿、法物及鎧仗，悉送上京。

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀下
passages.textZh: 留騎兵千人守魏，自率大軍而南。壬申，解里等至汴，晉帝重貴素服拜命，輿母李氏奉表請罪。
passages.textEn: He left a thousand horse to hold Wei and led the main army south himself. On renshen Jieli and the others reached Bian; the Jin emperor Chonggui received the order in plain clothes and, with his mother Lady Li, presented a memorial begging pardon.

label.zh: 留騎兵千人守魏，自率大軍而南，至汴
label.en: The Khitan army south from Wei to Bian

names.name: Liu Zhiyuan founds the Later Han

summary.zh: 契丹滅晉後，河東節度使劉知遠在太原稱帝，不改年號，仍稱天福十二年；契丹北撤後他南下入汴，國號漢，史稱後漢。後漢僅存四年，是五代中最短的朝代。
summary.en: After the Khitan destroyed the Jin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, took the throne at Taiyuan without a new era name, counting it Tianfu 12; when the Khitan withdrew he marched south into Bian and named his state Han — the Later Han, which lasted only four years, the shortest of the Five Dynasties.

label.en: Liu Zhiyuan marches south to Bian

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十 漢本紀
passages.textZh: 辛未，皇帝即位，稱天福十二年。

names.name: Guo Wei founds the Later Zhou

summary.zh: 後漢隱帝誅殺大臣，並欲加害鄴都留守郭威。郭威起兵攻入開封，廣順元年正月即皇帝位，國號周（後周）。同月，劉知遠之弟劉崇（劉旻）在太原自立，史稱北漢，依附契丹與後周對抗。
summary.en: Emperor Yin of the Later Han massacred his ministers and moved against Guo Wei, regent at Ye. Guo Wei marched on Kaifeng and in the first month of 951 took the throne as emperor of Zhou (the Later Zhou). The same month Liu Zhiyuan's brother Liu Chong (Liu Min) set himself up at Taiyuan — the Northern Han, which leaned on the Khitan against the Zhou.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十一 周本紀 太祖
passages.textZh: 廣順元年春正月丁卯，皇帝即位，大赦，改元，國號周。

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十一 周本紀 太祖
passages.textZh: 戊寅，漢劉崇自立于太原。

summary.zh: 周世宗柴榮即位不久，北漢劉旻聯合契丹來攻。顯德元年三月，世宗親征，在高平與北漢軍激戰，右軍將領樊愛能、何徽臨陣脫逃，世宗親冒矢石督戰，趙匡胤等奮擊，終獲大勝。戰後世宗斬樊愛能、何徽等七十餘將，整頓禁軍。
summary.en: Soon after Chai Rong (Emperor Shizong of Zhou) took the throne, Liu Min of the Northern Han attacked with Khitan help. In the third month of 954 Shizong took the field himself and met them at Gaoping; the generals Fan Aineng and He Hui fled with the right wing, but the emperor rode into the arrows and Zhao Kuangyin and others charged, winning a great victory. Afterwards Shizong beheaded Fan, He and some seventy officers and rebuilt the palace army.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十二 周本紀 世宗
passages.textZh: 己亥，侍衞馬軍都指揮使樊愛能、步軍都指揮使何徽伏誅。

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷一百十四 周書 世宗紀一
passages.textZh: 乙酉，車駕發京師。壬辰，至澤州。癸巳，王師與河東劉崇、契丹楊袞大戰於高平，賊軍敗績。
passages.textEn: On yiyou the emperor left the capital. On renchen he reached Zezhou. On guisi the imperial army fought Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan Yang Gun at Gaoping, and the enemy was routed.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷一百十四 周書 世宗紀一
passages.textZh: 初，車駕行次河陽，聞劉崇自潞而南，即倍程而進。
passages.textEn: At first, on reaching Heyang, the emperor heard that Liu Chong was coming south from Lu, and pressed on at double speed.

label.en: On at double speed to Zezhou
Liu Chong comes south from Lu

summary.zh: 顯德二年五月，周世宗下詔大毀佛寺，未經朝廷賜額的寺院一律廢除，禁止私自剃度，並收民間銅佛像鑄錢。這是「三武一宗滅佛」的最後一次。
summary.en: In the fifth month of 955 Shizong of Zhou ordered the great destruction of Buddhist temples: every temple without an imperial charter was closed, private ordination was forbidden, and bronze images were collected to be melted into coin. It was the last of the "three Wus and one Zong" persecutions of Buddhism.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十二 周本紀 世宗
passages.textZh: 甲戌，大毀佛寺，禁民親無侍養而為僧尼及私自度者。

names.name: Shizong takes the land between the Huai and the Yangtze

summary.zh: 顯德二年十一月起，周世宗三次親征南唐，攻克壽州等地。顯德五年，南唐割讓淮南十四州，以長江為界，對後周稱臣，削去帝號。
summary.en: From the eleventh month of 955 Shizong marched three times against the Southern Tang, taking Shouzhou and other cities. In 958 the Southern Tang ceded fourteen prefectures north of the Yangtze, accepted the river as the border, became a vassal of the Zhou and gave up the imperial title.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十二 周本紀 世宗
passages.textZh: 十一月乙未朔，李穀為淮南道行營都部署以伐唐。

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十二 周本紀 世宗
passages.textZh: 己亥，克淮南十有四州，以江為界。

summary.zh: 顯德六年四月，周世宗北伐契丹，四十二天內收復瀛、莫、寧三州及瓦橋、益津、淤口三關，正欲進取幽州時病重，回師開封後去世，年僅三十九歲。
summary.en: In the fourth month of 959 Shizong marched against the Khitan and in forty-two days retook Ying, Mo and Ning prefectures and the Waqiao, Yijin and Yukou passes. He was about to move on Youzhou when he fell ill; he returned to Kaifeng and died, only thirty-nine years old.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十二 周本紀 世宗
passages.textZh: 五月乙巳朔，取瀛州。

summary.zh: 名李存勗，沙陀人，晉王李克用之子。善戰，滅後梁、前蜀，建立後唐。晚年寵信伶人，自己也粉墨登場，取藝名「李天下」，政事敗壞，死於興教門之變。歐陽修在〈伶官傳序〉中以他為鑒：「憂勞可以興國，逸豫可以亡身。」
summary.en: Li Cunxu, a Shatuo, son of Li Keyong, Prince of Jin. A brilliant soldier, he destroyed the Later Liang and the Former Shu and founded the Later Tang. In later years he lavished favour on actors and went on stage himself as "Li Tianxia"; government collapsed and he died in the Xingjiao gate mutiny. Ouyang Xiu held him up as a warning: "toil and worry can raise a state; ease and pleasure can destroy a man."

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷四 唐本紀 莊宗上
passages.textZh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝，其先本號朱邪，蓋出於西突厥，至其後世，別自號曰沙陀

summary.zh: 字可道，瀛州景城人。歷仕後唐、後晉、契丹、後漢、後周五朝十帝，任宰相二十餘年，自號「長樂老」。主持刻印九經。歐陽修斥他「無廉恥」，也有人認為他在亂世中保全了百姓與文化。
summary.en: Courtesy name Kedao, of Jingcheng in Yingzhou. He served five regimes and ten emperors — Later Tang, Later Jin, the Khitan, Later Han and Later Zhou — and was chief minister for over twenty years, calling himself "the Old Man of Lasting Happiness". He oversaw the printing of the Nine Classics. Ouyang Xiu condemned him as "without shame"; others credit him with shielding people and learning through an age of chaos.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 雜傳 馮道
passages.textZh: 馮道字可道，瀛州景城人也。

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 雜傳 序
passages.textZh: 予讀馮道長樂老敍，見其自述以為榮，其可謂無廉恥者矣

summary.zh: 名柴榮，本姓柴，郭威皇后的姪子，被郭威收為養子。954年即位，高平之戰大勝，整頓禁軍、限制佛寺、擴建開封城，取淮南十四州，北伐收復三關，被視為五代最英明的君主。死後六個月，趙匡胤發動陳橋兵變奪取後周政權。
summary.en: Chai Rong, nephew of Guo Wei's empress, adopted by Guo Wei. Taking the throne in 954, he won at Gaoping, rebuilt the palace army, curbed the Buddhist temples, enlarged Kaifeng, took fourteen prefectures south of the Huai and retook three passes from the Khitan — reckoned the ablest ruler of the Five Dynasties. Six months after his death Zhao Kuangyin's Chenqiao mutiny ended the Zhou.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷十二 周本紀 世宗
passages.textZh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，本姓柴氏，邢州龍岡人也。

summary.zh: 字正倫，徐州人，幼年孤貧，被吳王楊行密收養，後為權臣徐溫養子，改名徐知誥。937年受吳禪稱帝，後恢復李姓，國號唐（南唐）。在位期間保境安民、與鄰國和好。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zhenglun, of Xuzhou, an orphan taken in by Yang Xingmi, King of Wu, and then adopted by the strongman Xu Wen as Xu Zhigao. He took the throne from the Wu in 937, later went back to the surname Li and named his state Tang (the Southern Tang), keeping the peace at home and with his neighbours.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷六十二 南唐世家
passages.textZh: 李昪字正倫，徐州人也。世本微賤，父榮，遇唐末之亂，不知其所終。昪少孤，流寓濠、泗間，楊行密攻濠州，得之，奇其狀貌，養以為子。

summary.zh: 字重光，南唐後主，李璟第六子。工書畫、善詩詞。975年宋軍攻破金陵，他出降被押往汴京，封違命侯，978年死於汴京。亡國後所作〈虞美人〉「問君能有幾多愁」等詞，被後人推為詞中絕唱。
summary.en: Courtesy name Chongguang, last ruler of the Southern Tang, sixth son of Li Jing; a gifted calligrapher, painter and poet. When Song troops took Jinling in 975 he surrendered and was taken to Bian as "Marquis of Disobeyed Orders", dying there in 978. The lyrics he wrote in captivity are counted among the finest in the form.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷六十二 南唐世家
passages.textZh: 煜字重光，初名從嘉，景第六子也。煜為人仁孝，善屬文，工書畫，而豐額駢齒，一目重瞳子。

summary.zh: 字具美，杭州臨安人，少年時販鹽為生。唐末以鎮壓黃巢等起事起家，據有兩浙，907年受後梁封為吳越王。修築錢塘江捍海石塘，奉行保境安民、尊奉中原王朝的國策，使吳越成為十國中最安定的地區之一。
summary.en: Courtesy name Jumei, of Lin'an near Hangzhou, a salt smuggler in his youth. He rose fighting Huang Chao and other rebels at the end of the Tang, held the two Zhe regions and was made King of Wuyue by the Later Liang in 907. He built the stone sea wall along the Qiantang, kept the peace and deferred to the northern courts, making Wuyue one of the calmest of the Ten Kingdoms.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷六十七 吳越世家
passages.textZh: 錢鏐字具美，杭州臨安人也。

summary.zh: 字光圖，許州舞陽人，年輕時以屠牛、盜驢、販私鹽為業，人稱「賊王八」。後從軍，護衛逃往蜀地的唐僖宗，逐步據有西川。907年唐亡後在成都稱帝，國號蜀，史稱前蜀。其墓永陵在今成都。
summary.en: Courtesy name Guangtu, of Wuyang in Xuzhou, who in his youth slaughtered cattle, stole donkeys and smuggled salt — the locals called him "Wang Ba the Thief". He became a soldier, guarded Emperor Xizong on his flight to Shu and gradually made western Sichuan his own. When the Tang fell in 907 he took the throne at Chengdu as emperor of Shu — the Former Shu. His tomb, the Yongling, stands in Chengdu.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷六十三 前蜀世家
passages.textZh: 王建字光圖，許州舞陽人也。隆眉廣顙，狀貌偉然。少無賴，以屠牛、盜驢、販私鹽為事，里人謂之「賊王八」。後為忠武軍卒，稍遷隊將。

summary.zh: 乾德元年，宋太祖以援助湖南周保權平定內亂為名，派慕容延釗、李處耘借道荊南出兵，順勢迫使荊南高繼沖納土歸朝，隨即攻克潭州，平定湖南。這是宋統一南方的第一步。
summary.en: In 963 Emperor Taizu, on the pretext of helping Zhou Baoquan of Hunan put down a mutiny, sent Murong Yanzhao and Li Chuyun through Jingnan; on the way they made Gao Jichong of Jingnan hand over his lands, then took Tanzhou and pacified Hunan — the first step in Song's conquest of the south.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀一
passages.textZh: 甲午，慕容延釗入荊南，高繼沖請歸朝，得州三，縣十七。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀一
passages.textZh: 乙未，克潭州。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀一 乾德元年
passages.textZh: 甲午，慕容延釗入荊南，高繼沖請歸朝，得州三，縣十七。乙未，克潭州。
passages.textEn: On jiawu Murong Yanzhao entered Jingnan and Gao Jichong submitted, giving up three prefectures and seventeen counties. On yiwei Tanzhou was taken.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀一 乾德元年
passages.textZh: 戊寅，慕容延釗破三江口，下岳州，克復朗州，湖南平。
passages.textEn: On wuyin Murong Yanzhao broke through at Sanjiangkou, took Yuezhou and recovered Langzhou; Hunan was pacified.

label.zh: 慕容延釗入荊南，克潭州

summary.zh: 乾德三年正月，王全斌等率宋軍分兩路入蜀，六十六日而平，後蜀主孟昶出降，宋得州四十五、縣一百九十八、戶五十三萬餘。
summary.en: In the first month of 965 Wang Quanbin and others invaded Shu by two routes and conquered it in sixty-six days; Meng Chang of the Later Shu surrendered, and Song gained forty-five prefectures, 198 counties and more than 530,000 households.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀二
passages.textZh: 乙酉，蜀主孟昶降。得州四十五、縣一百九十八、户五十三萬四千三十有九。

summary.zh: 開寶四年二月，潘美率宋軍攻克廣州，俘南漢主劉鋹，嶺南平定，宋得州六十、縣二百一十四。
summary.en: In the second month of 971 Pan Mei took Guangzhou and captured Liu Chang, ruler of the Southern Han; Lingnan was pacified and Song gained sixty prefectures and 214 counties.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀二
passages.textZh: 己丑，潘美克廣州，俘劉鋹，廣南平。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀二 開寶三年
passages.textZh: 九月己亥朔，命潭州防禦使潘美為賀州道兵馬行營都部署，朗州團練使尹崇珂副之。遣使發十州兵會賀州，以伐南漢。
passages.textEn: On jihai, the first of the ninth month, Pan Mei, defence commissioner of Tanzhou, was made commander of the Hezhou route with Yin Chongke as his deputy, and envoys raised the troops of ten prefectures to meet at Hezhou to attack Southern Han.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖紀二 開寶四年
passages.textZh: 癸丑，潘美等取英州、雄州。
passages.textEn: On guichou Pan Mei and the others took Yingzhou and Xiongzhou.

label.zh: 潘美為賀州道都部署，會賀州以伐南漢

summary.zh: 太平興國三年，吳越王錢俶入朝汴京，五月獻出所轄十三州一軍，納土歸宋。吳越免於兵火，杭州的繁榮得以保存。同年漳、泉二州的陳洪進也納土。
summary.en: In 978 Qian Chu, King of Wuyue, came to court at Bian and in the fifth month handed over his thirteen prefectures and one army district to the Song. Wuyue was spared war and Hangzhou's prosperity survived. Chen Hongjin of Zhang and Quan did the same that year.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀一
passages.textZh: 己酉，吳越國王錢俶來朝。

summary.zh: 太平興國四年，宋太宗親征北漢，擊退來援的遼軍，圍攻太原，五月北漢主劉繼元出降，北漢亡。唐末以來的分裂局面至此基本結束（燕雲十六州仍在遼手中）。宋太宗隨即乘勝攻遼，在高梁河大敗。
summary.en: In 979 Emperor Taizong marched in person against the Northern Han, drove off a Liao relief army and besieged Taiyuan; in the fifth month Liu Jiyuan surrendered and the Northern Han was over. The division that began at the end of the Tang was largely ended (the Sixteen Prefectures stayed with the Liao). Taizong went straight on to attack the Liao and was routed at the Gaoliang river.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀一
passages.textZh: 辛未，幸太原城，詔諭北漢主劉繼元使降。壬申夜，帝幸城西，督諸將發機石攻城。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀一 太平興國四年
passages.textZh: 甲子，帝發京師。戊寅，次澶州，觀魚於河。
passages.textEn: On jiazi the emperor left the capital. On wuyin he halted at Chanzhou and watched the fishing on the river.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀一 太平興國四年
passages.textZh: 三月庚辰朔，次鎮州。
passages.textEn: On gengchen, the first of the third month, he halted at Zhenzhou.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗紀一 太平興國四年
passages.textZh: 庚午，次太原，駐蹕汾東行營。辛未，幸太原城，詔諭北漢主劉繼元使降。
passages.textEn: On gengwu he reached Taiyuan and camped east of the Fen. On xinwei he went to the walls of Taiyuan and called on Liu Jiyuan, ruler of Northern Han, to surrender.

label.zh: 次太原，詔諭劉繼元使降

names.name: The Yongxi campaign and the death of Yang Ye

summary.zh: 雍熙三年，宋太宗分三路伐遼，東路曹彬在岐溝關大敗，全線撤退。西路副帥楊業奉命掩護雲、應等州百姓內遷，主帥潘美、監軍王侁逼他出戰，楊業請他們在陳家谷口設伏接應，出戰後轉戰至谷口卻不見援兵，力戰被俘，絕食三日而死。
summary.en: In 986 Emperor Taizong attacked the Liao on three fronts; Cao Bin's eastern army was crushed at Qigou pass and the whole offensive collapsed. Yang Ye, second in command in the west, was covering the evacuation of the people of Yun and Ying when his superior Pan Mei and the army inspector Wang Shen pushed him into battle. He asked them to wait in ambush at the mouth of the Chenjia valley; when he fought his way back there no one was waiting. He was captured after a desperate fight and starved himself to death in three days.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百七十二 楊業傳
passages.textZh: 因指陳家谷口曰：「諸君于此張步兵強弩，為左右翼以援，俟業轉戰至此，即以步兵夾擊救之，不然，無遺類矣。」

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷五 太宗紀二 雍熙三年
passages.textZh: 庚寅，北伐，以天平軍節度使曹彬為幽州道行營前軍馬步水陸都部署，河陽三城節度使崔彥進副之；侍衛馬軍都指揮使、彰化軍節度使米信為西北道都部署，沙州觀察使杜彥圭副之，以其眾出雄州；侍衛步軍都指揮使、靜難軍節度使田重進為定州路都部署，出飛狐。
passages.textEn: On gengyin the northern campaign began: Cao Bin was made commander of the Youzhou route with Cui Yanjin as his deputy, and Mi Xin commander of the north-west route with Du Yangui as his deputy, going out from Xiongzhou; Tian Zhongjin was made commander of the Dingzhou route, going out by Feihu.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷五 太宗紀二 雍熙三年
passages.textZh: 二月壬子，以檢校太師、忠武軍節度使潘美為雲、應、朔等州都部署，雲州觀察使楊業副之，出鴈門。
passages.textEn: On renzi of the second month Pan Mei was made commander for Yun, Ying, Shuo and the other prefectures with Yang Ye as his deputy, going out by Yanmen.

label.zh: 曹彬為幽州道都部署，米信以其眾出雄州
label.en: Cao Bin and Mi Xin out of Xiongzhou towards Youzhou

label.zh: 田重進為定州路都部署，出飛狐

label.en: Pan Mei and Yang Ye out by Yanmen

fiction.zh: 「楊家將」故事中的佘太君、穆桂英、天門陣、楊門女將等，多出自後世小說戲曲，正史無載；楊業之妻在史料中稱折氏的說法也晚出。
fiction.en: In the "Generals of the Yang family" stories, She Taijun, Mu Guiying, the Heavenly Gate formation and the women warriors of the Yang house come from later novels and opera, not the histories.

names.name: The rising of Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun

summary.zh: 淳化四年二月，蜀地青城縣茶農王小波聚眾起事，殺彭山縣令齊元振。王小波戰死後，李順繼為首領，994年攻佔成都，自稱大蜀王。宋軍收復成都後，餘部至995年才被平定。
summary.en: In the second month of 993 Wang Xiaobo, a tea grower of Qingcheng in Shu, raised a band and killed Qi Yuanzhen, magistrate of Pengshan. After Wang died in battle Li Shun led the rising, took Chengdu in 994 and called himself King of Great Shu. Song retook Chengdu, but the last bands were not crushed until 995.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷五 太宗紀二
passages.textZh: 永康軍青城縣民王小波聚徒為寇，殺眉州彭山縣令齊元振。

names.name: The "Heavenly Text" and the Taishan sacrifice

summary.zh: 澶淵之盟後，宋真宗聽從王欽若之議，以神道設教來挽回顏面。大中祥符元年正月，宣稱有「天書」降於承天門，群臣拜迎，改元大中祥符，同年十月東封泰山，此後各地爭獻祥瑞，耗費巨大。
summary.en: After the Chanyuan treaty Emperor Zhenzong, on Wang Qinruo's advice, sought to restore his prestige through signs from Heaven. In the first month of 1008 a "Heavenly Text" was announced as having descended on the Chengtian gate; the court greeted it with ceremony, the era was renamed Dazhong Xiangfu, and in the tenth month the emperor performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai. Auspicious omens poured in from everywhere at enormous cost.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷七 真宗紀二
passages.textZh: 上召群臣拜迎於朝元殿啟封，號稱天書。

summary.zh: 康定元年正月，西夏元昊進攻延州，宋將劉平、石元孫率軍來援，在延州城外三川口遭伏擊全軍覆沒，二人被俘。這是宋夏戰爭中宋軍的第一次大敗。
summary.en: In the first month of 1040 Yuanhao of Xi Xia attacked Yanzhou; the Song generals Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun, marching to its relief, were ambushed at Sanchuankou outside the city, their army destroyed and both captured — the first great Song defeat of the war with Xi Xia.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十 仁宗紀二
passages.textZh: 是月，元昊寇延州，執鄜延、環慶兩路副都總管劉平、鄜延副都總管石元孫。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百八十五 夏國傳上
passages.textZh: 未幾，夏人攻金明砦，執都監李士彬父子。破安遠、塞門、永平諸砦，圍延州，設伏三川口，執劉平、石元孫、傅偃、劉發、石遜等。
passages.textEn: Soon the Xia attacked the Jinming fort and captured the commandant Li Shibin and his son; they broke the Anyuan, Saimen and Yongping forts, besieged Yanzhou, laid an ambush at Sanchuankou and captured Liu Ping, Shi Yuansun, Fu Yan, Liu Fa, Shi Xun and others.

label.en: From the Jinming fort to Yanzhou

summary.zh: 慶曆元年二月，元昊進攻渭州，宋將任福輕敵冒進，在好水川中伏，任福及將士六千餘人戰死。
summary.en: In the second month of 1041 Yuanhao struck at Weizhou; the Song general Ren Fu pressed on rashly and was ambushed at Haoshuichuan, dying with more than six thousand of his men.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十一 仁宗紀三
passages.textZh: 是月，元昊寇渭州，環慶路馬步軍副總管任福敗于好水川，福及將佐軍士死者六千余人。

summary.zh: 慶曆三年，宋仁宗開天章閣召二府大臣條對時政，范仲淹上疏陳十事：明黜陟、抑僥倖、精貢舉、擇官長、均公田、厚農桑、修武備、減徭役、覃恩信、重命令，與富弼、韓琦等推行新政。因觸動官僚利益，被攻擊為「朋黨」，一年多後即告失敗。
summary.en: In 1043 Emperor Renzong opened the Tianzhang pavilion and asked his chief ministers for written proposals. Fan Zhongyan presented ten: clear promotion and demotion, curbing privilege, better examinations, choosing able governors, fair office lands, encouraging farming, military preparedness, lighter labour service, spreading the emperor's grace and respecting edicts. With Fu Bi and Han Qi he put them into effect, but the officials they threatened denounced them as a faction, and within little more than a year the reforms had failed.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百一十四 范仲淹傳
passages.textZh: 仲淹皇恐，退而上十事：一曰明黜陟。

names.name: The Qingli peace with Xi Xia

summary.zh: 宋夏連年交戰兩敗俱傷。慶曆四年，元昊自稱夏國主向宋稱臣，宋冊封其為夏國主，每年「歲賜」西夏銀、絹、茶等共二十五萬五千。
summary.en: Years of war had exhausted both sides. In 1044 Yuanhao called himself ruler of the Xia state and a vassal of Song; Song invested him as ruler of Xia and paid him yearly "gifts" of silver, silk and tea totalling 255,000 units.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十一 仁宗紀三
passages.textZh: 遣保安軍判官邵良佐使元昊，許封冊為夏國主，歲賜絹十萬匹、茶三萬斤。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百八十五 夏國傳上
passages.textZh: 凡歲賜銀、綺、絹、茶二十五萬五千

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 廣源州壯族首領儂智高多次請求內附未果，皇祐四年起兵，攻陷邕州，建號大南國，沿江而下圍攻廣州五十七日，嶺南大震。次年狄青奇襲崑崙關，在邕州歸仁鋪大敗儂軍，儂智高逃往大理。
summary.en: Nong Zhigao, a Zhuang chief of Guangyuan whose requests to submit to Song had been turned down, rose in 1052, took Yongzhou, proclaimed the state of Great Nan, came down the river and besieged Guangzhou for fifty-seven days, shaking all of Lingnan. The next year Di Qing took the Kunlun pass by surprise and crushed him at Guirenpu near Yongzhou; Nong fled to Dali.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十二 仁宗紀四
passages.textZh: 儂智高反。五月乙巳朔，智高陷邕州，遂陷橫、貴等八州，圍廣州。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十二 仁宗紀四
passages.textZh: 廣源州蠻儂智高反。
passages.textEn: Nong Zhigao, a man of the Guangyuan tribes, rebelled.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十二 仁宗紀四
passages.textZh: 五月乙巳朔，智高陷邕州，遂陷橫、貴等八州，圍廣州。
passages.textEn: On yisi, the first of the fifth month, Zhigao took Yongzhou, then Heng, Gui and eight prefectures in all, and besieged Guangzhou.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十二 仁宗紀四
passages.textZh: 戊午，狄青敗智高於邕州，斬首五千余級，智高遁去。
passages.textEn: On wuwu Di Qing beat Zhigao at Yongzhou, taking over five thousand heads, and Zhigao fled.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百九十 狄青傳
passages.textZh: 青明日乃整軍騎，一晝夜絕昆侖關，出歸仁鋪為陣。賊既失險，悉出逆戰。
passages.textEn: The next day Qing drew up his cavalry, crossed the Kunlun Pass in a day and a night and drew up at Guirenpu. Having lost the pass, the rebels came out in full to fight.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百九十 狄青傳
passages.textZh: 青執白旗麾騎兵，縱左右翼，出賊不意，大敗之，追奔五十里，斬首數千級
passages.textEn: Qing waved his cavalry on with a white flag, loosed both wings and took the rebels by surprise, routing them, pursuing for fifty li and taking several thousand heads

label.en: Di Qing over the Kunlun Pass

summary.zh: 司馬光編撰編年體通史，宋英宗命他在秘閣設局續修，宋神宗賜名《資治通鑑》並親製序文。司馬光在洛陽與劉攽、劉恕、范祖禹等修書十九年，1084年成書，共二百九十四卷，記事上起前403年三家分晉，下迄959年。
summary.en: Sima Guang was compiling a chronological history of China; Emperor Yingzong gave him an office in the imperial library to continue it, and Emperor Shenzong named it the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance and wrote its preface himself. Working in Luoyang with Liu Ban, Liu Shu and Fan Zuyu for nineteen years, Sima Guang finished it in 1084: 294 fascicles, from the partition of Jin in 403 BCE to 959.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百三十六 司馬光傳
passages.textZh: 至是，神宗名之曰《資治通鑒

summary.zh: 元豐八年宋神宗去世，年幼的哲宗即位，高太后臨朝聽政，召司馬光入朝。次年改元元祐，司馬光任宰相，盡廢王安石新法，史稱「元祐更化」。1093年哲宗親政後又恢復新法，新舊黨爭愈演愈烈。
summary.en: Emperor Shenzong died in 1085; the boy Zhezong succeeded with the Empress Dowager Gao as regent, and she summoned Sima Guang. From the next year, the first of the Yuanyou era, Sima Guang as chief minister abolished Wang Anshi's New Laws wholesale — the "Yuanyou restoration". When Zhezong took power himself in 1093 the New Laws came back and the factional struggle grew ever more bitter.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十七 哲宗紀一
passages.textZh: 資政殿學士司馬光過闕，入見。

summary.zh: 宋徽宗在東南設「應奉局」搜刮奇花異石運往汴京（「花石綱」），民怨沸騰。宣和二年十月，睦州青溪人方臘起事，數月間攻佔六州五十二縣。宋廷調派原準備北伐遼朝的童貫、譚稹率軍南下，次年四月擒方臘。
summary.en: Emperor Huizong's commissioners combed the southeast for rare plants and rocks to ship to Bian — the "flower and rock convoys" — and the people seethed. In the tenth month of 1120 Fang La of Qingxi in Muzhou rose and in a few months took six prefectures and fifty-two counties. The court sent south the armies of Tong Guan and Tan Zhen that had been meant for the war on the Liao, and captured Fang La in the fourth month of 1121.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十二 徽宗紀四
passages.textZh: 建德軍青溪妖賊方臘反，命譚稹討之。

summary.zh: 宣和三年二月，淮南盜宋江等攻掠淮陽軍，又轉戰京東、河北，進入楚州、海州境內，海州知州張叔夜設伏招降了他們。正史關於宋江的記載僅有寥寥數條。
summary.en: In the second month of 1121 the Huainan bandit Song Jiang and his band raided Huaiyang, then roamed through Jingdong and Hebei into Chu and Hai prefectures, where Zhang Shuye, prefect of Haizhou, ambushed them and accepted their surrender. The histories say no more than a few lines about him.

fiction.zh: 《水滸傳》中梁山泊一百單八將聚義、替天行道、征方臘等情節，是元明說書人與小說家的創作；史書只記宋江一夥流竄數州後被張叔夜招降，是否參與征方臘，史料記載互相矛盾。
fiction.en: The 108 heroes of Liangshan, "acting on Heaven's behalf" and the campaign against Fang La in the Water Margin are the work of Yuan and Ming storytellers; the histories record only a band that roamed several prefectures and surrendered to Zhang Shuye, and the sources contradict one another on whether he fought Fang La.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十二 徽宗紀四
passages.textZh: 淮南盜宋江等犯淮陽軍，遣將討捕，又犯京東、河北，入楚、海州界，命知州張叔夜招降之。

summary.zh: 宣和七年冬，金軍兩路南下，宋徽宗驚慌失措，十二月下詔禪位給太子趙桓（宋欽宗），自稱教主道君太上皇帝，隨即南逃。次年金軍圍汴京，再次年靖康之變，父子同被俘北去。
summary.en: In the winter of 1125 the Jin invaded on two fronts. In a panic Emperor Huizong abdicated in the twelfth month to his son Zhao Huan (Emperor Qinzong), styled himself "Retired Emperor, Lord of the Daoist Teaching", and fled south. The next year the Jin besieged Bian, and the year after came the Jingkang disaster, when father and son were both carried off north.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十二 徽宗紀四
passages.textZh: 庚申，詔內禪，皇太子即皇帝位。尊帝為教主道君太上皇帝，居於龍德宮。

names.name: The mutiny of Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan

summary.zh: 建炎三年三月，扈從統制苗傅、劉正彥在杭州發動兵變，殺樞密使王淵和宦官，逼宋高宗退位給三歲的皇子，由隆祐太后垂簾。張浚、呂頤浩、韓世忠等起兵勤王，四月高宗復辟，恢復建炎年號，苗、劉兵敗被殺。
summary.en: In the third month of 1129 the guard commanders Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan mutinied at Hangzhou, killed the head of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Yuan and the eunuchs, and forced Emperor Gaozong to abdicate to his three-year-old son under the Empress Dowager Longyou. Zhang Jun, Lü Yihao and Han Shizhong marched to the rescue; in the fourth month Gaozong was restored, the Jianyan era resumed, and Miao and Liu were beaten and executed.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十五 高宗紀二
passages.textZh: 庚戌，復紀年建炎。命張浚知樞密院事，苗傅、劉正彥並檢校少保。

confidenceNote.zh: 「十萬」「八千」等兵力數字出自後世記載，未見於此處引文。
confidenceNote.en: The figures of 100,000 and 8,000 come from later accounts, not from the passage quoted.

summary.zh: 建炎四年，金將完顏宗弼（兀朮）渡江南侵後北撤，韓世忠以八千水軍在鎮江一帶截擊，將金軍十萬困於黃天蕩四十八日。宗弼最終掘通老鸛河故道，乘無風之日以火箭焚燒宋軍大船而脫身。
summary.en: In 1130 the Jin general Wanyan Zongbi (Wuzhu), withdrawing north after raiding south of the Yangtze, was intercepted near Zhenjiang by Han Shizhong with eight thousand marines, who kept his army bottled up in the Huangtiandang marsh for forty-eight days. Zongbi finally escaped by digging out an old channel and, on a windless day, burning the big Song ships with fire arrows.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十四 韓世忠傳
passages.textZh: 世忠與二酋相持黃天蕩者四十八日。

names.name: Yue Fei retakes the six commanderies of Xiangyang

summary.zh: 紹興四年，偽齊李成攻佔襄陽、唐、鄧、隨、郢等州。岳飛上奏：「襄陽等六郡為恢復中原基本」，奉命出兵，擊潰李成，收復襄陽六郡。這是南宋第一次收復大片失地。
summary.en: In 1134 Li Cheng of the puppet state of Qi had taken Xiangyang, Tang, Deng, Sui and Ying. Yue Fei memorialised that "the six commanderies of Xiangyang are the foundation for recovering the Central Plain", was sent against them, routed Li Cheng and took back all six — the Southern Song's first large recovery of lost ground.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 襄陽等六郡為恢復中原基本，今當先取六郡，以除心膂之病。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 成夜遁，復襄陽。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 飛鼓眾而登，超投崖死，復郢州，遣張憲、徐慶復隨州。
passages.textEn: Yue Fei drove his men up the walls; Jing Chao threw himself off the cliff, Yingzhou was recovered, and Zhang Xian and Xu Qing were sent to recover Suizhou.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 成夜遁，復襄陽。劉豫益成兵屯新野，飛與王萬夾擊之，連破其眾。
passages.textEn: Li Cheng fled by night and Xiangyang was recovered. Liu Yu reinforced Li Cheng's troops at Xinye; Yue Fei and Wang Wan attacked them from two sides and broke them again and again.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 飛渡江中流，顧幕屬曰：「飛不擒賊，不涉此江。」抵郢州城下
passages.textEn: In midstream Yue Fei turned to his staff and said: "If I do not take the rebels, I will not cross this river again." He reached the walls of Yingzhou

label.zh: 飛渡江，抵郢州城下，復郢州

summary.zh: 紹興八年二月，宋高宗從建康回到臨安（杭州），此後以臨安為「行在所」，名義上仍以汴京為京師，實際上定都臨安近一百四十年。
summary.en: In the second month of 1138 Emperor Gaozong returned from Jiankang to Lin'an (Hangzhou), which from then on was his "temporary residence": Bian remained the capital in name, but Lin'an was the real capital for nearly 140 years.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十九 高宗紀六
passages.textZh: 戊寅，帝至臨安。

names.name: The Jin move their capital to Yanjing

summary.zh: 金海陵王完顏亮弒熙宗自立後，推行漢化並集權中央，貞元元年三月由上京會寧府遷都燕京，改稱中都大興府。北京從此開始成為王朝都城。
summary.en: Wanyan Liang, Prince of Hailing, who had murdered Emperor Xizong for the throne, pressed sinicisation and central control, and in the third month of 1153 moved the capital from Huining in the far north to Yanjing, renamed the Central Capital, Daxing. From this time Beijing was an imperial capital.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷五 海陵紀
passages.textZh: 改燕京爲中都，府曰大興，汴京爲南京，中京爲北京。

summary.zh: 宋孝宗即位後銳意恢復，隆興元年起用張浚北伐，李顯忠、邵宏淵攻克靈璧、宿州，金軍反攻，宋軍因二將不和在符離大潰。次年宋金議和，宋對金不再稱臣而稱姪，歲幣減為二十萬，史稱隆興和議。
summary.en: Emperor Xiaozong came to the throne determined to recover the north. In 1163 Zhang Jun sent Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan north; they took Lingbi and Suzhou, but when the Jin counter-attacked the two quarrelling generals' armies broke at Fuli. The peace of Longxing followed: Song called itself the Jin emperor's nephew rather than his subject, and the yearly payment fell to 200,000.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 孝宗紀一
passages.textZh: 甲寅，李顯忠、邵宏淵軍大潰于符離。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 孝宗紀一 隆興元年
passages.textZh: 李顯忠、邵宏淵至濠州。
passages.textEn: Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan reached Haozhou.

label.en: Routed at Fuli, back to Haozhou

summary.zh: 韓侂冑排擠宰相趙汝愚後掌權，指朱熹等人的道學為「偽學」。慶元年間朝廷禁止偽學，列出「偽學逆黨籍」五十九人，凡與之有關者不得任官、應試，史稱慶元黨禁。1202年才解除。
summary.en: Han Tuozhou drove out the chief minister Zhao Ruyu, took power and branded the Learning of the Way of Zhu Xi and his circle "false learning". During the Qingyuan era the court banned it and drew up a register of fifty-nine "rebels of false learning"; anyone connected with them was barred from office and the examinations. The ban was lifted in 1202.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三十七 寧宗紀一
passages.textZh: 甲辰，右諫議大夫劉德秀劾留正引用偽學之黨，詔落正觀文殿大學士，罷宮觀。

summary.zh: 開禧二年，韓侂冑主持北伐金朝，五月下詔伐金，宋軍各路相繼敗績，四川守將吳曦叛降金朝。1207年史彌遠與楊皇后密謀殺死韓侂冑，次年將其首級函送金朝，訂立嘉定和議，宋對金改稱姪為稱伯，歲幣增至三十萬。
summary.en: In 1206 Han Tuozhou launched a war on the Jin; war was declared in the fifth month, and one Song army after another was beaten, while Wu Xi, commander in Sichuan, went over to the Jin. In 1207 Shi Miyuan and Empress Yang had Han Tuozhou murdered, and the next year sent his head in a box to the Jin to seal the peace of Jiading, under which Song addressed the Jin emperor as "uncle" and raised the yearly payment to 300,000.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三十八 寧宗紀二
passages.textZh: 癸巳，以伐金告於天地、宗廟、社稷。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三十八 寧宗紀二
passages.textZh: 皇甫斌引兵攻唐州，敗績。

names.name: The Jin court flees to Kaifeng

summary.zh: 貞祐二年，蒙古大軍圍攻中都，金宣宗獻公主與金帛求和。蒙古軍撤退後，宣宗不顧太學生等反對，決意南遷汴京，河北各地隨即大亂，次年中都被蒙古攻陷。
summary.en: In 1214 the Mongols besieged the Central Capital and Emperor Xuanzong of Jin bought peace with a princess and treasure. When they withdrew he decided, over the protests of students of the imperial academy, to move south to Kaifeng; Hebei fell into chaos and the next year the Central Capital fell to the Mongols.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷十四 宣宗紀上
passages.textZh: 上決意南遷，詔告國內。

confidenceNote.zh: 《元史》說崩於「薩里川哈老徒之行宮」，其地今人有六盤山一帶與蒙古高原兩說；地圖上暫標於〈太祖紀〉所記清水縣附近。
confidenceNote.en: The History of Yuan says he died at "the travelling palace of Qalaatu on the Sari steppe", placed by some near the Liupan mountains and by others on the Mongolian plateau; the map marks it near Qingshui, the last place the annals name.

summary.zh: 1227年，成吉思汗在征西夏途中病倒，七月死於行營，西夏隨即投降。據《元史》，他臨終留下「假道於宋」、出兵唐鄧直擣大梁以滅金的策略。其埋葬地點至今不明。
summary.en: In 1227, campaigning against Xi Xia, Chinggis Khan fell ill and died in camp in the seventh month; Xi Xia surrendered soon after. According to the History of Yuan, he left on his deathbed the plan to pass through Song territory and strike from Tang and Deng at Kaifeng to destroy the Jin. Where he was buried is still unknown.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀
passages.textZh: 己丑，崩于薩里川哈老徒之行宮。

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖紀
passages.textZh: 臨崩謂左右曰：「金精兵在潼關，南據連山，北限大河，難以遽破。若假道于宋，宋、金世讎，必能許我，則下兵唐、鄧，直擣大梁。金急，必徵兵潼關。然以數萬之眾，千里赴援，人馬疲弊，雖至弗能戰，破之必矣。」

summary.zh: 成吉思汗死後兩年，太宗元年八月，諸王百官大會於怯綠連河（克魯倫河），遵照太祖遺詔推舉三子窩闊台即大汗位，初立朝儀，頒布大札撒（大法令）。窩闊台在位期間滅金、建和林城，並發動長子西征。
summary.en: Two years after Chinggis died, in the eighth month of 1229, the princes and officials gathered on the Kherlen river and, following his will, raised his third son Ögedei as Great Khan, introducing court ceremony and proclaiming the Great Yasa. Under Ögedei the Mongols destroyed the Jin, built Karakorum and launched the great western campaign.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗紀
passages.textZh: 秋八月己未，諸王百官大會于怯綠連河曲雕阿蘭之地，以太祖遺詔即皇帝位于庫鐵烏阿剌里。

summary.zh: 1234年宋蒙聯軍滅金後，宋理宗聽從趙范、趙葵之議，乘蒙古北撤收復三京：全子才、趙葵率軍入汴京，徐敏子進入洛陽。宋軍因糧運不繼，在洛陽城外被蒙古軍擊潰而退。蒙古以宋敗盟為由，次年起大舉攻宋，宋蒙戰爭持續四十餘年。
summary.en: After the Song and Mongols destroyed the Jin in 1234, Emperor Lizong, on the advice of Zhao Fan and Zhao Kui, tried to seize the three old capitals while the Mongols were away: Quan Zicai and Zhao Kui entered Kaifeng and Xu Minzi reached Luoyang. With no supplies getting through, the Song army was routed by the Mongols outside Luoyang and fell back. The Mongols took it as a breach of faith and from the next year invaded in force — a war that lasted more than forty years.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 理宗紀一
passages.textZh: 辛酉，詔遣太常寺主簿朱揚祖、閣門祗候林拓詣洛陽省謁八陵。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 理宗紀一
passages.textZh: 趙葵京河制置使、知應天府、南京留守，全子才關陝制置使、知河南府、西京留守。

names.name: Khubilai becomes Great Khan at Kaiping

summary.zh: 1256年，忽必烈命劉秉忠（僧子聰）在灤水北岸築開平城。1259年蒙哥死於釣魚城下，1260年三月忽必烈在開平召集部分宗王即大汗位，建元中統；其弟阿里不哥同時在和林稱汗，兄弟相爭四年，忽必烈獲勝。
summary.en: In 1256 Khubilai had Liu Bingzhong (the monk Zicong) build the city of Kaiping north of the Luan river. Möngke died before Diaoyu in 1259, and in the third month of 1260 Khubilai had some of the princes raise him as Great Khan at Kaiping, with the era Zhongtong; his brother Ariq Böke was proclaimed at Karakorum at the same time, and Khubilai won the four-year war between them.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷四 世祖紀一
passages.textZh: 命僧子聰卜地于桓州東、灤水北，城開平府，經營宮室。

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷四 世祖紀一
passages.textZh: 辛卯，帝即皇帝位

summary.zh: 至元八年十一月，忽必烈採用劉秉忠的建議，取《易經》「大哉乾元」之義，建國號為「大元」。次年改中都為大都，作為首都。
summary.en: In the eleventh month of 1271 Khubilai, on Liu Bingzhong's advice, took the dynastic name "Great Yuan" from the Book of Changes ("Great is the originating power of Qian"). The next year the Central Capital was renamed Dadu and made the capital.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷七 世祖紀四
passages.textZh: 建國號曰大元

summary.zh: 襄樊陷落後，元軍在伯顏率領下沿江東下。德祐元年二月，權臣賈似道親率十三萬宋軍在丁家洲迎戰，前軍孫虎臣敗績，夏貴不戰而走，宋軍全線潰散。南宋主力就此瓦解，賈似道被貶後在押解途中被殺。
summary.en: After Xiangyang fell, the Yuan army under Bayan came down the Yangtze. In the second month of 1275 the chief minister Jia Sidao led 130,000 Song troops to meet it at Dingjiazhou; the vanguard under Sun Huchen was beaten, Xia Gui fled without fighting, and the whole Song army collapsed. The Southern Song's main army was gone; Jia Sidao was banished and murdered on the way.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 瀛國公紀
passages.textZh: 庚申，虎臣與大元兵戰于丁家洲，敗績，奔魯港，夏貴不戰而去。

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷八 世祖紀五
passages.textZh: 大軍次丁家洲，戰船蔽江而下。宋賈似道分遣步帥孫虎臣及督府節制軍馬蘇劉義，集兵船于江之南北岸。
passages.textEn: The main army halted at Dingjiazhou, its warships covering the river as they came down. The Song minister Jia Sidao sent Sun Huchen and Su Liuyi to mass troops and ships on both banks.

label.zh: 戰船蔽江而下，次丁家洲
label.en: The Yuan fleet down the Yangzi to Dingjiazhou

summary.zh: 并州太原人，原為北漢名將，以驍勇善戰著稱，號「楊無敵」。北漢亡後歸宋，鎮守代州抵禦遼軍。986年雍熙北伐時在陳家谷口兵敗被俘，絕食而死。其子楊延昭、孫楊文廣也是名將，後世演為「楊家將」故事。
summary.en: Of Taiyuan in Bingzhou, a famous general of the Northern Han, called "Yang the Invincible". After the Northern Han fell he served Song, guarding Daizhou against the Liao. In the campaign of 986 he was beaten and captured at the mouth of the Chenjia valley and starved himself to death. His son Yang Yanzhao and grandson Yang Wenguang were generals too; later storytellers turned them into the "Generals of the Yang family".

fiction.zh: 楊家將小說戲曲中的佘太君、穆桂英、楊門女將等人物情節，多不見於正史。
fiction.en: She Taijun, Mu Guiying and the women warriors of the Yang house in novels and opera mostly do not appear in the histories.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百七十二 楊業傳
passages.textZh: 楊業，并州太原人。

summary.zh: 字平仲，華州下邽人，十九歲中進士。1004年遼軍大舉南下，朝臣多主張遷都避敵，時任宰相的寇準力勸宋真宗親征澶州，促成澶淵之盟。後遭王欽若、丁謂排擠，貶死雷州。
summary.en: Courtesy name Pingzhong, of Xiagui in Huazhou, who passed the examinations at nineteen. When the Liao invaded in force in 1004 and most of the court urged flight, Kou Zhun as chief minister pressed Emperor Zhenzong to go to the front at Chanzhou, leading to the Chanyuan treaty. Driven out by Wang Qinruo and Ding Wei, he died in exile at Leizhou.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百八十一 寇準傳
passages.textZh: 寇準，字平仲，華州下邽人也。

summary.zh: 字希文，蘇州吳縣人，兩歲喪父，母親改嫁朱家，他曾名朱說，苦讀成才。宋夏戰爭時與韓琦共同主持西北邊防，1043年主持慶曆新政。所作〈岳陽樓記〉有「先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂」之句。
summary.en: Courtesy name Xiwen, of Wu county in Suzhou. His father died when he was two and his mother remarried into the Zhu family, so he grew up as Zhu Yue, studying in poverty. In the war with Xi Xia he shared command of the northwest frontier with Han Qi, and in 1043 he led the Qingli reforms. His "Record of Yueyang Tower" holds the line "first to worry about the world's troubles, last to enjoy its pleasures".

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百一十四 范仲淹傳
passages.textZh: 范仲淹字希文，唐宰相履冰之後。其先邠州人也，後徙家江南，遂為蘇州吳縣人。

summary.zh: 字希仁，廬州合肥人。為官清廉剛正，任開封知府時大開正門，讓百姓直接陳訴，京師人說：「關節不到，有閻羅包老。」
summary.en: Courtesy name Xiren, of Hefei in Luzhou, an incorruptible and unbending official. As prefect of Kaifeng he opened the main gate so that people could bring their complaints straight to him; the capital said: "No back-door dealings get through — there's King Yama Old Bao."

fiction.zh: 戲曲小說中「包青天」日斷陽、夜斷陰，以及鍘美案、狸貓換太子、三俠五義等故事，均為後世創作。
fiction.en: The "Judge Bao" of opera and fiction — judging the living by day and the dead by night, the Chen Shimei case, the "civet cat for the crown prince" plot, the Three Heroes and Five Gallants — is a later creation.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百一十六 包拯傳
passages.textZh: 包拯，字希仁，廬州合肥人也。

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百一十六 包拯傳
passages.textZh: 京師為之語曰：「關節不到，有閻羅包老。」

summary.zh: 字永叔，廬陵人，四歲喪父，母親以荻草畫地教他識字。北宋文壇領袖，推動古文運動，主持科舉時拔擢蘇軾、蘇轍、曾鞏等人，參與編撰《新唐書》，獨撰《新五代史》。
summary.en: Courtesy name Yongshu, of Luling. His father died when he was four, and his mother taught him to write with reeds in the dirt. Leader of letters in the Northern Song and champion of the ancient-prose movement, he passed Su Shi, Su Zhe and Zeng Gong as chief examiner, helped compile the New Book of Tang and wrote the New History of the Five Dynasties alone.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百一十九 歐陽脩傳
passages.textZh: 歐陽脩，字永叔，廬陵人。四歲而孤，母鄭，守節自誓，親誨之學，家貧，至以荻畫地學書。

summary.zh: 字君實，陝州夏縣人。七歲時聽人講《左氏春秋》便能為家人複述大意。反對王安石變法，退居洛陽十五年主編《資治通鑑》。1085年哲宗即位後入朝為相，盡廢新法，次年去世。
summary.en: Courtesy name Junshi, of Xia county in Shanzhou. At seven he could retell to his family the gist of the Zuo Tradition after hearing it read. He opposed Wang Anshi's reforms and spent fifteen years in retirement at Luoyang compiling the Comprehensive Mirror. When Zhezong came to the throne in 1085 he returned as chief minister, abolished the New Laws, and died the next year.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百三十六 司馬光傳
passages.textZh: 司馬光，字君實，陝州夏縣人也。

summary.zh: 字存中，錢塘人，北宋科學家、政治家。參與王安石變法，出使遼國、主持西北邊防。晚年隱居潤州夢溪園，撰《夢溪筆談》，記載了畢昇發明活字印刷、指南針的磁偏角、「石油」之名等大量科技內容。
summary.en: Courtesy name Cunzhong, of Qiantang, scientist and statesman of the Northern Song. He took part in Wang Anshi's reforms, went as envoy to the Liao and commanded on the northwest frontier. In retirement at his Mengxi garden in Runzhou he wrote the Brush Talks from Dream Brook, which records Bi Sheng's movable type, the magnetic declination of the compass needle, the name "rock oil" and much else.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百三十一 沈遘傳 附從弟括
passages.textZh: 括，字存中，以父任為沭陽主簿。

summary.zh: 字漢臣，汾州西河人，出身行伍，臉上刺有軍人的金印。宋夏戰爭中常披髮戴銅面具衝鋒陷陣。1053年夜奪崑崙關，平定儂智高，官至樞密使，因武將身份遭文臣猜忌而罷職。
summary.en: Courtesy name Hanchen, of Xihe in Fenzhou, a common soldier with the army brand still tattooed on his face. In the war with Xi Xia he charged with his hair loose under a bronze mask. In 1053 he took the Kunlun pass by night and put down Nong Zhigao, rising to head the Bureau of Military Affairs, until the civil officials' distrust of a soldier drove him from office.

label.en: head of the Bureau of Military Affairs

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百九十 狄青傳
passages.textZh: 狄青，字漢臣，汾州西河人。

summary.zh: 字元長，興化仙遊人，書法家。宋徽宗時四度為相，打著繼承新法的旗號排斥異己，立「元祐黨人碑」，搜刮民財供徽宗揮霍，被太學生陳東列為「六賊」之首。欽宗即位後被貶，死於途中。
summary.en: Courtesy name Yuanchang, of Xianyou in Xinghua, a calligrapher. Four times chief minister under Huizong, he purged his enemies in the name of the New Laws, set up the stele of the "Yuanyou faction", and squeezed the people to pay for the emperor's extravagance; the student Chen Dong named him first of the "Six Traitors". Banished when Qinzong came to the throne, he died on the road.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百七十二 姦臣傳 蔡京
passages.textZh: 蔡京，字元長，興化仙遊人。

summary.zh: 名趙佶，宋神宗第十一子，1100年即位。書畫造詣極高，創「瘦金體」，主持編撰《宣和畫譜》，但寵信蔡京、童貫等人，大興「花石綱」，聯金滅遼反招金兵南下。1125年禪位，靖康之變被俘，死於五國城。
summary.en: Zhao Ji, eleventh son of Emperor Shenzong, who came to the throne in 1100. A superb painter and calligrapher, inventor of the "slender gold" script and patron of the Xuanhe painting catalogue, he trusted Cai Jing and Tong Guan, ran the "flower and rock convoys", and allied with the Jin against the Liao only to bring the Jin down on himself. He abdicated in 1125, was captured in the Jingkang disaster and died at Wuguocheng in the far northeast.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷十九 徽宗紀一
passages.textZh: 諱佶，神宗第十一子也

summary.zh: 字良臣，延安人，家貧嗜酒，出身行伍。參與平定方臘，苗劉兵變時率軍勤王，1130年在黃天蕩以少數水軍困住金軍四十八日。與岳飛同為南宋中興名將，岳飛被害時當面質問秦檜，此後辭官閉門不出。
summary.en: Courtesy name Liangchen, of Yan'an, a poor, hard-drinking common soldier. He fought against Fang La, marched to Gaozong's rescue in the Miao–Liu mutiny, and in 1130 bottled up the Jin army in the Huangtiandang marsh for forty-eight days. One of the great generals of the Southern Song revival with Yue Fei, he confronted Qin Hui to his face over Yue Fei's death and then retired behind closed doors.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十四 韓世忠傳
passages.textZh: 韓世忠字良臣，延安人。風骨偉岸，目瞬如電。

summary.zh: 字會之，江寧人。靖康之變時被俘北去，1130年南歸，自稱殺死看守逃回，當時就有人懷疑。宋高宗時兩度為相，主持與金議和，1141年以「莫須有」的罪名殺害岳飛，簽訂紹興和議。專權十九年。
summary.en: Courtesy name Huizhi, of Jiangning. Carried north in the Jingkang disaster, he came back in 1130 claiming to have killed his guards and escaped — a story doubted even then. Twice chief minister under Gaozong, he drove the peace with the Jin, had Yue Fei killed in 1141 on a charge of "perhaps", signed the Shaoxing treaty and held power for nineteen years.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百七十三 姦臣傳 秦檜
passages.textZh: 秦檜，字會之，江寧人。登政和五年第，補密州教授。

summary.zh: 字元晦，一字仲晦，徽州婺源人（生於福建尤溪）。集理學之大成，撰《四書章句集注》，元代以後成為科舉的標準教材。晚年在慶元黨禁中被斥為「偽學」之首，死後才得平反。
summary.en: Courtesy name Yuanhui or Zhonghui, of Wuyuan in Huizhou (born at Youxi in Fujian). He brought Neo-Confucianism to its synthesis; his Collected Commentaries on the Four Books became the standard text of the examinations from the Yuan on. In his last years he was condemned as chief of the "false learning" in the Qingyuan ban, and rehabilitated only after his death.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百二十九 道學傳 朱熹
passages.textZh: 朱熹，字元晦，一字仲晦，徽州婺源人。

summary.zh: 字務觀，號放翁，越州山陰人。十二歲能作詩文，參加禮部考試時名列秦檜之孫之前，被秦檜黜落。一生主張抗金收復中原，存詩九千餘首，絕筆〈示兒〉有「王師北定中原日，家祭無忘告乃翁」之句。
summary.en: Courtesy name Wuguan, art name Fangweng, of Shanyin in Yuezhou. He wrote poetry at twelve; when he ranked above Qin Hui's grandson in the examinations, Qin Hui had him failed. All his life he called for war to recover the north; more than nine thousand of his poems survive, and his last, "To My Son", asks that when the royal armies retake the Central Plain the family not forget to tell him at the ancestral sacrifice.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百九十五 陸游傳
passages.textZh: 陸游字務觀，山陰人。年十二能詩文，蔭補登仕郎。鎖廳薦送第一，秦檜孫塤適居其次，檜怒，至罪主司。

summary.zh: 字幼安，號稼軒，齊州歷城人，生於金朝統治下的北方。二十二歲聚眾抗金，曾率五十餘騎闖入五萬人的金營擒拿叛徒張安國南歸。南歸後長期不得重用，以詞抒發壯志，與蘇軾並稱「蘇辛」。
summary.en: Courtesy name You'an, art name Jiaxuan, of Licheng in Qizhou, born in the north under Jin rule. At twenty-two he raised a band against the Jin and once rode with fifty men into a camp of fifty thousand to seize the traitor Zhang Anguo and bring him south. In the south he was long kept from real command and poured his ambitions into lyrics; with Su Shi he is paired as "Su and Xin".

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百零一 辛棄疾傳
passages.textZh: 辛棄疾字幼安，齊之歷城人。

confidenceNote.zh: 卒年約在1155年後，確切年份不詳。
confidenceNote.en: She died some time after about 1155; the exact year is unknown.

summary.zh: 號易安居士，齊州章丘人，李格非之女，嫁趙明誠，夫婦共同收集金石，撰成《金石錄》。靖康之變後流寓江南，丈夫病逝，晚景淒涼。其詞前期清麗、後期悲苦，被推為婉約派詞人之宗。
summary.en: Art name Yi'an Jushi, of Zhangqiu in Qizhou, daughter of Li Gefei, wife of Zhao Mingcheng, with whom she collected bronze and stone inscriptions for the Records of Metal and Stone. After the Jingkang disaster she drifted south, her husband died, and her last years were bleak. Her lyrics, bright when young and grief-stricken later, make her the foremost poet of the "delicate" school.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百四十四 文苑傳 李格非 附女清照
passages.textZh: 女清照，詩文尤有稱于時，嫁趙挺之之子明誠，自號「易安居士」

summary.zh: 字師憲，台州人，制置使賈涉之子，因姊姊為宋理宗貴妃而得重用。1259年鄂州之戰私下向忽必烈求和，卻謊報大捷，此後專權十餘年，推行公田法。襄陽被圍數年不救，1275年丁家洲兵敗，被貶後在漳州木綿庵被押送官鄭虎臣所殺。
summary.en: Courtesy name Shixian, of Taizhou, son of the commissioner Jia She, who rose because his sister was Emperor Lizong's favourite consort. In 1259 at Ezhou he secretly sued Khubilai for peace while reporting a great victory, then held power for more than ten years, imposing the public-fields scheme. He left Xiangyang besieged for years without relief, was routed at Dingjiazhou in 1275, banished, and killed at Muyan temple in Zhangzhou by his escort Zheng Huchen.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百七十四 姦臣傳 賈似道
passages.textZh: 賈似道，字師憲，台州人，制置使涉之子也。

confidenceNote.zh: 設關年代不詳；此以孟嘗君事（約前299）為始見。遺址在今河南靈寶市函谷關鎮王垛村一帶；《元和郡縣圖志》記在唐靈寶縣南十里（卷六）或西南十一里（卷二）。
confidenceNote.en: When the pass was built is unknown; it is drawn from the Lord Mengchang episode (c. 299 BCE), its first appearance here. The site is at Wangduo village, Lingbao, Henan; the Yuanhe Gazetteer puts it ten li south (juan 6) or eleven li south-west (juan 2) of Tang Lingbao.

summary.zh: 秦的函谷關。齊孟嘗君自秦逃歸，夜半至函谷關，關法雞鳴方出客，門客學雞鳴，得以出關。漢武帝元鼎三年（前114）徙關於新安，以故關為弘農縣；唐人稱此地為函谷故城，即秦函谷關城、漢弘農縣。
summary.en: The Qin Hangu Pass. Lord Mengchang of Qi, escaping from Qin, reached Hangu Pass at midnight; the rule was to let travellers out only at cockcrow, and a retainer who could crow like a cock got him through. In 114 BCE Emperor Wu of Han moved the pass to Xin'an and made the old pass Hongnong county; Tang writers called the site the old Hangu city — the Qin pass-city and Han Hongnong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十五 孟嘗君列傳
passages.textZh: 夜半至函谷關。秦昭王後悔出孟嘗君，求之已去，即使人馳傳逐之。孟嘗君至關，關法鷄鳴而出客，孟嘗君恐追至，客之居下坐者有能爲鷄鳴，而鷄齊鳴，遂發傳出。
passages.textEn: At midnight he reached Hangu Pass. King Zhao of Qin regretted letting him go, found him gone and sent riders after him. At the pass the rule was to let travellers out at cockcrow; fearing pursuit, Lord Mengchang had a retainer from the lowest seats crow like a cock — all the cocks crowed, and the pass let him through.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀 元鼎三年
passages.textZh: 三年冬，徙函谷關於新安。以故關為弘農縣。
passages.textEn: In the winter of the third year [of Yuanding, 114 BCE] Hangu Pass was moved to Xin'an, and the old pass made Hongnong county.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷六 河南道二 陝州靈寶縣
passages.textZh: 函谷故城，在縣南十里。秦函谷關城，漢弘農縣也。
passages.textEn: The old Hangu city, ten li south of the county: the Qin pass-city of Hangu, Han Hongnong county.

confidenceNote.zh: 遺址在今河南新安縣城東；唐記在新安縣東一里。下限210年取《元和郡縣圖志》所推潼關代興之時，並非此關廢止之年。
confidenceNote.en: The site is just east of Xin'an, Henan. The end date (210) follows the Yuanhe Gazetteer's dating of Tong Pass taking over; it is not when this pass was abandoned.

summary.zh: 漢武帝元鼎三年（前114），樓船將軍楊僕恥居關外，上疏請以家僮七百人徙函谷關於新安，武帝從之。東漢中平元年（184）置八關都尉，函谷為八關之一。據《元和郡縣圖志》考證，初平二年（191）董卓挾獻帝西遷，出函谷關，此前關皆在新安；至建安十六年（211）曹操破馬超已在潼關，關址當於其間西移。
summary.en: In 114 BCE the general Yang Pu, ashamed to live "outside the pass", asked to move Hangu Pass to Xin'an with seven hundred of his own household men, and Emperor Wu agreed. In 184 commandants were set over Eight Passes around Luoyang, Hangu among them. The Yuanhe Gazetteer argues that the pass was still at Xin'an when Dong Zuo dragged Emperor Xian west in 191, and that by 211, when Cao Cao beat Ma Chao, the gate had moved west to Tong Pass.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀 元鼎三年
passages.textZh: 三年冬，徙函谷關於新安。以故關為弘農縣。
passages.textEn: In the winter of the third year [of Yuanding, 114 BCE] Hangu Pass was moved to Xin'an, and the old pass made Hongnong county.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 華州華陰縣 潼關條
passages.textZh: 漢武帝元鼎三年，楊僕為樓船將軍，本宜陽人，恥居關外，上疏請以家僮七百人徙關於新安，武帝從之，即今新安縣東一里函谷故關是也。而郵傳所馳，出於南路，至後漢獻帝初平二年，董卓脅帝西幸長安，出函谷關，自此已前，其關並在新安。其後二十年，至建安十六年，曹公破馬超於潼關，則是中間徙於今所。
passages.textEn: In 114 BCE Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, a man of Yiyang ashamed to live outside the pass, asked to move it to Xin'an with seven hundred of his household men; Emperor Wu agreed — this is the old Hangu Pass one li east of Xin'an today. In 191 Dong Zhuo forced Emperor Xian west to Chang'an through Hangu Pass, so until then the pass was at Xin'an. Twenty years later, in 211, Cao Cao beat Ma Chao at Tong Pass: so it moved to its present place in between.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀 中平元年
passages.textZh: 三月戊申，以河南尹何進爲大將軍，將兵屯都亭。置八關都尉官。
passages.textEn: On wushen of the third month He Jin, Intendant of Henan, was made General-in-Chief and camped with troops at Duting. Commandants of the Eight Passes were appointed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han, Li Xian's commentary (676)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀 中平元年 李賢注
passages.textZh: 八關謂函谷、廣城、伊闕、大谷、轘轅、旋門、小平津、孟津也。
passages.textEn: The Eight Passes are Hangu, Guangcheng, Yique, Dagu, Huanyuan, Xuanmen, Xiaopingjin and Mengjin.

note.en: identified with it by Tang geographers

confidenceNote.zh: 始見於建安十六年（211）。唐潼關在華陰縣東北三十九里；此取今陝西潼關縣港口一帶的約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded in 211. Tang Tong Pass lay 39 li north-east of Huayin; the point is near Gangkou, Tongguan county, Shaanxi.

summary.zh: 漢末代函谷關而起。據《元和郡縣圖志》，初平二年（191）關尚在新安，建安十六年（211）曹操破馬超已在潼關。其地即古桃林塞，關西一里有潼水，因以名關。天寶十四載（755）安祿山陷東京，封常清勸高仙芝棄陝州，「急保潼關」。
summary.en: Tong Pass took over from Hangu at the end of Han: by the Yuanhe Gazetteer's reckoning the pass was still at Xin'an in 191 and at Tong by 211, when Cao Cao beat Ma Chao there. The Tang identified it with the ancient Taolin barrier; it took its name from the Tong stream a li to its west. When An Lushan took Luoyang in 755, Feng Changqing urged Gao Xianzhi to give up Shanzhou and "hurry to hold Tong Pass".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 魏書一 武帝紀 建安十六年
passages.textZh: 超等屯潼關，公勑諸將：「關西兵精悍，堅壁勿與戰。」
passages.textEn: Ma Chao and the others camped at Tong Pass. Cao Cao ordered his generals: "The troops west of the pass are fierce; keep behind your walls and do not fight them."

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 華州華陰縣
passages.textZh: 潼關，在縣東北三十九里，古桃林塞也，春秋時晉侯使詹嘉處瑕以守桃林之塞是也。關西一里有潼水，因以名關。
passages.textEn: Tong Pass, 39 li north-east of the county: the ancient Taolin barrier, which in the Spring and Autumn period the lord of Jin had Zhan Jia hold from Xia. A li west of the pass is the Tong stream, which gives it its name.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 華州華陰縣 潼關條
passages.textZh: 至後漢獻帝初平二年，董卓脅帝西幸長安，出函谷關，自此已前，其關並在新安。其後二十年，至建安十六年，曹公破馬超於潼關，則是中間徙於今所。
passages.textEn: In 191 Dong Zhuo forced Emperor Xian west to Chang'an through Hangu Pass, so until then the pass was at Xin'an. Twenty years later, in 211, Cao Cao beat Ma Chao at Tong Pass: so it moved to its present place in between.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百四 高仙芝傳 天寶十四載
passages.textZh: 十三日，祿山陷東京，常清以餘眾奔陜州，謂仙芝曰：「累日血戰，賊鋒不可當。且潼關無兵，若狂寇奔突，則京師危矣。宜棄此守，急保潼關。」
passages.textEn: On the thirteenth An Lushan took the Eastern Capital. Feng Changqing fled with what was left to Shanzhou and told Gao Xianzhi: "We have fought for days and cannot stop them. Tong Pass has no troops; if the rebels break through, the capital is lost. Give up this post and hurry to hold Tong Pass."

confidenceNote.zh: 此以楚懷王入秦（前299）為始見。遺址在今陝西丹鳳縣武關鎮。
confidenceNote.en: Drawn from King Huai's journey (299 BCE), its first appearance here. The site is Wuguan town, Danfeng county, Shaanxi.

summary.zh: 秦昭王致書楚懷王，約會於武關；昭王伏兵武關，詐稱秦王，懷王至則閉關，劫之西至咸陽。漢時南陽郡治宛「西通武關，東受江、淮」。
summary.en: King Zhao of Qin invited King Huai of Chu to meet him at Wu Pass, posted troops there under a general posing as the king, shut the pass behind Huai and carried him off to Xianyang. In Han times Wan, seat of Nanyang, "reaches Wu Pass to the west and the Yangzi and Huai to the east".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十 楚世家 懷王三十年
passages.textZh: 寡人願與君王會武關，面相約，結盟而去，寡人之願也。
passages.textEn: It is my wish to meet Your Majesty at Wu Pass, agree face to face and swear a covenant.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十 楚世家 懷王三十年
passages.textZh: 昭王詐令一將軍伏兵武關，號爲秦王。楚王至，則閉武關，遂與西至咸陽，朝章臺，如蕃臣，不與亢禮。
passages.textEn: King Zhao had a general lie in wait at Wu Pass calling himself the king of Qin. When the king of Chu arrived they shut Wu Pass and took him west to Xianyang, where he was received at the Zhang terrace like a vassal, not as an equal.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷二十八 地理志 南陽
passages.textZh: 宛，西通武關，東受江、淮，一都之會也。
passages.textEn: Wan reaches Wu Pass to the west and takes in the Yangzi and Huai to the east: a meeting place of the realm.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以建安二十年（215）為始見。關在秦嶺北坡清姜河谷，今陝西寶雞市南；此為約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded here in 215. The pass is in the Qingjiang valley on the north face of the Qinling, south of Baoji, Shaanxi; the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 建安二十年（215）四月，曹操西征張魯，自陳倉出散關，至河池。《元和郡縣圖志》記散關在陳倉縣西南五十二里，並引諸葛亮出散關圍陳倉事。
summary.en: In the fourth month of 215 Cao Cao, marching on Zhang Lu, went out from Chencang through San Pass to Hechi. The Yuanhe Gazetteer puts the pass 52 li south-west of Chencang and recalls Zhuge Liang coming out through it to besiege Chencang.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 魏書一 武帝紀 建安二十年
passages.textZh: 夏四月，公自陳倉以出散關，至河池。
passages.textEn: In the summer, fourth month, Cao Cao went out from Chencang through San Pass to Hechi.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 鳳翔府陳倉縣
passages.textZh: 散關，在縣西南五十二里。《蜀志》諸葛亮出散關圍陳倉。
passages.textEn: San Pass, 52 li south-west of the county. The Shu records: Zhuge Liang came out through San Pass to besiege Chencang.

confidenceNote.zh: 北周（557–581）所置，確年不詳，此從北周建國之年起繪。約址在今陝西隴縣西、隴山東坡。
confidenceNote.en: Built under the Northern Zhou (557–581), year unknown; drawn from 557. Approximately west of Long county, Shaanxi, on the eastern slope of the Long range.

summary.zh: 《元和郡縣圖志》記大震關在隴州西六十一里，後周所置；相傳漢武帝至此遇雷震，因以為名。
summary.en: The Yuanhe Gazetteer puts Dazhen Pass 61 li west of Longzhou, built under the (Northern) Zhou, and says it was named for a thunderclap that met Emperor Wu of Han there.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 隴州汧源縣
passages.textZh: 大震關，在州西六十一里。後周置。漢武至此遇雷震，因名。
passages.textEn: Dazhen Pass, 61 li west of the prefecture. Built under the Zhou. Emperor Wu of Han met a thunderclap here, hence the name.

confidenceNote.zh: 唐人記在平高縣（今寧夏固原）東南三十里；今人比定不一，此取約址，誤差可達二十餘公里。宋代另有同名的蕭關，不在此處。
confidenceNote.en: The Tang put it 30 li south-east of Pinggao (today Guyuan, Ningxia); modern identifications differ, so the point may be twenty-odd km off. A Song-era Xiao Pass was a different place.

summary.zh: 漢文帝十四年（前166），匈奴單于以十四萬騎入朝那、蕭關，殺北地都尉，擄掠人畜，燒回中宮，候騎至雍、甘泉。《元和郡縣圖志》記蕭關故城在原州平高縣東南三十里。
summary.en: In 166 BCE the Xiongnu chanyu came in through Chaona and Xiao Pass with 140,000 horsemen, killed the commandant of Beidi, carried off people and herds, burned the Huizhong palace and sent scouts as far as Yong and Ganquan. The Yuanhe Gazetteer puts the old Xiao Pass city 30 li south-east of Pinggao, seat of Yuanzhou.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十 匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 漢孝文皇帝十四年，匈奴單于十四萬騎入朝那、蕭關，殺北地都尉卬，虜人民畜產甚多，遂至彭陽。使奇兵入燒回中宮，候騎至雍甘泉。
passages.textEn: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen of Han the chanyu came in through Chaona and Xiao Pass with 140,000 horsemen, killed Ang, commandant of Beidi, carried off many people and animals and reached Pengyang. A flying column burned the Huizhong palace; scouts reached Yong and Ganquan.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷三 關內道三 原州平高縣
passages.textZh: 蕭關故城，在縣東南三十里。《漢書》文帝十四年，匈奴入蕭關，殺北地都尉，是也。
