passages.textEn: The old Xiao Pass city, 30 li south-east of the county: where, the Book of Han says, the Xiongnu came in through Xiao Pass in the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen and killed the commandant of Beidi.

confidenceNote.zh: 天然渡口，全時段繪出。約址在今陝西大荔縣朝邑與山西永濟市蒲州之間的黃河兩岸；河道屢有擺動。
confidenceNote.en: A natural crossing, drawn for the whole period. Approximately between Chaoyi (Dali, Shaanxi) and Puzhou (Yongji, Shanxi); the river has shifted repeatedly.

summary.zh: 黃河渡口，唐人稱其河橋「通秦、晉之道」。漢二年（前205）魏王豹盛兵蒲阪、塞臨晉，韓信陳船佯渡臨晉，而從夏陽以木罌缻渡軍，襲安邑。建安十六年（211）曹操與馬超相持於潼關，潛遣徐晃、朱靈夜渡蒲阪津，據河西為營。唐朝邑縣（漢臨晉縣地）西南有蒲津關。
summary.en: The Yellow River crossing that, as the Tang put it, "joins the roads of Qin and Jin". In 205 BCE King Bao of Wei massed troops at Puban and blocked Linjin; Han Xin lined up boats as if to cross at Linjin while his men crossed upstream at Xiayang on wooden jars and fell on Anyi. In 211, facing Ma Chao at Tong Pass, Cao Cao sent Xu Huang and Zhu Ling across the Puban ford by night to camp west of the river. In Tang times Pujin Pass stood south-west of Chaoyi, once Han Linjin.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十二 淮陰侯列傳
passages.textZh: 魏王盛兵蒲阪，塞臨晉，信乃益爲疑兵，陳船欲度臨晉，而伏兵從夏陽以木罌缻渡軍，襲安邑。
passages.textEn: The king of Wei massed troops at Puban and blocked Linjin. Han Xin set up decoys, lining up boats as if to cross at Linjin, while hidden troops crossed at Xiayang on wooden jars and fell on Anyi.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 魏書一 武帝紀 建安十六年
passages.textZh: 公急持之，而潛遣徐晃、朱靈等夜渡蒲阪津，據河西爲營。
passages.textEn: Cao Cao held them hard in front while secretly sending Xu Huang, Zhu Ling and others across the Puban ford by night to make camp west of the river.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 同州朝邑縣
passages.textZh: 本漢臨晉縣地。大荔國在今縣東三十步，故王城是也。後魏置南五泉縣，西魏改為朝邑縣，以北據朝阪，故以為名。縣西南有蒲津關。
passages.textEn: Once the land of Han Linjin county. The old Dali kingdom lay thirty paces east of the present county, its royal city. The Northern Wei set up Nanwuquan county, which the Western Wei renamed Chaoyi for the Chao slope to its north. South-west of the county is Pujin Pass.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷二 關內道二 同州朝邑縣
passages.textZh: 河橋，本秦后子奔晉，造舟於河，通秦、晉之道，今屬河西縣。
passages.textEn: The river bridge began when Prince Hou of Qin fled to Jin and made a pontoon over the river, joining the roads of Qin and Jin; it now belongs to Hexi county.

confidenceNote.zh: 從築城之年（前571）起繪。故地在今河南滎陽市汜水鎮西。
confidenceNote.en: Drawn from its walling in 571 BCE. The site is west of Sishui town, Xingyang, Henan.

summary.zh: 魯襄公二年（前571），諸侯會於戚，孟獻子請「城虎牢以偪鄭」，遂城虎牢，鄭人乃與晉和。楚漢相爭時，酈食其勸劉邦「塞成皋之險」。唐汜水縣即鄭之制邑、漢之成皋縣，一名虎牢。
summary.en: In 571 BCE, at a meeting of the lords at Qi, Meng Xianzi proposed "walling Hulao to press Zheng"; Hulao was walled and Zheng made peace with Jin. In the war of Chu and Han, Li Yiji urged Liu Bang to "block the defile of Chenggao". Tang Sishui county was Zheng's Zhi and Han's Chenggao, also called Hulao.

passages.sourceEn: Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan, 4th c. BCE)
passages.locator: 襄公二年
passages.textZh: 孟獻子曰．請城虎牢以偪鄭．
passages.textEn: Meng Xianzi said: let us wall Hulao to press Zheng.

passages.sourceEn: Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan, 4th c. BCE)
passages.locator: 襄公二年
passages.textZh: 冬．復會于戚．齊崔武子．及滕薛小邾之大夫皆會．知武子之言故也．遂城虎牢．鄭人乃成．
passages.textEn: In winter they met again at Qi; Cui Wuzi of Qi and the officers of Teng, Xue and Little Zhu all came, as Zhi Wuzi had said they would. Then they walled Hulao, and Zheng made peace.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十七 酈生陸賈列傳
passages.textZh: 收取滎陽，據敖倉之粟，塞成皋之險，杜大行之道，距蜚狐之口，守白馬之津，以示諸侯效實形制之勢，則天下知所歸矣。
passages.textEn: Take Xingyang, hold the grain of the Ao granary, block the defile of Chenggao, close the Taihang road, guard the mouth of Feihu and hold the White Horse ford: show the lords where real strength lies, and the realm will know whom to follow.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷五 河南道一 河南府汜水縣
passages.textZh: 古東虢國，鄭之制邑，漢之成皋縣，一名虎牢。
passages.textEn: The ancient Eastern Guo, Zheng's town of Zhi, Han's Chenggao county, also called Hulao.

confidenceNote.zh: 天然山道，全時段繪出。約址在今河南偃師與登封之間的轘轅山。
confidenceNote.en: A natural mountain road, drawn for the whole period. Approximately on Mount Huanyuan between Yanshi and Dengfeng, Henan.

summary.zh: 魯襄公二十一年（前552），晉欒盈出奔過周，周王「使候出諸轘轅」。舊注：緱氏縣東南有轘轅關，道路險隘，凡十二曲，將去復還，故名。東漢末何進所置八關之一。
summary.en: In 552 BCE, when Luan Ying of Jin fled through Zhou, the king had him escorted out "by way of Huanyuan". An old note says Huanyuan Pass lay south-east of Goushi, a narrow road of twelve turns that seems to double back on itself — hence the name. One of the Eight Passes set up under He Jin at the end of Eastern Han.

passages.sourceEn: Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan, 4th c. BCE)
passages.locator: 襄公二十一年
passages.textZh: 使司徒禁掠欒氏者．歸所取焉．使候出諸轘轅．
passages.textEn: He had the minister of the masses stop those plundering the Luan party and return what they had taken, and had an escort see them out by Huanyuan.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷五 河南道一 河南府緱氏縣
passages.textZh: 轘轅山，在縣東南四十六里。《左傳》「欒盈過周，王使候出諸轘轅」。注曰：「緱氏縣東南有轘轅關，道路險隘，凡十二曲，將去復還，故曰轘轅。」後漢河南尹何進所置八關，此其一也。
passages.textEn: Mount Huanyuan, 46 li south-east of the county. The Zuozhuan: "When Luan Ying passed through Zhou, the king had an escort see him out by Huanyuan." A note says: "South-east of Goushi is Huanyuan Pass, a narrow road of twelve turns that seems to come back as it goes, hence Huanyuan." It was one of the Eight Passes set up by He Jin, Intendant of Henan, under the Later Han.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀 中平元年
passages.textZh: 三月戊申，以河南尹何進爲大將軍，將兵屯都亭。置八關都尉官。
passages.textEn: On wushen of the third month He Jin, Intendant of Henan, was made General-in-Chief and camped with troops at Duting. Commandants of the Eight Passes were appointed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han, Li Xian's commentary (676)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀 中平元年 李賢注
passages.textZh: 八關謂函谷、廣城、伊闕、大谷、轘轅、旋門、小平津、孟津也。
passages.textEn: The Eight Passes are Hangu, Guangcheng, Yique, Dagu, Huanyuan, Xuanmen, Xiaopingjin and Mengjin.

confidenceNote.zh: 伊水穿山的峽口，今河南洛陽市南龍門，全時段繪出。
confidenceNote.en: The gorge of the Yi river at Longmen, south of Luoyang; drawn for the whole period.

summary.zh: 秦昭王十四年（前293），白起攻韓、魏於伊闕，斬首二十四萬，虜其將公孫喜，拔五城。東漢中平元年（184）置八關都尉，伊闕為其一。隋煬帝營東京，宮城北據邙山，「南直伊闕之口」；煬帝登邙山望伊闕，曰：「此非龍門邪？」
summary.en: In 293 BCE Bai Qi attacked Han and Wei at Yique, took 240,000 heads, captured their general Gongsun Xi and seized five cities. In 184 it became one of the Eight Passes guarding Luoyang. Emperor Yang of Sui built his Eastern Capital with Mount Mang behind it and the palace "facing the mouth of Yique"; looking at the gorge from Mount Mang he had asked, "Is this not a Dragon Gate?"

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十三 白起王翦列傳
passages.textZh: 其明年，白起為左更，攻韓、魏於伊闕，斬首二十四萬，又虜其將公孫喜，拔五城。
passages.textEn: The next year Bai Qi, now of the Zuogeng rank, attacked Han and Wei at Yique, took 240,000 heads, captured their general Gongsun Xi and seized five cities.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀 中平元年
passages.textZh: 三月戊申，以河南尹何進爲大將軍，將兵屯都亭。置八關都尉官。
passages.textEn: On wushen of the third month He Jin, Intendant of Henan, was made General-in-Chief and camped with troops at Duting. Commandants of the Eight Passes were appointed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han, Li Xian's commentary (676)
passages.locator: 卷八 孝靈帝紀 中平元年 李賢注
passages.textZh: 八關謂函谷、廣城、伊闕、大谷、轘轅、旋門、小平津、孟津也。
passages.textEn: The Eight Passes are Hangu, Guangcheng, Yique, Dagu, Huanyuan, Xuanmen, Xiaopingjin and Mengjin.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷五 河南道一 河南府
passages.textZh: 其宮北據邙山，南直伊闕之口，洛水貫都，有河漢之象，東去故城一十八里。初，煬帝嘗登邙山，觀伊闕，顧曰：「此非龍門邪？自古何因不建都於此？」
passages.textEn: The palace has Mount Mang behind it to the north and faces the mouth of Yique to the south; the Luo runs through the city like the Milky Way; it lies 18 li west of the old city. Emperor Yang once climbed Mount Mang, looked at Yique and said: "Is this not a Dragon Gate? Why has no one built a capital here?"

note.en: Tang name of its eastern mouth

confidenceNote.zh: 井陘是長數十公里的山道，此點取東口井陘口（唐土門口，今河北石家莊市鹿泉區西南）。天然隘道，全時段繪出。
confidenceNote.en: Jingxing is a mountain road tens of kilometres long; the point marks its eastern mouth (Tang Tumen, south-west of Luquan, Shijiazhuang). A natural defile, drawn for the whole period.

summary.zh: 《呂氏春秋》列為天下九塞之一，《述征記》稱為太行第五陘。楚漢之際，韓信、張耳以兵數萬東下井陘擊趙，陳餘聚兵井陘口，號稱二十萬；李左車說陳餘：「井陘之道，車不得方軌，騎不得成列。」唐時井陘口名土門口，在獲鹿縣西南十里，四面高、中央下，似井，故名。
summary.en: One of the nine great passes of the Lüshi chunqiu, and the fifth of the Taihang passes in the Shuzheng ji. In the Chu–Han war Han Xin and Zhang Er came east through Jingxing with a few tens of thousands to attack Zhao, and Chen Yu massed a reputed 200,000 at its mouth; Li Zuoche warned him that "on the Jingxing road carts cannot go two abreast, nor horsemen in rank". In Tang times its mouth was called Tumen, ten li south-west of Huolu: high on four sides and low in the middle, like a well (jing) — hence the name.

passages.sourceEn: Lüshi chunqiu (c. 239 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十三 有始覽
passages.textZh: 何謂九塞？大汾，冥阨，荊阮，方城，殽，井陘，令疵，句注，居庸。
passages.textEn: What are the nine passes (sai)? Dafen, Ming'e, Jingruan, Fangcheng, Xiao, Jingxing, Lingci, Gouzhu and Juyong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十二 淮陰侯列傳
passages.textZh: 信與張耳以兵數萬，欲東下井陘擊趙。趙王、成安君陳餘聞漢且襲之也，聚兵井陘口，號稱二十萬。
passages.textEn: Han Xin and Zhang Er, with a few tens of thousands, meant to go east down through Jingxing and attack Zhao. The king of Zhao and Chen Yu, Lord of Cheng'an, hearing of it, massed troops at the mouth of Jingxing, said to be 200,000.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十二 淮陰侯列傳
passages.textZh: 今井陘之道，車不得方軌，騎不得成列，行數百里，其勢糧食必在其後。
passages.textEn: On the Jingxing road carts cannot go two abreast nor horsemen in rank; over a march of hundreds of li their grain must trail behind them.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十七 河北道二 恆州獲鹿縣
passages.textZh: 井陘口，今名土門口，縣西南十里。即太行八陘之第五陘也，四面高，中央下，似井，故名
passages.textEn: The mouth of Jingxing, now called Tumen, ten li south-west of the county: the fifth of the eight Taihang passes; high on four sides and low in the middle, like a well, hence the name.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十六 河北道一 懷州河內縣
passages.textZh: 《述征記》曰太行山首始於河內，自河內北至幽州，凡百嶺，連亙十二州之界。有八陘：第一曰軹關陘，今屬河南府濟源縣，在縣理西十一里；第二太行陘，第三白陘，此兩陘今在河內；第四滏口陘，對鄴西；第五井陘；第六飛狐徑，一名望都關；第七蒲陰陘，此三陘在中山；第八軍都陘，在幽州。
passages.textEn: The Shuzheng ji says: the Taihang range starts in Henei and runs north to Youzhou, a hundred ridges across twelve prefectures. It has eight passes (xing): first the Zhiguan pass, now in Jiyuan county of Henan prefecture, eleven li west of the county seat; second the Taihang pass and third the Bai pass, both now in Henei; fourth the Fukou pass, facing west of Ye; fifth Jingxing; sixth the Feihu pass, also called Wangdu Pass; seventh the Puyin pass — these three in Zhongshan; eighth the Jundu pass, in Youzhou.

confidenceNote.zh: 天然隘道，全時段繪出。按唐濟源縣西十一里取約址，在今河南濟源市西。
confidenceNote.en: A natural pass, drawn for the whole period. Placed eleven li west of Tang Jiyuan, west of today's Jiyuan, Henan.

summary.zh: 太行八陘之第一陘（《述征記》，《元和郡縣圖志》引），唐時屬河南府濟源縣，在縣西十一里。
summary.en: The first of the eight Taihang passes in the Shuzheng ji (as quoted in the Yuanhe Gazetteer); in Tang times in Jiyuan county, eleven li west of the county seat.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十六 河北道一 懷州河內縣
passages.textZh: 《述征記》曰太行山首始於河內，自河內北至幽州，凡百嶺，連亙十二州之界。有八陘：第一曰軹關陘，今屬河南府濟源縣，在縣理西十一里；第二太行陘，第三白陘，此兩陘今在河內；第四滏口陘，對鄴西；第五井陘；第六飛狐徑，一名望都關；第七蒲陰陘，此三陘在中山；第八軍都陘，在幽州。

It has eight passes (xing): first the Zhiguan pass, now in Jiyuan county of Henan prefecture, eleven li west of the county seat; second the Taihang pass and third the Bai pass, both now in Henei; fourth the Fukou pass, facing west of Ye; fifth Jingxing; sixth the Feihu pass, also called Wangdu Pass; seventh the Puyin pass — these three in Zhongshan; eighth the Jundu pass, in Youzhou.

confidenceNote.en: A natural pass, drawn for the whole period. The point is its southern end, thirty li north-west of Tang Henei (Qinyang, Henan); the road climbs north toward Shangdang.

summary.zh: 太行八陘之第二陘。唐時在懷州河內縣西北三十里，闊三步，長四十里。
summary.en: The second of the eight Taihang passes. In Tang times thirty li north-west of Henei county in Huaizhou: three paces wide and forty li long.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十六 河北道一 懷州河內縣
passages.textZh: 太行徑，在縣西北三十里。連山中斷曰陘。
passages.textEn: The Taihang pass, thirty li north-west of the county. A break in a mountain chain is called a xing.

passages.textEn: The Taihang pass is three paces wide and forty li long.

confidenceNote.zh: 原文只說「在河內」。今人多比定於今河南輝縣西北通往山西陵川的山道，此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: The source says only "in Henei". Modern writers usually place it on the road from north-west of Huixian, Henan, up to Lingchuan, Shanxi; the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 太行八陘之第三陘；《述征記》謂與太行陘同在河內。
summary.en: The third of the eight Taihang passes; the Shuzheng ji puts it, like the Taihang pass, in Henei.

confidenceNote.en: A natural pass, drawn for the whole period. Approximately at the source of the Fuyang river, Fengfeng, Handan, Hebei.

summary.zh: 太行八陘之第四陘，在鄴城以西。
summary.en: The fourth of the eight Taihang passes, west of Ye.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)

confidenceNote.en: A natural defile, drawn for the whole period. Approximately the Feihu gorge between Laiyuan and Yu counties, Hebei.

summary.zh: 太行八陘之第六陘，一名望都關。楚漢之際，酈食其勸劉邦「距蜚狐之口」。晉咸寧元年（275）句注碑以盧龍、飛狐與句注並為北方之險。
summary.en: The sixth of the eight Taihang passes, also called Wangdu Pass. In the Chu–Han war Li Yiji urged Liu Bang to "guard the mouth of Feihu". The Gouzhu stele of 275 names Lulong, Feihu and Gouzhu as the strongholds of the north.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷九十七 酈生陸賈列傳
passages.textZh: 收取滎陽，據敖倉之粟，塞成皋之險，杜大行之道，距蜚狐之口，守白馬之津，以示諸侯效實形制之勢，則天下知所歸矣。
passages.textEn: Take Xingyang, hold the grain of the Ao granary, block the defile of Chenggao, close the Taihang road, guard the mouth of Feihu and hold the White Horse ford: show the lords where real strength lies, and the realm will know whom to follow.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十四 河東道三 代州雁門縣
passages.textZh: 晉咸寧元年句注碑曰：「蓋北方之險，有盧龍、飛狐，句注為之首，天下之阻，所以分別內外也。」
passages.textEn: The Gouzhu stele of the first year of Xianning of Jin (275) says: "Of the strongholds of the north — Lulong, Feihu — Gouzhu is the chief: the barrier of the realm, which divides inside from outside."

note.zh: 今人多以為即後世紫荊關一帶
note.en: usually identified with the later Zijing Pass

confidenceNote.zh: 原文不記確址。今人多比定於今河北易縣西的紫荊關一帶，亦有異說；此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: The source gives no site. It is usually placed at Zijing Pass west of Yi county, Hebei, though not by everyone; the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 太行八陘之第七陘；《述征記》以井陘、飛狐、蒲陰三陘在中山。
summary.en: The seventh of the eight Taihang passes; the Shuzheng ji puts Jingxing, Feihu and Puyin "in Zhongshan".

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十六 河北道一 懷州河內縣

confidenceNote.zh: 天然隘道，全時段繪出。關溝在今北京市昌平區西北，此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: A natural defile, drawn for the whole period. The Guangou valley north-west of Changping, Beijing; the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 《呂氏春秋》天下九塞之一；《述征記》稱太行第八陘軍都陘，在幽州。
summary.en: One of the nine great passes of the Lüshi chunqiu; the Shuzheng ji calls it the Jundu pass, eighth of the Taihang passes, in Youzhou.

passages.sourceEn: Lüshi chunqiu (c. 239 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十三 有始覽
passages.textZh: 何謂九塞？大汾，冥阨，荊阮，方城，殽，井陘，令疵，句注，居庸。
passages.textEn: What are the nine passes (sai)? Dafen, Ming'e, Jingruan, Fangcheng, Xiao, Jingxing, Lingci, Gouzhu and Juyong.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十六 河北道一 懷州河內縣
passages.textZh: 《述征記》曰太行山首始於河內，自河內北至幽州，凡百嶺，連亙十二州之界。有八陘：第一曰軹關陘，今屬河南府濟源縣，在縣理西十一里；第二太行陘，第三白陘，此兩陘今在河內；第四滏口陘，對鄴西；第五井陘；第六飛狐徑，一名望都關；第七蒲陰陘，此三陘在中山；第八軍都陘，在幽州。
passages.textEn: The Shuzheng ji says: the Taihang range starts in Henei and runs north to Youzhou, a hundred ridges across twelve prefectures. It has eight passes (xing): first the Zhiguan pass, now in Jiyuan county of Henan prefecture, eleven li west of the county seat; second the Taihang pass and third the Bai pass, both now in Henei; fourth the Fukou pass, facing west of Ye; fifth Jingxing; sixth the Feihu pass, also called Wangdu Pass; seventh the Puyin pass — these three in Zhongshan; eighth the Jundu pass, in Youzhou.

confidenceNote.zh: 天然隘道，全時段繪出。在今山西代縣西北，後世雁門關一帶。
confidenceNote.en: A natural pass, drawn for the whole period. North-west of Dai county, Shanxi, around the later Yanmen Pass.

summary.zh: 《呂氏春秋》天下九塞之一。唐代州雁門縣西北的西陘山即句注山。晉咸寧元年（275）句注碑稱：「蓋北方之險，有盧龍、飛狐，句注為之首。」漢高祖欲伐匈奴，不從婁敬之說，逾句注，困於平城。
summary.en: One of the nine great passes of the Lüshi chunqiu. Mount Xixing, north-west of Yanmen county in Tang Daizhou, is Mount Gouzhu. The Gouzhu stele of 275 says: "Of the strongholds of the north — Lulong, Feihu — Gouzhu is the chief." Emperor Gaozu of Han, ignoring Lou Jing's warning, crossed Gouzhu to attack the Xiongnu and was trapped at Pingcheng.

passages.sourceEn: Lüshi chunqiu (c. 239 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十三 有始覽
passages.textZh: 何謂九塞？大汾，冥阨，荊阮，方城，殽，井陘，令疵，句注，居庸。
passages.textEn: What are the nine passes (sai)? Dafen, Ming'e, Jingruan, Fangcheng, Xiao, Jingxing, Lingci, Gouzhu and Juyong.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十四 河東道三 代州
passages.textZh: 今按句注在州西北三十五里，雁門縣界西陘山是也。
passages.textEn: Gouzhu is 35 li north-west of the prefecture: Mount Xixing in Yanmen county.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十四 河東道三 代州雁門縣
passages.textZh: 句注山，一名西陘山，在縣西北三十里。晉咸寧元年句注碑曰：「蓋北方之險，有盧龍、飛狐，句注為之首，天下之阻，所以分別內外也。」漢高祖欲伐匈奴，不從婁敬之說，械係於廣武，遂逾句注，困於平城，謂此地也。
passages.textEn: Mount Gouzhu, also called Mount Xixing, thirty li north-west of the county. The Gouzhu stele of 275 says: "Of the strongholds of the north — Lulong, Feihu — Gouzhu is the chief: the barrier of the realm, which divides inside from outside." When Gaozu of Han set out against the Xiongnu he would not heed Lou Jing, put him in chains at Guangwu, crossed Gouzhu and was trapped at Pingcheng: this is the place.

confidenceNote.zh: 今人多以為在今河北遷西縣北喜峰口一帶的灤河谷道，此取約址。天然通道，全時段繪出。
confidenceNote.en: Usually placed in the Luan valley around Xifengkou, north of Qianxi, Hebei; the point is approximate. A natural route, drawn for the whole period.

summary.zh: 建安十二年（207）曹操北征，七月大水，傍海道不通，田疇請為嚮導；曹軍出盧龍塞，塞外道絕不通，乃塹山堙谷五百餘里，經白檀，歷平岡，涉鮮卑庭，東指柳城。晉句注碑以盧龍與飛狐、句注並為北方之險。
summary.en: In 207, on his northern campaign, Cao Cao found the coast road flooded in the seventh month; Tian Chou offered to guide him, and the army went out through Lulong Pass. Beyond it there was no road, so they cut through hills and filled valleys for over five hundred li, by Baitan and Pinggang, across the Xianbei grounds, heading east for Liucheng. The Gouzhu stele of 275 names Lulong with Feihu and Gouzhu as the strongholds of the north.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 魏書一 武帝紀 建安十二年
passages.textZh: 秋七月，大水，傍海道不通，田疇請爲鄉導，公從之。引軍出盧龍塞，塞外道絕不通，乃壍山堙谷五百餘里，經白檀，歷平岡，涉鮮卑庭，東指柳城。
passages.textEn: In autumn, the seventh month, there were great floods and the coast road was impassable. Tian Chou asked to guide them and Cao Cao agreed. He led the army out through Lulong Pass; beyond it the road was cut, so they dug through hills and filled valleys for more than five hundred li, passing Baitan and Pinggang and crossing the Xianbei grounds, heading east for Liucheng.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷十四 河東道三 代州雁門縣
passages.textZh: 晉咸寧元年句注碑曰：「蓋北方之險，有盧龍、飛狐，句注為之首，天下之阻，所以分別內外也。」
passages.textEn: The Gouzhu stele of the first year of Xianning of Jin (275) says: "Of the strongholds of the north — Lulong, Feihu — Gouzhu is the chief: the barrier of the realm, which divides inside from outside."

confidenceNote.zh: 此以開皇十八年（598）為始見。隋唐臨渝關的位置有異說（今河北撫寧東榆關一帶，或今山海關附近），此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded here in 598. Where the Sui–Tang Linyu Pass stood is disputed (around Yuguan east of Funing, Hebei, or near today's Shanhaiguan); the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 隋開皇十八年（598），高句麗王高元率靺鞨萬餘騎寇遼西，隋文帝命漢王諒為元帥，總水陸討之；時餽運不繼，六軍乏食，師出臨渝關，復遇疾疫，王師不振。
summary.en: In 598 King Go Won of Goguryeo raided Liaoxi with ten thousand Mohe horsemen. Emperor Wen of Sui sent the Prince of Han, Yang Liang, against him by land and sea; supplies failed, the armies went hungry, and when they went out through Linyu Pass disease struck and the campaign foundered.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷八十一 東夷傳 高麗
passages.textZh: 明年，元率靺鞨之眾萬餘騎寇遼西，營州總管韋沖擊走之。高祖聞而大怒，命漢王諒為元帥，總水陸討之，下詔黜其爵位。時餽運不繼，六軍乏食，師出臨渝關，復遇疾疫，王師不振。
passages.textEn: The next year Go Won led over ten thousand Mohe horsemen to raid Liaoxi; Wei Chong, Area Commander of Yingzhou, drove them off. The emperor, furious, made the Prince of Han, Liang, commander-in-chief over land and sea forces, and stripped Go Won of his titles. Supplies could not keep up and the armies went hungry; going out through Linyu Pass they met an epidemic, and the royal army foundered.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以建安二十年（215）為始見。漢末陽平關約在今陝西勉縣西（武侯鎮一帶），此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded here in 215. The late-Han Yangping Pass was roughly west of Mian county, Shaanxi (around Wuhou town); the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 建安二十年（215）七月，曹操征張魯至陽平。張魯使弟衞與將楊昂等據陽平關，橫山築城十餘里，曹軍攻之不能拔，引軍還；守軍懈散，曹操遣解𢢼、高祚等乘險夜襲，大破之，張魯潰奔巴中。
summary.en: In the seventh month of 215 Cao Cao reached Yangping on his march against Zhang Lu. Zhang Lu's brother Wei and the general Yang Ang held Yangping Pass with a wall more than ten li long across the hills; Cao could not take it and turned back, but when the defenders relaxed he sent Xie Biao and Gao Zuo over the heights by night, routed them, and Zhang Lu fled to Ba.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 魏書一 武帝紀 建安二十年
passages.textZh: 秋七月，公至陽平。張魯使弟衞與將楊昂等據陽平關，橫山築城十餘里，攻之不能拔，乃引軍還。賊見大軍退，其守備解散。公乃密遣解𢢼、高祚等乘險夜襲，大破之，斬其將楊任，進攻衞，衞等夜遁，魯潰奔巴中。
passages.textEn: In autumn, the seventh month, Cao Cao reached Yangping. Zhang Lu had his brother Wei and the general Yang Ang hold Yangping Pass, walling across the hills for more than ten li. Unable to take it, Cao withdrew. Seeing the army leave, the defenders let their guard drop; Cao secretly sent Xie Biao, Gao Zuo and others over the heights by night, routed them and killed their general Yang Ren. He pressed on against Wei, who fled by night, and Zhang Lu broke and fled to Ba.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以景元四年（263）為始見，設置當更早，年代不詳。在今四川劍閣縣劍門關。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded here in 263; it must be older, but when it was set up is unknown. The site is Jianmen Pass, Jiange county, Sichuan.

summary.zh: 景元四年（263）魏伐蜀，姜維、廖化與張翼、董厥退保劍閣以拒鍾會，列營守險，會不能克，糧運懸遠，將議還歸；而鄧艾自陰平由景谷道傍入，破諸葛瞻於綿竹，後主請降。唐劍州有大劍鎮，本姜維拒鍾會之壘，峭壁千丈，下瞰絕澗，飛閣以通行旅。
summary.en: When Wei invaded Shu in 263, Jiang Wei, Liao Hua, Zhang Yi and Dong Jue fell back to hold Jiange against Zhong Hui. Camped on the heights, they held; Zhong Hui, with supplies far behind, was thinking of retreat — but Deng Ai slipped in from Yinping by the Jinggu road, beat Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, and the Shu ruler surrendered. In Tang Jianzhou the Dajian garrison stood on Jiang Wei's old rampart: cliffs a thousand zhang high above a sheer gorge, crossed by a hanging gallery road.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 蜀書十四 姜維傳
passages.textZh: 翼、厥甫至漢壽，維、化亦捨陰平而退。適與翼、厥合，皆退保劍閣以拒會。
passages.textEn: Zhang Yi and Dong Jue had just reached Hanshou when Jiang Wei and Liao Hua also gave up Yinping and fell back; joining them, they all retired to hold Jiange against Zhong Hui.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 蜀書十四 姜維傳
passages.textZh: 維不答書，列營守險。會不能克，糧運縣遠，將議還歸。而鄧艾自陰平由景谷道傍入，遂破諸葛瞻於綿竹。後主請降於艾，艾前據成都。
passages.textEn: Jiang Wei did not answer, and camped on the heights. Zhong Hui could not take them; his supplies were far behind and he was thinking of going home. But Deng Ai came in by a side road from Yinping through the Jinggu way and beat Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu. The Shu ruler surrendered to Deng Ai, who went on to hold Chengdu.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 魏書二十八 鄧艾傳
passages.textZh: 從陰平由邪徑經漢德陽亭趣涪，出劍閣西百里，去成都三百餘里，奇兵衝其腹心。劍閣之守必還赴涪，則會方軌而進；劍閣之軍不還，則應涪之兵寡矣。
passages.textEn: From Yinping, by a byway through the Han Deyang post to Fu — a hundred li west of Jiange, three hundred from Chengdu — a surprise force strikes at their heart. If the Jiange garrison turns back to Fu, Zhong Hui advances freely; if it does not, Fu will have few defenders.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 劍南道下 劍州普安縣
passages.textZh: 大劍鎮，在縣東四十八里。本薑維拒鍾會壘也，在開遠戍東十一里。其山峭壁千丈，下瞰絕澗，飛閣以通行旅，梁時於此置大劍戍。
passages.textEn: The Dajian garrison, 48 li east of the county: originally the rampart from which Jiang Wei held off Zhong Hui, eleven li east of the Kaiyuan post. Its cliffs rise a thousand zhang over a sheer gorge, and travellers pass by a hanging gallery; the Liang set up the Dajian post here.

confidenceNote.zh: 設關確年不詳，此以元封年間（約前108）「列亭鄣至玉門」為始。關址一般比定於今甘肅敦煌西北的小方盤城一帶，但小方盤城是否即關城，學界有爭議。此關何時廢、東移，史無明文；下限取唐關始見之年（629）。
confidenceNote.en: When the gate was set up is unknown; it is drawn from the Yuanfeng years (c. 108 BCE), when "forts were lined as far as Yumen". The site is usually placed near Xiaofangpan, north-west of Dunhuang, though whether that ruin was the gate itself is debated. When the gate was abandoned or moved east is not recorded; it is drawn until the Tang gate first appears (629).

summary.zh: 漢通西域的北門。趙破奴破姑師後，「酒泉列亭鄣至玉門」。李廣利伐大宛，士卒饑乏，上書請罷兵，武帝大怒，「使使遮玉門」，軍有敢入者輒斬。《漢書·西域傳》稱西域「東則接漢，厄以玉門、陽關」，出玉門、陽關有南北二道。東漢班超上疏：「但願生入玉門關。」唐時稱玉門故關，在沙州壽昌縣西北一百一十七里，謂之北道，「此西域之門戶也」。
summary.en: The northern gate of Han to the Western Regions. After Zhao Ponu broke Gushi, "Jiuquan lined its forts and watchtowers as far as Yumen". When Li Guangli's army before Dayuan ran out of food and he asked to come home, Emperor Wu in fury "sent envoys to bar the Jade Gate": any soldier who came through would be beheaded. The Book of Han says the Western Regions "border Han on the east, closed off by the Jade Gate and Yang Pass", and that two roads led west from them. Ban Chao, in the Eastern Han, wrote that he asked only "to come back alive through the Jade Gate". Tang writers called it the old Jade Gate, 117 li north-west of Shouchang in Shazhou — the northern road, "the door to the Western Regions".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳
passages.textZh: 王恢數使，為樓蘭所苦，言天子，天子發兵令恢佐破奴擊破之，封恢為浩侯。於是酒泉列亭鄣至玉門矣。
passages.textEn: Wang Hui, often sent as envoy and harried by Loulan, told the emperor, who sent troops with Wang Hui to help Zhao Ponu break them, and made Wang Hui Marquis of Hao. Then Jiuquan lined its forts and watchtowers as far as Yumen.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳
passages.textZh: 使使上書言：「道遠多乏食；且士卒不患戰，患饑。人少，不足以拔宛。願且罷兵，益發而復往。」天子聞之，大怒，而使使遮玉門，曰軍有敢入者輒斬之！貳師恐，因留敦煌。
passages.textEn: He sent a memorial: "The road is long and food short; the men fear hunger more than battle. We are too few to take Dayuan. Let us stop for now and come back with more." The emperor, hearing it, was furious and sent envoys to bar the Jade Gate: any soldier who dared come in would be beheaded. The Ershi general, afraid, stayed at Dunhuang.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十六上 西域傳 序
passages.textZh: 東則接漢，厄以玉門、陽關，西則限以蔥嶺。
passages.textEn: On the east they border Han, closed off by the Jade Gate and Yang Pass; on the west they are bounded by the Pamirs.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十六上 西域傳 序
passages.textZh: 自玉門、陽關出西域有兩道：從鄯善傍南山北，波河西行至莎車，為南道
passages.textEn: From the Jade Gate and Yang Pass two roads lead into the Western Regions: from Shanshan along the north foot of the southern mountains, following the river west to Shache, is the southern road

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 班超傳
passages.textZh: 臣不敢望到酒泉郡，但願生入玉門關。
passages.textEn: I dare not hope to reach Jiuquan commandery; I ask only to come back alive through the Jade Gate.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷四十 隴右道下 沙州壽昌縣
passages.textZh: 玉門故關，在縣西北一百一十七里。謂之北道，西趣車師前庭及疏勒。此西域之門戶也
passages.textEn: The old Jade Gate, 117 li north-west of the county: called the northern road, leading west to the Former Jushi court and Shule. This is the door to the Western Regions.

question.zh: 漢玉門關是否曾經西移？
question.en: Did the Han Jade Gate move west?

claim.zh: 唐人說漢罷玉門關屯戍，把戍卒遷到酒泉郡玉門縣，縣因以得名。
claim.en: A Tang source says Han withdrew the Jade Gate garrison and resettled its men in Yumen county of Jiuquan, which took its name from them.

source.zh: 《元和郡縣圖志》卷四十 肅州玉門縣
source.en: Yuanhe Gazetteer, juan 40, Yumen county of Suzhou

accounts.quoteZh: 本漢舊縣，屬酒泉郡。漢罷玉門關屯戍，徙其人於此，因以名縣。

claim.zh: 有學者據此推測，玉門關初設於酒泉郡境（今嘉峪關、玉門一帶），後來才西移至敦煌西北；也有學者認為此條只是說戍卒遷徙，不足以證明關址移動。
claim.en: Some scholars infer that the gate first stood in Jiuquan (around today's Jiayuguan and Yumen) and only later moved west of Dunhuang; others hold the passage records only a resettlement, not a move of the gate.

note.zh: 地圖只繪敦煌西北的關址。
note.en: The map draws only the site north-west of Dunhuang.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以玄奘過瓜州（貞觀三年629年秋起行之後）為始見。唐瓜州城一般比定為今甘肅瓜州縣東南的鎖陽城；兩種記載相去數十里，此按玄奘傳取城北疏勒河（瓠𤬜河）畔的約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded with Xuanzang's passage through Guazhou, after he set out in the autumn of 629. Tang Guazhou is usually identified with the Suoyang ruins south-east of Guazhou county, Gansu; the two records differ by tens of li, and the point follows Xuanzang's account, on the Shule (Hulu) river north of the city.

summary.zh: 唐代的玉門關在瓜州。玄奘西行至瓜州，聞「從此北行五十餘里有瓠𤬜河…上置玉門關，路必由之，即西境之襟喉也」，關外西北又有五烽。《元和郡縣圖志》則記玉門關在瓜州晉昌縣東二十步。
summary.en: The Tang Jade Gate stood in Guazhou. When Xuanzang reached Guazhou on his way west he was told that "fifty-odd li north of here is the Hulu river … over it stands the Jade Gate, which every traveller must pass: the throat of the western frontier", with five beacon towers beyond it to the north-west. The Yuanhe Gazetteer instead puts the Jade Gate twenty paces east of Jinchang, seat of Guazhou.

passages.sourceZh: 大唐大慈恩寺三藏法師傳
passages.sourceEn: Biography of Xuanzang (Huili and Yancong, 688)
passages.locator: 卷一
passages.textZh: 從此北行五十餘里有瓠𤬜河，下廣上狹，洄波甚急，深不可渡。上置玉門關，路必由之，即西境之襟喉也。關外西北又有五烽，候望者居之，各相去百里，中無水草。
passages.textEn: Fifty-odd li north of here is the Hulu river, wide below and narrow above, with swift whirling currents, too deep to ford. Over it stands the Jade Gate, which every traveller must pass: the throat of the western frontier. Beyond the gate to the north-west are five beacon towers, manned by watchmen, each a hundred li from the next, with no water or grass between.
passages.url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/大唐大慈恩寺三藏法師傳/卷01

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷四十 隴右道下 瓜州晉昌縣
passages.textZh: 玉門關，在縣東二十步。
passages.textEn: The Jade Gate, twenty paces east of the county.

question.en: Where in Guazhou was the Tang Jade Gate?

claim.zh: 在瓜州城北五十餘里的瓠𤬜河上。
claim.en: Fifty-odd li north of Guazhou, on the Hulu river.

source.zh: 《大唐大慈恩寺三藏法師傳》卷一

accounts.quoteZh: 從此北行五十餘里有瓠𤬜河，下廣上狹，洄波甚急，深不可渡。上置玉門關

claim.zh: 在瓜州治所晉昌縣東二十步。
claim.en: Twenty paces east of Jinchang, the seat of Guazhou.

accounts.quoteZh: 玉門關，在縣東二十步。

note.zh: 兩說相去數十里，今人比定亦不一。
note.en: The two differ by tens of li, and modern identifications differ too.

confidenceNote.zh: 設關確年不詳；此取漢武帝伐大宛之後（約前101）為始，係約數。遺址一般比定於今敦煌西南南湖鄉古董灘一帶。
confidenceNote.en: When it was set up is unknown; it is drawn from c. 101 BCE, after the Dayuan war — an estimate. The site is usually placed at Gudongtan, Nanhu, south-west of Dunhuang.

summary.zh: 漢通西域的南門。《漢書·西域傳》稱西域「東則接漢，厄以玉門、陽關」，自玉門、陽關出西域有南北二道。唐時陽關在沙州壽昌縣西六里，以居玉門之南，故曰陽關；本漢所置，謂之南道，西趣鄯善、莎車。
summary.en: The southern gate of Han to the Western Regions. The Book of Han says the Western Regions "border Han on the east, closed off by the Jade Gate and Yang Pass", with two roads leading west from them. In Tang times Yang Pass lay six li west of Shouchang in Shazhou; it was called Yang ("south side") because it lay south of the Jade Gate. Built by Han, it opened the southern road west to Shanshan and Shache.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十六上 西域傳 序
passages.textZh: 東則接漢，厄以玉門、陽關，西則限以蔥嶺。
passages.textEn: On the east they border Han, closed off by the Jade Gate and Yang Pass; on the west they are bounded by the Pamirs.

passages.sourceEn: Yuanhe Gazetteer (Li Jifu, 813)
passages.locator: 卷四十 隴右道下 沙州壽昌縣
passages.textZh: 陽關，在縣西六里。以居玉門蘭之南，故曰陽關。本漢置也，謂之南道，西趣鄯善、莎車。後魏當於此置陽關縣，周廢。
passages.textEn: Yang Pass, six li west of the county. It lies south of the Jade Gate, hence "Yang". Built by Han, it is called the southern road, leading west to Shanshan and Shache. The Northern Wei set up a Yangguan county here, which the Zhou abolished.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以甘露三年（前51）為始見。今人比定於今內蒙古磴口縣西北狼山的峽谷口石城一帶，此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded here in 51 BCE. Identified with a stone fort at a gorge mouth in the Lang mountains north-west of Dengkou, Inner Mongolia; the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 甘露三年（前51）呼韓邪單于入朝後歸國，漢遣長樂衛尉董忠、車騎都尉韓昌將騎萬六千，又發邊郡士馬以千數，送單于出朔方雞鹿塞。
summary.en: In 51 BCE, after Huhanye chanyu had come to court, Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang with 16,000 horsemen and thousands more from the frontier commanderies to escort him home out through the Jilu pass in Shuofang.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十四下 匈奴傳下
passages.textZh: 漢遣長樂衛尉高昌侯董忠、車騎都尉韓昌將騎萬六千，又發邊郡士馬以千數，送單于出朔方雞鹿塞。
passages.textEn: Han sent Dong Zhong, Marquis of Gaochang and Commandant of the Changle Guard, and Han Chang, Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry, with sixteen thousand horsemen, and raised thousands more men and horses from the frontier commanderies, to escort the chanyu out through the Jilu pass in Shuofang.

confidenceNote.zh: 高闕是陰山（狼山）的某一山口，今人比定意見不一，此取約址。天然隘口，全時段繪出。
confidenceNote.en: Gaoque was a gap in the Yin (Lang) mountains; modern identifications differ and the point is approximate. A natural gap, drawn for the whole period.

summary.zh: 趙武靈王變俗胡服，習騎射，北破林胡、樓煩，築長城，自代並陰山下，至高闕為塞。漢元朔五年（前124）衛青率六將軍、十餘萬人出朔方、高闕擊胡。
summary.en: King Wuling of Zhao, adopting nomad dress and mounted archery, beat the Linhu and Loufan in the north and built a long wall from Dai along the foot of the Yin mountains to Gaoque, which he made a frontier post. In 124 BCE Wei Qing led six generals and over a hundred thousand men out through Shuofang and Gaoque against the nomads.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十 匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 而趙武靈王亦變俗胡服，習騎射，北破林胡、樓煩。築長城，自代并陰山下，至高闕爲塞。
passages.textEn: King Wuling of Zhao too changed customs, wearing nomad dress and training mounted archers, and broke the Linhu and Loufan in the north. He built a long wall from Dai along the foot of the Yin mountains to Gaoque, making it the frontier.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十 匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 其明年春，漢以衛青爲大將軍，將六將軍，十餘萬人，出朔方、高闕擊胡。
passages.textEn: In spring of the next year Han made Wei Qing General-in-Chief, at the head of six generals and over a hundred thousand men, to strike the nomads out through Shuofang and Gaoque.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以秦末（約前207）為始見。一般比定於今廣東南雄市北大庾嶺一帶（後世梅關附近），此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded at the end of Qin (c. 207 BCE). Usually placed on the Dayu ridge north of Nanxiong, Guangdong (near the later Mei Pass); the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 秦末南海尉任囂死，趙佗移檄橫浦、陽山、湟谿三關：「盜兵且至，急絕道聚兵自守！」隨後擊併桂林、象郡，自立為南越武王。元鼎五年（前112）漢伐南越，樓船將軍楊仆出豫章，下橫浦。
summary.en: When Ren Xiao, Commandant of Nanhai, died at the end of Qin, Zhao Tuo sent word to the three passes of Hengpu, Yangshan and Huangxi: "Bandit armies are coming — cut the roads, gather troops and hold!" He then took Guilin and Xiang and made himself King Wu of Nanyue. In 112 BCE, when Han attacked Nanyue, Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, came out of Yuzhang and down through Hengpu.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十三 南越列傳
passages.textZh: 囂死，佗即移檄告橫浦、陽山、湟谿關曰：「盜兵且至，急絕道聚兵自守！」因稍以法誅秦所置長吏，以其黨為假守。秦已破滅，佗即擊并桂林、象郡，自立為南越武王。
passages.textEn: When Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo at once sent word to the passes of Hengpu, Yangshan and Huangxi: "Bandit armies are coming — cut the roads, gather troops and hold!" Bit by bit he had the officials Qin had appointed executed under the law and put his own men in as acting governors. When Qin had fallen he took Guilin and Xiang and set himself up as King Wu of Nanyue.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十三 南越列傳
passages.textZh: 主爵都尉楊仆為樓船將軍，出豫章，下橫浦；
passages.textEn: Yang Pu, Commandant of Noble Ranks, as General of the Towered Ships, came out of Yuzhang and down through Hengpu;

confidenceNote.zh: 此以秦末（約前207）為始見。約在今廣東陽山縣一帶，確址不明。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded at the end of Qin (c. 207 BCE). Somewhere around Yangshan county, Guangdong; the exact site is unknown.

summary.zh: 秦末趙佗移檄橫浦、陽山、湟谿三關，令「急絕道聚兵自守」，此其一。
summary.en: One of the three passes — Hengpu, Yangshan, Huangxi — that Zhao Tuo ordered at the end of Qin to "cut the roads, gather troops and hold".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十三 南越列傳
passages.textZh: 囂死，佗即移檄告橫浦、陽山、湟谿關曰：「盜兵且至，急絕道聚兵自守！」
passages.textEn: When Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo at once sent word to the passes of Hengpu, Yangshan and Huangxi: "Bandit armies are coming — cut the roads, gather troops and hold!"

confidenceNote.zh: 此以秦末（約前207）為始見。一般認為在今廣東英德市境內，連江入北江處附近，確址不明。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded at the end of Qin (c. 207 BCE). Usually thought to be in Yingde, Guangdong, near where the Lian river joins the Bei; the exact site is unknown.

summary.zh: 秦末趙佗移檄橫浦、陽山、湟谿三關，令「急絕道聚兵自守」，此其一。
summary.en: One of the three passes — Hengpu, Yangshan, Huangxi — that Zhao Tuo ordered at the end of Qin to "cut the roads, gather troops and hold".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百十三 南越列傳
passages.textZh: 囂死，佗即移檄告橫浦、陽山、湟谿關曰：「盜兵且至，急絕道聚兵自守！」
passages.textEn: When Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo at once sent word to the passes of Hengpu, Yangshan and Huangxi: "Bandit armies are coming — cut the roads, gather troops and hold!"

confidenceNote.zh: 從楚築關之年（前377）起繪。漢江關在魚復（今重慶奉節，瞿塘峽口）；楚所築捍關是否即此地，有異說，見下。
confidenceNote.en: Drawn from Chu's building of the pass (377 BCE). The Han Jiang Pass was at Yufu (Fengjie, Chongqing, at the mouth of the Qutang gorge); whether Chu's pass stood here is disputed — see below.

summary.zh: 楚肅王四年（前377），蜀伐楚，取茲方，楚因築捍關以拒蜀。兩漢之際公孫述據蜀，使將軍任滿「東據扞關」，於是盡有益州之地。東漢岑彭伐蜀，長驅入江關，令軍中無得虜掠。
summary.en: In 377 BCE, when Shu attacked Chu and took Zifang, Chu built the Han Pass to hold Shu back. Between the two Han dynasties Gongsun Shu, ruling Shu, sent his general Ren Man to "hold the Han Pass in the east", and so held all of Yizhou. Under the restored Han, Cen Peng drove deep through the Jiang Pass, and forbade his men to plunder.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十 楚世家 肅王四年
passages.textZh: 四年，蜀伐楚，取茲方。於是楚爲捍關以距之。
passages.textEn: In the fourth year Shu attacked Chu and took Zifang. Chu then built the Han Pass to hold it off.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷十三 公孫述傳
passages.textZh: 述遂使將軍侯丹開白水關，北守南鄭；將軍任滿從閬中下江州，東據扞關。於是盡有益州之地。
passages.textEn: Gongsun Shu sent his general Hou Dan to open the Baishui Pass and hold Nanzheng in the north, and his general Ren Man down from Langzhong to Jiangzhou to hold the Han Pass in the east. So he held all of Yizhou.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷十七 岑彭傳
passages.textZh: 彭上劉隆為南郡太守，自率臧宮、劉歆長驅入江關，令軍中無得虜掠。
passages.textEn: Cen Peng recommended Liu Long as Grand Administrator of Nanjun and himself led Zang Gong and Liu Xin on a long drive through the Jiang Pass, forbidding his army to plunder.

question.en: Where was the pass Chu built in 377 BCE?

claim.zh: 在長江瞿塘峽口（今重慶奉節），即漢之江關。
claim.en: At the mouth of the Qutang gorge (Fengjie, Chongqing): the later Han Jiang Pass.

claim.zh: 在清江（夷水）上，今湖北長陽一帶；漢魚復的扞關、江關是後來的關。
claim.en: On the Qing (Yi) river around Changyang, Hubei; the Han Pass and Jiang Pass at Yufu came later.

note.en: The Shiji does not say where.

confidenceNote.zh: 此以伍子胥奔吳（約前522）為始見。傳統比定在今安徽含山縣北小峴山，史無確證。
confidenceNote.en: First recorded with Wu Zixu's flight (c. 522 BCE). Traditionally placed on Mount Xiaoxian north of Hanshan, Anhui, without firm evidence.

summary.zh: 伍子胥自鄭與太子建之子勝奔吳，到昭關，關吏欲執之；子胥與勝獨身步走，幾不得脫，追者在後，至江，漁父渡之。
summary.en: Wu Zixu, fleeing from Zheng to Wu with Sheng, son of Crown Prince Jian, came to Zhao Pass, where the guards tried to seize them. He and Sheng escaped on foot, barely, with pursuers behind; at the river a fisherman ferried them across.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六十六 伍子胥列傳
passages.textZh: 建有子名勝。伍胥懼，乃與勝俱奔吳。到昭關，昭關欲執之。伍胥遂與勝獨身步走，幾不得脫。追者在後。至江，江上有一漁父乘船，知伍胥之急，乃渡伍胥。
passages.textEn: Jian had a son named Sheng. Wu Zixu, afraid, fled with Sheng to Wu. At Zhao Pass the guards tried to seize them; Wu Zixu and Sheng went on alone on foot and barely got away, with pursuers behind them. At the river a fisherman in a boat, seeing his danger, ferried him across.

note.zh: 今人多以為即後世平靖關一帶
note.en: usually identified with the later Pingjing Pass

confidenceNote.zh: 大別山北麓的隘道，天然隘口，全時段繪出。今人多以為即後世平靖關一帶（今河南信陽市南），此取約址。
confidenceNote.en: A defile on the north side of the Dabie mountains; a natural pass, drawn for the whole period. Usually identified with the later Pingjing Pass south of Xinyang, Henan; the point is approximate.

summary.zh: 《呂氏春秋》天下九塞之一。魯定公四年（前506）吳師伐楚，楚左司馬戌謀「悉方城外以毀其舟，還塞大隧、直轅、冥阨」，與子常前後夾擊吳軍。
summary.en: One of the nine great passes of the Lüshi chunqiu. When Wu invaded Chu in 506 BCE, the Chu marshal Xu planned to "take everything outside Fangcheng to destroy their boats, and come back to block Dasui, Zhiyuan and Ming'e", so that he and Zichang could take the Wu army front and rear.

passages.sourceEn: Lüshi chunqiu (c. 239 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷十三 有始覽
passages.textZh: 何謂九塞？大汾，冥阨，荊阮，方城，殽，井陘，令疵，句注，居庸。
passages.textEn: What are the nine passes (sai)? Dafen, Ming'e, Jingruan, Fangcheng, Xiao, Jingxing, Lingci, Gouzhu and Juyong.

passages.sourceEn: Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan, 4th c. BCE)
passages.locator: 定公四年
passages.textZh: 左司馬戌謂子常曰．子沿漢而與之上下．我悉方城外以毀其舟．還塞大隧．直轅．冥阨．子濟漢而伐之．我自後擊之．必大敗之．
passages.textEn: The Marshal of the Left, Xu, said to Zichang: "You move up and down the Han river with them. I will take everything outside Fangcheng to destroy their boats, and come back to block Dasui, Zhiyuan and Ming'e. Then you cross the Han and attack, and I strike from behind — we will crush them."

summary.zh: 慕容永所主之燕，據長子；為慕容垂所攻，城破，永被擒殺。
summary.en: The Yan state of Murong Yong, based at Changzi; Murong Chui besieged it, the city fell, and Yong was captured and put to death.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 載記 慕容垂
passages.textZh: 垂進圍長子，永將賈韜潛為內應。垂進軍入城，永奔北門，為前驅所獲，於是數而戮之，並其所署公卿刁雲等三十餘人。
passages.textEn: Chui besieged Changzi, and Yong's officer Jia Tao secretly worked for him inside. Chui entered the city; Yong fled to the north gate and was caught by the vanguard, and Chui charged him with his crimes and put him to death, with more than thirty of his ministers including Diao Yun.

summary.zh: 譙縱殺益州刺史毛璩，據蜀叛晉；晉將朱齡石克成都，斬譙縱，益州平。
summary.en: Qiao Zong killed Mao Qu, Inspector of Yi, and held Shu in revolt against Jin; the Jin general Zhu Lingshi took Chengdu and beheaded him.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷十 安帝紀 義熙元年
passages.textZh: 平西參軍譙縱害平西將軍、益州刺史毛璩，以蜀叛。
passages.textEn: Qiao Zong, an adjutant of the General Who Pacifies the West, killed Mao Qu, the general and Inspector of Yi Province, and rose in revolt with Shu.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷十 安帝紀 義熙九年
passages.textZh: 秋七月，朱齡石克成都，斬譙縱，益州平。
passages.textEn: In the seventh month, in autumn, Zhu Lingshi took Chengdu and beheaded Qiao Zong; Yi Province was pacified.

summary.zh: 沮渠蒙遜所主之涼，都姑臧，以義熙八年稱河西王；破西涼李士業於蓼泉，入酒泉。
summary.en: The Liang state of Juqu Mengxun, with its capital at Guzang; he took the title King of Hexi in 412, and beat Li Shiye of Western Liang at Liaoquan and entered Jiuquan.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十九 載記 沮渠蒙遜
passages.textZh: 俄而蒙遜遷于姑臧，以義熙八年僭即河西王位，大赦境內，改元玄始。
passages.textEn: Soon Mengxun moved to Guzang and in the eighth year of Yixi usurped the title of King of Hexi, proclaimed an amnesty and changed the era name to Xuanshi.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 涼武昭王傳（附士業）
passages.textZh: 勒眾復戰，敗於蓼泉，為蒙遜所害。士業諸弟酒泉太守翻、新城太守預、領羽林右監密、左將軍眺、右將軍亮等西奔敦煌，蒙遜遂入於酒泉。
passages.textEn: He rallied his men and fought again, was beaten at Liaoquan and killed by Mengxun. Shiye's brothers Fan, Yu, Mi, Tiao, Liang and others fled west to Dunhuang, and Mengxun entered Jiuquan.

summary.zh: 李玄盛所主之涼，自敦煌遷居酒泉；其子士業東伐北涼，敗死於蓼泉，北涼入酒泉。
summary.en: The Liang state of Li Xuansheng, who moved from Dunhuang to Jiuquan; his son Shiye attacked Northern Liang, was killed at Liaoquan, and Northern Liang entered Jiuquan.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 涼武昭王傳
passages.textZh: 乃以張體順為甯遠將軍、建康太守，鎮樂涫，征宋繇為右將軍，領敦煌護軍，與其子敦煌太守讓鎮敦煌，遂遷居於酒泉。
passages.textEn: He made Zhang Tishun general and governor of Jiankang to hold Leguan, summoned Song Yao as general of the right in charge of Dunhuang to hold it with his son Rang, the governor of Dunhuang, and then moved his residence to Jiuquan.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 涼武昭王傳（附士業）
passages.textZh: 勒眾復戰，敗於蓼泉，為蒙遜所害。士業諸弟酒泉太守翻、新城太守預、領羽林右監密、左將軍眺、右將軍亮等西奔敦煌，蒙遜遂入於酒泉。
passages.textEn: He rallied his men and fought again, was beaten at Liaoquan and killed by Mengxun. Shiye's brothers Fan, Yu, Mi, Tiao, Liang and others fled west to Dunhuang, and Mengxun entered Jiuquan.

summary.zh: 都和龍之燕，末主馮文通；北魏屢伐之，文通終奔高麗。
summary.en: The Yan state centred on Helong, whose last ruler was Feng Wentong; Northern Wei attacked it repeatedly, and Wentong finally fled to Goguryeo.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 延和元年
passages.textZh: 己巳，車駕至和龍，臨其城。文通石城太守李崇、建德太守王融十餘郡來降，發其民三萬人穿圍塹以守之。
passages.textEn: On jisi the emperor reached Helong and came up to its walls. Ten or more of Wentong's commanderies, including Shicheng under Li Chong and Jiande under Wang Rong, surrendered, and thirty thousand of their people were put to digging siege trenches.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 太延二年
passages.textZh: 五月乙卯，馮文通奔高麗。
passages.textEn: On yimao of the fifth month Feng Wentong fled to Goguryeo.

summary.zh: 王衍所主之蜀，都成都；後唐兵至，敗於三泉，衍出降。
summary.en: The Shu state of Wang Yan, with its capital at Chengdu; when Later Tang attacked, his army was routed at Sanquan and he surrendered.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 唐書 莊宗紀七
passages.textZh: 時王衍將幸秦州，以其軍五萬屯於利州。聞我師至，遣步騎三萬逆戰於三泉，延孝與李嚴以勁騎三千擊之，蜀軍大敗，斬首五千級，餘眾奔潰。王衍聞敗，自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津，浮梁而去。
passages.textEn: Wang Yan was about to visit Qinzhou and had fifty thousand men camped at Lizhou. Hearing our army was coming, he sent thirty thousand foot and horse to meet it at Sanquan; Yanxiao and Li Yan struck them with three thousand picked horse, and the Shu army was routed with five thousand beheaded and the rest scattered. Hearing of the defeat, Wang Yan fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, cutting the floating bridge at Jibai ford behind him.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 唐書 莊宗紀七
passages.textZh: 丙辰，蜀主王衍出降，語在衍傳。
passages.textEn: On bingchen Wang Yan, the ruler of Shu, came out and surrendered; the details are in his biography.

summary.zh: 段氏所主之國，晚期國事決於高祥、高和兄弟；蒙古軍薄大理城，高祥遁走被斬。
summary.en: The kingdom of the Duan, in whose last years power lay with the brothers Gao Xiang and Gao He; when the Mongol army reached Dali, Gao Xiang fled and was beheaded.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷四 世祖本紀一 歲癸丑
passages.textZh: 十二月丙辰，軍薄大理城。初，大理主段氏微弱，國事皆決於高祥、高和兄弟。是夜，祥率眾遁去，命大將也古及拔突兒追之。
passages.textEn: On bingchen of the twelfth month the army closed on the city of Dali. The Duan rulers of Dali had long been weak, and affairs of state were decided by the brothers Gao Xiang and Gao He. That night Xiang fled with his followers, and the generals Yegu and Batur were sent after him.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷四 世祖本紀一 歲癸丑
passages.textZh: 癸亥，獲高祥，斬于姚州。
passages.textEn: On guihai Gao Xiang was caught and beheaded at Yaozhou.

summary.zh: 莊宗所建之唐：前軍入汴，梁亡；後伐蜀，敗蜀軍於三泉，王衍出降。
summary.en: The Tang of Emperor Zhuangzong: its vanguard took Bian, ending Liang; later it attacked Shu, routed its army at Sanquan, and Wang Yan surrendered.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三十 唐書 莊宗紀四
passages.textZh: 己卯遲明，前軍至汴城，嗣源令左右捉生攻封丘門，梁開封尹王瓚請以城降。俄而帝與大軍繼至，王瓚迎帝自大梁門入。
passages.textEn: At dawn on jimao the vanguard reached Bian. Siyuan had his men attack the Fengqiu gate, and Wang Zan, Liang's prefect of Kaifeng, offered to surrender the city. Soon the emperor arrived with the main army, and Wang Zan received him in through the Daliang gate.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三十三 唐書 莊宗紀七
passages.textZh: 丙辰，蜀主王衍出降，語在衍傳。
passages.textEn: On bingchen Wang Yan, the ruler of Shu, came out and surrendered; the details are in his biography.

summary.zh: 袁氏據鄴之主。出攻袁譚，留審配守鄴；曹操圍鄴，尚還救，部將臨陣降，眾大潰，走中山。
summary.en: The Yuan leader at Ye. He went to attack Yuan Tan leaving Shen Pei to hold Ye; when Cao Cao besieged it he came back to relieve it, but his officers surrendered on the field and he fled to Zhongshan.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 二月，尚復攻譚，留蘇由、審配守鄴。
passages.textEn: In the second month Shang again attacked Tan, leaving Su You and Shen Pei to hold Ye.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 其將馬延、張顗等臨陣降，衆大潰，尚走中山。
passages.textEn: His officers Ma Yan, Zhang Yi and others surrendered on the field; his army broke, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.

summary.zh: 袁氏之一。畏曹操，棄平原走保南皮；建安十年正月為曹操所破，被斬。
summary.en: One of the Yuan. Fearing Cao Cao he left Pingyuan for Nanpi, where Cao routed and beheaded him in the first month of 205.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 譚懼，拔平原，走保南皮。
passages.textEn: Tan took fright, left Pingyuan and fell back to hold Nanpi.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 十年春正月，攻譚，破之，斬譚，誅其妻子，冀州平。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the tenth year, in spring, he attacked Tan, routed him, beheaded him and executed his wife and children; Ji Province was pacified.

summary.zh: 殺石祗，自稱帝號。與慕容恪戰於魏昌，十戰皆勝，終為恪所擒，送於薊。
summary.en: He killed Shi Zhi and took the imperial title. At Weichang he beat Murong Ke ten times, but was finally captured by him and sent to Ji.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百十 載記 慕容儁
passages.textZh: 及冉閔殺石祗，僭稱大號，遣其使人常煒聘於俊。
passages.textEn: When Ran Min had killed Shi Zhi and usurped the imperial title, he sent his envoy Chang Wei on a mission to Jun.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百七 載記 冉閔
passages.textZh: 俄而燕騎大至，圍之數周。閔眾寡不敵，躍馬潰圍東走，行二十餘里，馬無故而死，為恪所擒，及董閏、張溫等送之於薊。
passages.textEn: Soon the Yan horsemen arrived in force and surrounded him several times over. Outnumbered, Min broke through on horseback and fled east; after some twenty li his horse died for no reason, and he was captured by Ke and sent to Ji with Dong Run, Zhang Wen and others.

summary.zh: 率兵十餘萬援王世充，與李世民相持於武牢二十餘日，兵敗，被生擒於陣。
summary.en: He led over a hundred thousand men to relieve Wang Shichong, faced Li Shimin at Wulao for over twenty days, was routed, and was captured on the field.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 建德自滎陽西上，築壘於板渚，太宗屯武牢，相持二十餘日。
passages.textEn: Jiande came west from Xingyang and built a camp at Banzhu; Taizong held Wulao, and they faced each other for over twenty days.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 追奔三十里，斬首三千餘級，虜其眾五萬，生擒建德於陣。
passages.textEn: He pursued them thirty li, beheaded over three thousand, took fifty thousand prisoners and captured Jiande alive on the field.

summary.zh: 據東都，為李世民所圍；竇建德被擒後，率官屬詣軍門請降。
summary.en: He held the Eastern Capital under siege by Li Shimin; after Dou Jiande was captured he came to the camp gate with his officials and surrendered.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 乃將建德至東都城下。世充懼，率其官屬二千餘人詣軍門請降，山東悉平。
passages.textEn: He brought Jiande to the walls of the Eastern Capital. Shichong took fright and came to the camp gate with over two thousand of his officials to surrender; all the land east of the mountains was pacified.

summary.zh: 孫權部將。權征關羽，先遣蒙：蒙伏精兵於船中，使人白衣搖櫓作商賈，盡收關羽江邊屯候，襲公安，據江陵。
summary.en: An officer of Sun Quan. When Quan marched against Guan Yu he sent Lü Meng ahead: Meng hid troops in boats rowed by men dressed as merchants, seized Guan Yu's river posts, surprised Gong'an and held Jiangling.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 吳書 呂蒙傳
passages.textZh: 蒙至尋陽，盡伏其精兵𦩷𦪇中，使白衣搖櫓，作商賈人服，晝夜兼行，至羽所置江邊屯候，盡收縛之，是故羽不聞知。
passages.textEn: When Meng reached Xunyang he hid all his best troops in the holds of the boats, had men in plain clothes work the oars dressed as merchants, and travelled day and night; reaching the posts Yu had set along the river, he seized and bound every one of their men, so that Yu heard nothing.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 吳書 吳主傳
passages.textZh: 閏月，權征羽，先遣呂蒙襲公安，獲將軍士仁。蒙到南郡，南郡太守糜芳以城降，蒙據江陵，撫其老弱，釋於禁之囚。陸遜別取宜都，獲秭歸、枝江、夷道，還屯夷陵，守峽口以備蜀。
passages.textEn: In the intercalary month Quan marched against Yu, sending Lü Meng ahead to surprise Gong'an, where he took General Shi Ren. When Meng reached Nan commandery its governor Mi Fang surrendered the city; Meng occupied Jiangling, comforted the old and weak, and freed Yu Jin from prison. Lu Xun separately took Yidu, with Zigui, Zhijiang and Yidao, and returned to hold Yiling and the mouth of the gorges against Shu.

confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 秦王政十八年大舉攻趙：王翦率上地之兵下井陘，端和率河內之兵圍邯鄲；十九年王翦、羌瘣盡取趙地東陽，得趙王。
summary.en: In the eighteenth year of King Zheng, Qin attacked Zhao in force: Wang Jian led the troops of Shangdi down through Jingxing and Duanhe led those of Henei to besiege Handan; in the nineteenth year Wang Jian and Qiang Hui took all of Zhao's eastern lands and captured the king of Zhao.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 十八年，大興兵攻趙，王翦將上地，下井陘，端和將河內，羌瘣伐趙，端和圍邯鄲城。十九年，王翦、羌瘣盡定取趙地東陽，得趙王。
passages.textEn: In the eighteenth year Qin raised a great army against Zhao: Wang Jian led the troops of Shangdi down through Jingxing, Duanhe led those of Henei, Qiang Hui attacked Zhao, and Duanhe besieged the city of Handan. In the nineteenth year Wang Jian and Qiang Hui took all of Zhao's land east of the Yang and captured the king of Zhao.

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 秦王政二十六年，齊王建與相后勝發兵守西界，不與秦通；秦使將軍王賁自燕南下攻齊，得齊王建。
summary.en: In the twenty-sixth year of King Zheng, Jian of Qi and his chancellor Hou Sheng guarded their western border and broke with Qin; Qin sent Wang Ben south from Yan to attack Qi, and he captured King Jian.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 二十六年，齊王建與其相后勝發兵守其西界，不通秦。秦使將軍王賁從燕南攻齊，得齊王建。
passages.textEn: In the twenty-sixth year Jian, king of Qi, and his chancellor Hou Sheng sent troops to guard their western border and broke off with Qin. Qin sent General Wang Ben south from Yan to attack Qi, and he captured King Jian.

label.en: Wang Ben south from Yan into Qi

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 建安九年二月，袁尚出攻袁譚，留審配等守鄴；曹操圍鄴，決漳水灌城，城中餓死者過半。袁尚還救，其將臨陣降，眾大潰，尚走中山。八月審配兄子審榮夜開城門，配敗被擒斬，鄴定。
summary.en: In the second month of 204 Yuan Shang went to attack Yuan Tan, leaving Shen Pei and others to hold Ye. Cao Cao besieged Ye and flooded it from the Zhang River; more than half of those inside starved. Yuan Shang came back to relieve it, but his officers surrendered on the field, his army broke and he fled to Zhongshan. In the eighth month Shen Pei's nephew opened a gate at night; Shen Pei was beaten, captured and beheaded, and Ye was secured.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 二月，尚復攻譚，留蘇由、審配守鄴。
passages.textEn: In the second month Shang again attacked Tan, leaving Su You and Shen Pei to hold Ye.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 五月，毀土山、地道，作圍壍，決漳水灌城；城中餓死者過半。
passages.textEn: In the fifth month he gave up the earthen mounds and tunnels, dug a ring of trenches and let the Zhang River flood the city; more than half of those inside starved to death.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 其將馬延、張顗等臨陣降，衆大潰，尚走中山。
passages.textEn: His officers Ma Yan, Zhang Yi and others surrendered on the field; his army broke, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 八月，審配兄子榮夜開所守城東門內兵。配逆戰，敗，生禽配，斬之，鄴定。
passages.textEn: In the eighth month Shen Rong, Shen Pei's nephew, opened the east gate he was guarding at night and let the troops in. Pei fought back and was beaten; he was taken alive and beheaded, and Ye was secured.

label.en: Cao crosses the river and besieges Ye
Yuan Shang returns to relieve Ye

confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 袁譚懼曹操，棄平原走保南皮。建安十年正月曹操攻譚，破之，斬譚，冀州平。
summary.en: Fearing Cao Cao, Yuan Tan left Pingyuan and fell back to hold Nanpi. In the first month of 205 Cao attacked him, routed him and beheaded him; Ji Province was pacified.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 譚懼，拔平原，走保南皮。
passages.textEn: Tan took fright, left Pingyuan and fell back to hold Nanpi.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷一 魏書 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 十年春正月，攻譚，破之，斬譚，誅其妻子，冀州平。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the tenth year, in spring, he attacked Tan, routed him, beheaded him and executed his wife and children; Ji Province was pacified.

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 劉備進圍雒城，劉璋子劉循守之，被攻將近一年；諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲等溯江定白帝、江州、江陽。建安十九年夏雒城破，劉備進圍成都數十日，劉璋出降。
summary.en: Liu Bei besieged Luo, held by Liu Zhang's son Liu Xun, for nearly a year, while Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun and others came upriver and took Baidi, Jiangzhou and Jiangyang. In the summer of 214 Luo fell; Liu Bei besieged Chengdu for several tens of days and Liu Zhang came out and surrendered.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 諸葛亮、張飛、趙雲等將兵溯流定白帝、江州、江陽，惟關羽留鎮荊州。
passages.textEn: Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun and others led troops upriver and took Baidi, Jiangzhou and Jiangyang; only Guan Yu stayed behind to hold Jing Province.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 先主進軍圍雒；時璋子循守城，被攻且一年。
passages.textEn: The First Sovereign advanced and besieged Luo; Zhang's son Xun held the city and was under attack for nearly a year.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 蜀書 先主傳
passages.textZh: 十九年夏，雒城破，進圍成都數十日，璋出降。
passages.textEn: In the summer of the nineteenth year Luo fell; he went on to besiege Chengdu for several tens of days, and Zhang came out and surrendered.

label.zh: 諸葛亮等溯流定白帝、江州
label.en: Zhuge Liang and others come upriver

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 孫權征關羽，先遣呂蒙：蒙伏精兵於船中，使人白衣搖櫓作商賈，晝夜兼行，盡收關羽江邊屯候；襲公安，士仁降，南郡太守糜芳以城降，蒙據江陵。陸遜別取宜都。十二月關羽父子被擒，遂定荊州。
summary.en: Sun Quan marched against Guan Yu, sending Lü Meng ahead: Meng hid his best troops in the boats with oarsmen dressed as merchants, travelled day and night and seized Guan Yu's river posts; he surprised Gong'an, where Shi Ren surrendered, and Mi Fang surrendered Nan commandery, so Meng held Jiangling. Lu Xun took Yidu. In the twelfth month Guan Yu and his son were captured and Jing Province was secured.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 吳書 吳主傳
passages.textZh: 閏月，權征羽，先遣呂蒙襲公安，獲將軍士仁。蒙到南郡，南郡太守糜芳以城降，蒙據江陵，撫其老弱，釋於禁之囚。陸遜別取宜都，獲秭歸、枝江、夷道，還屯夷陵，守峽口以備蜀。
passages.textEn: In the intercalary month Quan marched against Yu, sending Lü Meng ahead to surprise Gong'an, where he took General Shi Ren. When Meng reached Nan commandery its governor Mi Fang surrendered the city; Meng occupied Jiangling, comforted the old and weak, and freed Yu Jin from prison. Lu Xun separately took Yidu, with Zigui, Zhijiang and Yidao, and returned to hold Yiling and the mouth of the gorges against Shu.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷五十四 吳書 呂蒙傳
passages.textZh: 蒙至尋陽，盡伏其精兵𦩷𦪇中，使白衣搖櫓，作商賈人服，晝夜兼行，至羽所置江邊屯候，盡收縛之，是故羽不聞知。
passages.textEn: When Meng reached Xunyang he hid all his best troops in the holds of the boats, had men in plain clothes work the oars dressed as merchants, and travelled day and night; reaching the posts Yu had set along the river, he seized and bound every one of their men, so that Yu heard nothing.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Three Kingdoms (Chen Shou, c. 290)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 吳書 吳主傳
passages.textZh: 十二月，璋司馬馬忠獲羽及其子平、都督趙累等於章鄉，遂定荊州。
passages.textEn: In the twelfth month Ma Zhong, aide to Pan Zhang, captured Yu, his son Ping, the commander Zhao Lei and others at Zhangxiang; and so Jing Province was secured.

label.en: Lü Meng's disguised boats to Gong'an

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 慕容俊已克幽、薊，略地至冀州。冉閔帥騎拒之，與慕容恪遇於魏昌城，十戰皆勝；恪以鐵鎖連馬，選善射者五千方陣而前，燕騎大至，圍閔數重。閔潰圍東走，馬斃，為恪所擒，送於薊。
summary.en: Murong Jun had taken You and Ji and was overrunning Ji Province. Ran Min led his horsemen against him and met Murong Ke at Weichang, winning ten engagements; then Ke chained his horses together and advanced in a square of five thousand archers, and the Yan horse arrived in force and surrounded Ran Min. He broke out eastward, but his horse died; he was captured by Ke and sent to Ji.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百七 載記 冉閔
passages.textZh: 時慕容俊已克幽、薊，略地至於冀州。閔帥騎距之，與慕容恪相遇于魏昌城。
passages.textEn: By then Murong Jun had taken You and Ji and was overrunning the land as far as Ji Province. Min led his horsemen against him and met Murong Ke at the city of Weichang.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百七 載記 冉閔
passages.textZh: 乃與恪遇，十戰皆敗之。恪乃以鐵鎖連馬，簡善射鮮卑勇而無剛者五千，方陣而前。
passages.textEn: He engaged Ke and beat him in ten battles. Ke then chained his horses together, picked five thousand brave Xianbei who were good archers, and advanced in a square.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百七 載記 冉閔
passages.textZh: 俄而燕騎大至，圍之數周。閔眾寡不敵，躍馬潰圍東走，行二十餘里，馬無故而死，為恪所擒，及董閏、張溫等送之於薊。
passages.textEn: Soon the Yan horsemen arrived in force and surrounded him several times over. Outnumbered, Min broke through on horseback and fled east; after some twenty li his horse died for no reason, and he was captured by Ke and sent to Ji with Dong Run, Zhang Wen and others.

label.zh: 慕容氏克薊，略地至冀州
label.en: Yan from Ji into Ji Province

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 慕容垂分遣慕容楷出滏口、慕容農入壺關，自率軍入天井關至壺壁。慕容永率精卒五萬來拒，垂偽退設伏，夾擊大破之，永奔長子；垂進圍長子，永將賈韜為內應，城破，永被擒殺。
summary.en: Murong Chui sent Murong Kai out through Fukou and Murong Nong in through Huguan, and himself came through the Tianjing Pass to Hubi. Murong Yong met him with fifty thousand picked troops; Chui feigned a retreat into an ambush and routed him, and Yong fled to Changzi. Chui besieged Changzi; Yong's officer Jia Tao betrayed it from within, and Yong was captured and put to death.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 載記 慕容垂
passages.textZh: 垂遣慕容楷出自滏口，慕容農入自壺關，垂頓於鄴之西南，月餘不進。
passages.textEn: Chui sent Murong Kai out through Fukou and Murong Nong in through Huguan, and himself halted south-west of Ye for over a month without advancing.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 載記 慕容垂
passages.textZh: 垂進師入自天井關，至於壺壁。永率精卒五萬來距，阻河曲以自固，馳使請戰。
passages.textEn: Chui advanced through the Tianjing Pass to Hubi. Yong came against him with fifty thousand picked troops, entrenched himself behind a bend of the river, and sent riders to offer battle.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 載記 慕容垂
passages.textZh: 垂引軍偽退，永追奔數里，國發伏兵馳斷其後，楷、農夾擊之，永師大敗，斬首八千餘級，永奔還長子。
passages.textEn: Chui feigned a retreat; Yong pursued for several li, Guo's hidden troops cut off his rear, and Kai and Nong attacked him from both sides. Yong's army was routed with over eight thousand beheaded, and Yong fled back to Changzi.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 載記 慕容垂
passages.textZh: 垂進圍長子，永將賈韜潛為內應。垂進軍入城，永奔北門，為前驅所獲，於是數而戮之，並其所署公卿刁雲等三十餘人。
passages.textEn: Chui besieged Changzi, and Yong's officer Jia Tao secretly worked for him inside. Chui entered the city; Yong fled to the north gate and was caught by the vanguard, and Chui charged him with his crimes and put him to death, with more than thirty of his ministers including Diao Yun.

label.zh: 垂入天井關，至壺壁、長子
label.en: Chui through Tianjing Pass to Changzi

confidenceNote.zh: 路線據史文所記地名示意，非實際行軍路線。
confidenceNote.en: The routes join the places the sources name; they are not the actual line of march.

summary.zh: 晉以朱齡石為益州刺史伐蜀。至白帝，開函書，令眾軍從外水取成都，疑兵出內水；譙縱果重兵備內水，又遣侯輝等萬餘人屯彭模，夾水為城。齡石四面並登，斬侯輝、譙詵，南城潰散。譙縱奔涪城，為巴西人王志所斬；齡石克成都，益州平。
summary.en: Jin sent Zhu Lingshi as Inspector of Yi to attack Shu. At Baidi he opened sealed orders: the armies were to take Chengdu by the Outer River while a feint went up the Inner River. Qiao Zong did guard the Inner River, and posted Hou Hui with over ten thousand men in forts on both banks at Pengmo. Zhu stormed them, beheading Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, and the south fort broke. Qiao Zong fled to Fucheng and was beheaded by Wang Zhi of Baxi; Zhu took Chengdu and Yi Province was pacified.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷十 安帝紀 義熙八年
passages.textZh: 十二月，以西陵太守朱齡石爲建威將軍、益州刺史，帥師伐蜀。
passages.textEn: In the twelfth month Zhu Lingshi, governor of Xiling, was made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yi Province, and led an army against Shu.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 朱齡石傳
passages.textZh: 至白帝，發書，曰：「眾軍悉從外水取成都，臧熹、朱林於中水取廣漢，使羸弱乘高艦十餘，由內水向黃虎。」
passages.textEn: At Baidi the letter was opened. It said: "All the armies are to take Chengdu by the Outer River; Zang Xi and Zhu Lin are to take Guanghan by the Middle River; the weak are to take a dozen tall ships up the Inner River towards Huanghu."

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 朱齡石傳
passages.textZh: 眾軍乃倍道兼行，譙縱果備內水，使其大將譙道福以重兵戍涪城，遣其前將軍秦州刺史侯輝、尚書僕射蜀郡太守譙詵等率眾萬餘屯彭模，夾水為城。
passages.textEn: The armies pressed on at double speed. Qiao Zong did indeed guard the Inner River: he had his general Qiao Daofu hold Fucheng in strength, and sent Hou Hui and Qiao Shen with over ten thousand men to camp at Pengmo, building forts on both banks.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 朱齡石傳
passages.textZh: 四面並登，斬侯輝、譙詵，仍回軍以麾，南城即時散潰。
passages.textEn: They scaled the walls on all sides and beheaded Hou Hui and Qiao Shen; when the army turned and signalled to the south fort, it broke up at once.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Song (Shen Yue, 488)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 朱齡石傳
passages.textZh: 譙縱聞諸處盡敗，奔于涪城，巴西人王志斬送。
passages.textEn: Hearing that he had been beaten everywhere, Qiao Zong fled to Fucheng, where Wang Zhi of Baxi beheaded him and sent in his head.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷十 安帝紀 義熙九年
passages.textZh: 秋七月，朱齡石克成都，斬譙縱，益州平。
passages.textEn: In the seventh month, in autumn, Zhu Lingshi took Chengdu and beheaded Qiao Zong; Yi Province was pacified.

label.en: The armies go upriver from Baidi
Up the Outer River to Pengmo

question.en: In which year was Shu taken?

claim.zh: 義熙九年（413）七月克成都。
claim.en: Chengdu was taken in the seventh month of Yixi 9 (413).

accounts.quoteZh: 秋七月，朱齡石克成都，斬譙縱，益州平。

claim.zh: 朱齡石傳繫至彭模於「十年六月」。
claim.en: Zhu Lingshi's biography dates the arrival at Pengmo to "the sixth month of the tenth year".

accounts.quoteZh: 十年六月，齡石至彭模

summary.zh: 西涼李士業率步騎三萬東伐北涼，沮渠蒙遜自浩亹來，戰於懷城，士業敗；復戰於蓼泉，為蒙遜所殺。其弟等西奔敦煌，蒙遜入酒泉；其後李翻、李恂等棄敦煌，奔北山。
summary.en: Li Shiye of Western Liang marched east against Northern Liang with thirty thousand men. Juqu Mengxun came from Haomen and beat him at Huaicheng; Shiye fought again at Liaoquan and was killed. His brothers fled west to Dunhuang and Mengxun entered Jiuquan; later Li Fan, Li Xun and others abandoned Dunhuang for the northern mountains.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 涼武昭王傳（附士業）
passages.textZh: 士業遂率步騎三萬東伐，鎰於都瀆澗。蒙遜自浩亹來，距戰於懷城，為蒙遜所敗。
passages.textEn: Shiye then marched east with thirty thousand foot and horse and halted at the Dudu ravine. Mengxun came from Haomen and met him at Huaicheng, where Shiye was beaten by Mengxun.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 涼武昭王傳（附士業）
passages.textZh: 勒眾復戰，敗於蓼泉，為蒙遜所害。士業諸弟酒泉太守翻、新城太守預、領羽林右監密、左將軍眺、右將軍亮等西奔敦煌，蒙遜遂入於酒泉。
passages.textEn: He rallied his men and fought again, was beaten at Liaoquan and killed by Mengxun. Shiye's brothers Fan, Yu, Mi, Tiao, Liang and others fled west to Dunhuang, and Mengxun entered Jiuquan.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Jin (Fang Xuanling et al., 648)
passages.locator: 卷八十七 涼武昭王傳（附士業）
passages.textZh: 翻及弟敦煌太守恂與諸子等棄敦煌，奔於北山，蒙遜以索嗣子遠緒行敦煌太守。
passages.textEn: Fan, his brother Xun the governor of Dunhuang, and their sons abandoned Dunhuang and fled to the northern mountains; Mengxun made Suo Si's son Yuanxu acting governor of Dunhuang.

summary.zh: 魏太武帝親伐和龍，北燕十餘郡來降，魏軍圍城，破其出戰之眾萬餘人（432）。其後魏遣娥清、古弼率精騎一萬再討馮文通；文通求救於高麗，高麗遣將來迎，文通奔高麗（436）。
summary.en: Emperor Taiwu of Wei marched on Helong in person; over ten of Northern Yan's commanderies surrendered, the city was besieged and a sortie of tens of thousands was routed (432). Later Wei sent E Qing and Gu Bi with ten thousand picked horse against Feng Wentong again; he asked Goguryeo for help, Goguryeo sent troops to fetch him, and he fled to Goguryeo (436).

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 延和元年
passages.textZh: 六月庚寅，車駕伐和龍。
passages.textEn: On gengyin of the sixth month the emperor marched against Helong.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 延和元年
passages.textZh: 己巳，車駕至和龍，臨其城。文通石城太守李崇、建德太守王融十餘郡來降，發其民三萬人穿圍塹以守之。
passages.textEn: On jisi the emperor reached Helong and came up to its walls. Ten or more of Wentong's commanderies, including Shicheng under Li Chong and Jiande under Wang Rong, surrendered, and thirty thousand of their people were put to digging siege trenches.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 延和元年
passages.textZh: 八月甲戌，文通使數萬人出城挑戰，昌黎公元丘與河間公元齊擊破之，死者萬餘人。
passages.textEn: On jiaxu of the eighth month Wentong sent tens of thousands out to offer battle; Yuan Qiu, Duke of Changli, and Yuan Qi, Duke of Hejian, routed them, and over ten thousand died.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 太延二年
passages.textZh: 辛未，平東將軍娥清、安西將軍古弼，率精騎一萬討馮文通，平州刺史元嬰又率遼西將軍會之。文通迫急，求救於高麗，高麗使其大將葛蔓盧以步騎二萬人迎文通。
passages.textEn: On xinwei E Qing and Gu Bi led ten thousand picked horse against Feng Wentong, joined by Yuan Ying, Inspector of Ping Province. Hard pressed, Wentong asked Goguryeo for help, and Goguryeo sent its general Ge Manlu with twenty thousand foot and horse to fetch him.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Wei (Wei Shou, 554)
passages.locator: 卷四上 世祖紀上 太延二年
passages.textZh: 五月乙卯，馮文通奔高麗。
passages.textEn: On yimao of the fifth month Feng Wentong fled to Goguryeo.

label.en: The Wei emperor marches on Helong
